examples.pinyin: Zǎo diǎn chūmén, miǎnde dǔchē chídào.
examples.english: Leave early to avoid being late because of traffic.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 用于给出建议或解释做某事的目的（为了避免坏事发生）。口语常用。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 尚(esteem)黑(dark)? 不，是政治团体。想象党旗。
vocabulary.etymology: Simplified from 黨。 Originally depicted a group or faction. The character '尚' (esteem) may hint at shared ideals.

examples.chinese: 他是那个党的成员。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì nàge dǎng de chéngyuán.
examples.english: He is a member of that party.

examples.chinese: 今晚有党的会议。
examples.pinyin: Jīn wǎn yǒu dǎng de huìyì.
examples.english: There is a party meeting tonight.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 语境敏感词。在中文中通常特指政党，尤其常指中国共产党。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 像一个人走进门里。
vocabulary.etymology: A pictograph originally depicting the tip of an arrow entering something, representing the concept of entering.

examples.chinese: 请入座。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng rù zuò.
examples.english: Please take a seat (enter your seat).

examples.chinese: 他已经入睡了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǐjīng rù shuì le.
examples.english: He has already fallen asleep (entered sleep).

vocabulary.usage_notes: 单用较文雅或正式，口语中更常用'进'。但作为构词语素（如'入学'、'入口'）非常常见。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 入(enter)学(school) - 进入学校。
vocabulary.etymology: 入 (to enter) + 学 (school/learning). Literally 'to enter school'.

examples.chinese: 我妹妹今年九月入学。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ mèimei jīnnián jiǔyuè rùxué.
examples.english: My younger sister will start school this September.

examples.chinese: 入学考试难吗？
examples.pinyin: Rùxué kǎoshì nán ma?
examples.english: Is the entrance exam difficult?

vocabulary.mnemonic: 全(all)力(power) - 所有的力量。
vocabulary.etymology: 全 (complete/all) + 力 (strength/power).

examples.chinese: 我们会全力支持你。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen huì quánlì zhīchí nǐ.
examples.english: We will support you with all our strength.

examples.chinese: 医生正在全力抢救病人。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng zhèngzài quánlì qiǎngjiù bìngrén.
examples.english: The doctors are trying their utmost to save the patient.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 常与'以'搭配：'尽全力'，或与'支持'、'投入'等动词搭配。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 全(all)新(new) - 完全新的。
vocabulary.etymology: 全 (complete/all) + 新 (new).

examples.chinese: 我买了一台全新的电脑。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi le yī tái quánxīn de diànnǎo.
examples.english: I bought a brand new computer.

examples.chinese: 这是一个全新的开始。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yī gè quánxīn de kāishǐ.
examples.english: This is a brand new beginning.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 强调'完全、彻底地新'，区别于'比较新'。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 八(eight)厶(private)? 不私了，就是'公'。也指雄性。
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted something fair and impartial, opposing '私' (private). The character may have represented a division of something equally.

examples.chinese: 这是公园，是公的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì gōngyuán, shì gōng de.
examples.english: This is a park, it's public.

examples.chinese: 这只猫是公的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī māo shì gōng de.
examples.english: This cat is male.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 含义广泛。作为形容词单独使用时，常与'母'相对表示性别，或与'私'相对表示公共属性。更多时候作为构词成分。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 公(public/lord)主(master) - 君王的主（女儿）。
vocabulary.etymology: 公 (duke/lord) + 主 (master). Originally referred to the daughter of a feudal lord or the emperor.

examples.chinese: 小女孩都喜欢扮成公主。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo nǚhái dōu xǐhuān bàn chéng gōngzhǔ.
examples.english: Little girls all like to dress up as princesses.

examples.chinese: 那位公主非常善良。
examples.pinyin: Nà wèi gōngzhǔ fēicháng shànliáng.
examples.english: That princess is very kind.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 公(public)众(mass) - 公共的众人。
vocabulary.etymology: 公 (public) + 众 (crowd/mass).

examples.chinese: 这件事引起了公众的关注。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì yǐnqǐ le gōngzhòng de guānzhù.
examples.english: This matter has attracted public attention.

examples.chinese: 在公众场合要小声说话。
examples.pinyin: Zài gōngzhòng chǎnghé yào xiǎoshēng shuōhuà.
examples.english: You should speak softly in public places.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 常与'场合'、'人物'、'利益'、'意见'等搭配。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 公(father-in-law)婆(mother-in-law) - 丈夫的父母。
vocabulary.etymology: 公 (here meaning father-in-law) + 婆 (old woman/mother-in-law). A specific term for a husband's parents.

examples.chinese: 周末我要去看望公婆。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒ yào qù kànwàng gōngpó.
examples.english: I'm going to visit my parents-in-law this weekend.

examples.chinese: 她和公婆住在一起。
examples.pinyin: Tā hé gōngpó zhù zài yīqǐ.
examples.english: She lives with her parents-in-law.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 特指丈夫的父母。妻子的父母是'岳父岳母'。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 公(public)安(safety) - 公共安全（部门）。
vocabulary.etymology: 公 (public) + 安 (safety/security).

examples.chinese: 有困难可以找公安。
examples.pinyin: Yǒu kùnnán kěyǐ zhǎo gōng'ān.
examples.english: If you have trouble, you can go to the police.

examples.chinese: 公安同志，我的钱包被偷了。
examples.pinyin: Gōng'ān tóngzhì, wǒ de qiánbāo bèi tōu le.
examples.english: Officer, my wallet was stolen.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 中国对警察的正式称呼。口语中也常直接叫'警察'。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 公(male)鸡(chicken) - 公的鸡。
vocabulary.etymology: 公 (male) + 鸡 (chicken).

examples.chinese: 天还没亮，公鸡就开始打鸣了。
examples.pinyin: Tiān hái méi liàng, gōngjī jiù kāishǐ dǎmíng le.
examples.english: Before dawn, the rooster started crowing.

examples.chinese: 这只公鸡的羽毛很漂亮。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī gōngjī de yǔmáo hěn piàoliang.
examples.english: This rooster's feathers are very beautiful.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 共(together)和(harmony)国(country) - 共同和谐治理的国家。
vocabulary.etymology: 共 (together) + 和 (harmony) + 国 (country/nation). A country governed by shared and harmonious rule (as opposed to a monarchy).

examples.chinese: 中华人民共和国成立于1949年。
examples.pinyin: Zhōnghuá Rénmín Gònghéguó chénglì yú yī jiǔ sì jiǔ nián.
examples.english: The People's Republic of China was founded in 1949.

examples.chinese: 法国是一个共和国。
examples.pinyin: Fǎguó shì yī gè gònghéguó.
examples.english: France is a republic.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 专有名词，通常大写。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 关(concern)爱(love) - 关心和爱护。
vocabulary.etymology: 关 (to concern/relate to) + 爱 (love).

examples.chinese: 父母总是关爱自己的孩子。
examples.pinyin: Fùmǔ zǒng shì guān'ài zìjǐ de háizi.
examples.english: Parents always care for their own children.

examples.chinese: 社会需要更多的关爱。
examples.pinyin: Shèhuì xūyào gèng duō de guān'ài.
examples.english: Society needs more loving care.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 比'关心'情感更深，带有爱护的意味。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 关(connect)联(unite) - 连接联合在一起。
vocabulary.etymology: 关 (to connect/relate) + 联 (to unite/associate).

examples.chinese: 这两个问题紧密关联。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liǎng gè wèntí jǐnmì guānlián.
examples.english: These two issues are closely related.

examples.chinese: 我没看出这两件事有什么关联。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ méi kàn chū zhè liǎng jiàn shì yǒu shénme guānlián.
examples.english: I don't see any connection between these two matters.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 兴致(interest)勃勃(vigorous) - 兴趣勃勃生机勃发。
vocabulary.etymology: 兴致 (interest/mood) + 勃勃 (vigorous/exuberant). An idiom describing lively interest.

examples.chinese: 孩子们兴致勃勃地准备去春游。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen xìngzhìbóbó de zhǔnbèi qù chūnyóu.
examples.english: The children are full of enthusiasm preparing for the spring outing.

examples.chinese: 他谈起自己的爱好总是兴致勃勃。
examples.pinyin: Tā tán qǐ zìjǐ de àihào zǒng shì xìngzhìbóbó.
examples.english: He always talks about his hobbies with great enthusiasm.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 四字成语。作状语时后面常加'地'。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 兴(prosper)隆(prosperous) - 双重繁荣，专门形容生意好。
vocabulary.etymology: 兴 (prosperous) + 隆 (prosperous/grand). A reinforcing combination meaning great prosperity.

examples.chinese: 这家餐馆生意很兴隆。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cānguǎn shēngyì hěn xīnglóng.
examples.english: This restaurant's business is very brisk.

examples.chinese: 祝你买卖兴隆！
examples.pinyin: Zhù nǐ mǎimài xīnglóng!
examples.english: Wishing you thriving business!

vocabulary.usage_notes: 几乎专门用于形容生意、买卖、商业活动繁荣。

vocabulary.english: to provide for the elderly / to retire
vocabulary.mnemonic: 养(support)老(old) - 供养老人。
vocabulary.etymology: 养 (to support/nourish) + 老 (old).

examples.chinese: 他存钱是为了以后养老。
examples.pinyin: Tā cún qián shì wèile yǐhòu yǎnglǎo.
examples.english: He saves money to provide for his old age later.

examples.chinese: 这个城市适合养老。
examples.pinyin: Zhège chéngshì shìhé yǎnglǎo.
examples.english: This city is suitable for retirement.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 可指个人为老年生活做准备，也可指社会或家庭赡养老人。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 内(inside)地(land) - 内部的土地（相对于沿海或特区）。
vocabulary.etymology: 内 (inside/inland) + 地 (land/area).

examples.chinese: 很多香港人去内地工作。
examples.pinyin: Hěnduō Xiānggǎng rén qù Nèidì gōngzuò.
examples.english: Many Hong Kong people go to work in mainland China.

examples.chinese: 我家在内地的一个小城市。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā zài nèidì de yī gè xiǎo chéngshì.
examples.english: My home is in a small city inland.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 在大陆指内陆地区；在港澳台语境中常特指中国大陆（不含港澳台）。

vocabulary.english: to attempt, attempt (often with negative connotation)
vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of someone on their tiptoes (企) trying to steal a picture (图/圖) – a sneaky attempt.
vocabulary.etymology: 企 (stand on tiptoe, look forward to) + 图 (diagram, plan). Together conveys the idea of "looking forward to a plan" or scheming.

examples.chinese: 他企图蒙混过关，但被老师发现了。
examples.pinyin: Tā qǐtú ménghùn guòguān, dàn bèi lǎoshī fāxiàn le.
examples.english: He tried to slip through, but the teacher caught him.

examples.chinese: 别再打逃跑的企图了，好好工作。
examples.pinyin: Bié zài dǎ táopǎo de qǐtú le, hǎohāo gōngzuò.
examples.english: Stop making plans to run away and get to work.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often carries a slightly negative or suspicious nuance, implying an ill-advised or scheming attempt.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The excellent (优) wins (胜), the inferior (劣) gets thrown out (汰). Nature's leaderboard.
vocabulary.etymology: A fixed phrase from 优 (excellent), 胜 (win/victory), 劣 (inferior), 汰 (discard/eliminate). Coined to translate Darwin's concept.

examples.chinese: 这个行业的竞争就是优胜劣汰，很残酷。
examples.pinyin: Zhège hángyè de jìngzhēng jiù shì yōushèng liètài, hěn cánkù.
examples.english: Competition in this industry is survival of the fittest; it's brutal.

examples.chinese: 别抱怨了，社会本来就是优胜劣汰的。
examples.pinyin: Bié bàoyuàn le, shèhuì běnlái jiù shì yōushèng liètài de.
examples.english: Stop complaining, society has always been about the survival of the fittest.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used to describe competitive environments in nature, business, or society.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Excellent (优) substance (质) = Top-notch stuff.
vocabulary.etymology: 优 (excellent, superior) + 质 (quality, substance). Literally "superior quality".

examples.chinese: 我们店只卖优质的水果，贵一点也值。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen diàn zhǐ mài yōuzhì de shuǐguǒ, guì yīdiǎn yě zhí.
examples.english: Our shop only sells high-quality fruit; it's worth the extra cost.

examples.chinese: 想找一份优质的爱情可真不容易。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎng zhǎo yī fèn yōuzhì de àiqíng kě zhēn bù róngyì.
examples.english: Finding a high-quality romantic relationship is really not easy.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used to describe products, services, resources, or content.

vocabulary.mnemonic: To meet (会) and see (见) someone officially. Think of a press conference handshake.
vocabulary.etymology: 会 (meet, gather) + 见 (see). A formal term for a meeting or audience.

examples.chinese: 总统今天下午会见了外国大使。
examples.pinyin: Zǒngtǒng jīntiān xiàwǔ huìjiàn le wàiguó dàshǐ.
examples.english: The president met with the foreign ambassador this afternoon.

examples.chinese: 经理正在会议室会见重要客户。
examples.pinyin: Jīnglǐ zhèngzài huìyìshì huìjiàn zhòngyào kèhù.
examples.english: The manager is meeting with an important client in the conference room.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for formal meetings between officials, leaders, or in business contexts. More formal than 见面.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The leader (长) of the meeting/association (会). The head of the club.
vocabulary.etymology: 会 (association, society) + 长 (chief, head). The head of a society or organization.

examples.chinese: 他是我们校友会的会长，组织能力特别强。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒmen xiàoyǒuhuì de huìzhǎng, zǔzhī nénglì tèbié qiáng.
examples.english: He is the president of our alumni association and has great organizational skills.

examples.chinese: 下个月要选举新的摄影协会会长。
examples.pinyin: Xià gè yuè yào xuǎnjǔ xīn de shèyǐng xiéhuì huìzhǎng.
examples.english: Next month we will elect a new chairperson for the photography club.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Specifically for the leader of a society, club, association, or committee.

vocabulary.english: to spread out, to transmit outwards
vocabulary.mnemonic: Transmit (传) something out (出). News going out the door.
vocabulary.etymology: 传 (transmit, pass on) + 出 (go out). A verb-complement compound meaning to transmit outward.

examples.chinese: 会议室里传出了激烈的争吵声。
examples.pinyin: Huìyìshì lǐ chuánchū le jīliè de zhēngchǎo shēng.
examples.english: The sound of a fierce argument came from the conference room.

examples.chinese: 这个消息千万不能传出去。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiāoxi qiānwàn bù néng chuán chūqù.
examples.english: This news must absolutely not be spread.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for sounds, news, signals, or information moving from an inside/private space to the outside/public.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A single (单) sheet for transmitting (传) information. The paper you get handed on the street.
vocabulary.etymology: 传 (transmit) + 单 (single sheet). A single sheet used to transmit information.

examples.chinese: 刚才有人在地铁口发新店开业的传单。
examples.pinyin: Gāngcái yǒu rén zài dìtiě kǒu fā xīn diàn kāiyè de chuándān.
examples.english: Someone was handing out flyers for a new store opening at the subway entrance just now.

examples.chinese: 别把这种医药传单当真，多半是骗人的。
examples.pinyin: Bié bǎ zhè zhǒng yīyào chuándān dàngzhēn, duōbàn shì piànrén de.
examples.english: Don't take these medical leaflets seriously; they're mostly scams.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly refers to promotional or advertising flyers, often handed out in public.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The vehicle (媒) that transmits (传) information. News trucks.
vocabulary.etymology: 传 (transmit) + 媒 (medium, intermediary). Short for 传播媒介 (communication medium).

examples.chinese: 他在一家很大的传媒公司工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yī jiā hěn dà de chuánméi gōngsī gōngzuò.
examples.english: He works for a very large media company.

examples.chinese: 现在的网络传媒影响力太大了。
examples.pinyin: Xiànzài de wǎngluò chuánméi yǐngxiǎnglì tài dà le.
examples.english: Online media nowadays has too much influence.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to the media industry or mass communication channels collectively (TV, press, internet).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Words (言) being passed on (传). The gossip telephone game.
vocabulary.etymology: 传 (pass on) + 言 (words, speech). Words that are passed around.

examples.chinese: 别信那些传言，都是假的。
examples.pinyin: Bié xìn nàxiē chuányán, dōu shì jiǎ de.
examples.english: Don't believe those rumors; they're all fake.

examples.chinese: 公司里传言他要辞职，也不知道是真是假。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī lǐ chuányán tā yào cízhí, yě bù zhīdào shì zhēn shì jiǎ.
examples.english: There's a rumor in the company that he's going to resign, but who knows if it's true.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Emphasizes the act of spreading unofficial information. Often implies the information is unverified.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Transmit (传) and transport (输). Like data zipping through a cable.
vocabulary.etymology: 传 (transmit) + 输 (transport, convey). Often used together in technical contexts.

examples.chinese: 这个U盘的数据传输速度很快。
examples.pinyin: Zhège U pán de shùjù chuánshū sùdù hěn kuài.
examples.english: This USB drive has very fast data transfer speeds.

examples.chinese: 信号传输过程被干扰了。
examples.pinyin: Xìnhào chuánshū guòchéng bèi gānrǎo le.
examples.english: The signal transmission process was interfered with.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used in technical contexts for data, signals, power, or files. More formal/specific than 传送.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The injured (伤) and the perished (亡). A grim casualty report.
vocabulary.etymology: 伤 (wound, injure) + 亡 (perish, die). A combined term for losses in personnel.

examples.chinese: 这场地震造成了严重的伤亡。
examples.pinyin: Zhè chǎng dìzhèn zàochéng le yánzhòng de shāngwáng.
examples.english: This earthquake caused severe casualties.

examples.chinese: 官方还没有公布具体的伤亡数字。
examples.pinyin: Guānfāng hái méiyǒu gōngbù jùtǐ de shāngwáng shùzì.
examples.english: The authorities have not yet released specific casualty figures.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used in reports of accidents, disasters, or conflicts. A formal, collective term.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The opening (口) where you're injured (伤). Like a sad little mouth on your skin.
vocabulary.etymology: 伤 (wound) + 口 (opening, mouth). Literally "wound opening".

examples.chinese: 小心别碰到水，伤口会感染的。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn bié pèng dào shuǐ, shāngkǒu huì gǎnrǎn de.
examples.english: Be careful not to get it wet; the wound could get infected.

examples.chinese: 他膝盖上的伤口已经结痂了。
examples.pinyin: Tā xīgài shàng de shāngkǒu yǐjīng jiējiā le.
examples.english: The wound on his knee has already scabbed over.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The general word for a physical wound, cut, or sore.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A wounded (伤) person/member (员). Someone on a stretcher.
vocabulary.etymology: 伤 (wound) + 员 (person, member). A person who is wounded.

examples.chinese: 救护车正在把伤员送往医院。
examples.pinyin: Jiùhùchē zhèngzài bǎ shāngyuán sòng wǎng yīyuàn.
examples.english: The ambulance is transporting the injured to the hospital.

examples.chinese: 现场有几名伤员需要立即救治。
examples.pinyin: Xiànchǎng yǒu jǐ míng shāngyuán xūyào lìjí jiùzhì.
examples.english: There are several injured people on site who need immediate treatment.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A formal term, often used in medical, military, or disaster response contexts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A person (亻 in 伶) with a sharp (利) mind. Think of a clever servant.
vocabulary.etymology: 伶 (actor, performer; from a word for musician) + 俐 (clever, sharp). Both characters contribute to the meaning of cleverness and agility.

examples.chinese: 这个小姑娘嘴特别甜，人也伶俐。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiǎo gūniang zuǐ tèbié tián, rén yě línglì.
examples.english: This little girl is very sweet-talking and clever.

examples.chinese: 他做事伶俐，老板很喜欢他。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuòshì línglì, lǎobǎn hěn xǐhuan tā.
examples.english: He works cleverly and efficiently, and the boss really likes him.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used to describe children or young people who are clever and quick in speech and action. Slightly literary but still used.

vocabulary.english: to lower one's head, to submit, to admit defeat
vocabulary.mnemonic: Your head (头) goes low (低). Either looking at your phone or admitting you're wrong.
vocabulary.etymology: 低 (low) + 头 (head). A verb-object compound meaning to lower the head.

examples.chinese: 他犯错后，终于向父母低头认错了。
examples.pinyin: Tā fàncuò hòu, zhōngyú xiàng fùmǔ dītóu rèncuò le.
examples.english: After making a mistake, he finally lowered his head and admitted his fault to his parents.

examples.chinese: 别总低头玩手机，对颈椎不好。
examples.pinyin: Bié zǒng dītóu wán shǒujī, duì jǐngzhuī bù hǎo.
examples.english: Don't always look down at your phone; it's bad for your neck.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Has both literal (looking down) and figurative (submitting, admitting defeat) meanings.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Low (低) warmth/temperature (温). The freezer setting.
vocabulary.etymology: 低 (low) + 温 (temperature, warmth). Literally "low temperature".

examples.chinese: 天气预报说明天有低温，记得多穿点。
examples.pinyin: Tiānqì yùbào shuō míngtiān yǒu dīwēn, jìde duō chuān diǎn.
examples.english: The weather forecast says there will be low temperatures tomorrow; remember to dress warmly.

examples.chinese: 这种疫苗需要低温保存。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng yìmiáo xūyào dīwēn bǎocún.
examples.english: This type of vaccine needs to be stored at a low temperature.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used in weather forecasts, science, and instructions for storage (e.g., food, medicine).

vocabulary.mnemonic: A place to live (住) and a house (宅). Your actual home building.
vocabulary.etymology: 住 (live, reside) + 宅 (house, residence). A formal compound for a dwelling place.

examples.chinese: 这个小区都是高档住宅。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiǎoqū dōu shì gāodàng zhùzhái.
examples.english: This residential complex is all high-end housing.

examples.chinese: 他名下有好几处住宅。
examples.pinyin: Tā míng xià yǒu hǎo jǐ chù zhùzhái.
examples.english: He owns several residences.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A formal term referring to residential buildings or housing in general, common in real estate and official contexts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The enlightened one. Think of a serene statue with a topknot.
vocabulary.etymology: A phonetic translation of Sanskrit "Buddha," meaning "the awakened one." The character itself is not etymologically related.

examples.chinese: 奶奶每天早晚都拜佛。
examples.pinyin: Nǎinai měitiān zǎowǎn dōu bài Fó.
examples.english: Grandma prays to Buddha every morning and evening.

examples.chinese: 他心态特别好，跟个佛似的。
examples.pinyin: Tā xīntài tèbié hǎo, gēn gè Fó shìde.
examples.english: He has such a good mindset, just like a Buddha.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Capitalized as a proper noun when referring to the Buddha. Can be used figuratively to describe a very calm person.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The teachings (教) of Buddha (佛).
vocabulary.etymology: 佛 (Buddha) + 教 (teaching, religion). The religion founded on the teachings of the Buddha.

examples.chinese: 他对佛教文化很感兴趣。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì Fójiào wénhuà hěn gǎn xìngqù.
examples.english: He is very interested in Buddhist culture.

examples.chinese: 佛教是从印度传到中国的。
examples.pinyin: Fójiào shì cóng Yìndù chuán dào Zhōngguó de.
examples.english: Buddhism was transmitted from India to China.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The standard term for the religion of Buddhism.

vocabulary.mnemonic: For zuō: A person (亻) in a workshop making stuff. For zuò: A person getting up (乍) to do something.
vocabulary.etymology: The character originally depicted a person (亻) starting to rise (乍), implying "to arise, to do." The 'workshop' meaning is derived.

examples.chinese: 他家以前是开木工作坊的。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiā yǐqián shì kāi mùgōng zuōfang de.
examples.english: His family used to run a carpenter's workshop.

examples.chinese: 这么晚了，你还在作什么？
examples.pinyin: Zhème wǎn le, nǐ hái zài zuò shénme?
examples.english: It's so late, what are you still doing?

vocabulary.usage_notes: As 'zuō', it's almost only used in 作坊 (workshop). The vast majority of the time it's read 'zuò' meaning 'to do, make, act as'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Something made/done (作) is wasted/abolished (废). Toss it in the void.
vocabulary.etymology: 作 (make, do) + 废 (abolish, waste). To make something abolished, i.e., render it invalid.

examples.chinese: 这张优惠券月底就作废了，赶紧用。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhāng yōuhuìquàn yuèdǐ jiù zuòfèi le, gǎnjǐn yòng.
examples.english: This coupon will become invalid at the end of the month; use it quickly.

examples.chinese: 旧合同已经作废了，以新的为准。
examples.pinyin: Jiù hétong yǐjīng zuòfèi le, yǐ xīn de wéi zhǔn.
examples.english: The old contract has been cancelled; the new one is the standard.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for tickets, coupons, documents, or agreements that lose their validity.

vocabulary.mnemonic: What you do (作) and when you rest (息). Your daily clock.
vocabulary.etymology: 作 (work, do) + 息 (rest, breath). The rhythm of activity and rest.

examples.chinese: 你作息太不规律了，老是熬夜。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zuòxī tài bù guīlǜ le, lǎo shì áoyè.
examples.english: Your daily routine is too irregular; you're always staying up late.

examples.chinese: 公司规定作息时间是朝九晚五。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī guīdìng zuòxī shíjiān shì cháojiǔ wǎnwǔ.
examples.english: The company's stipulated work schedule is 9 to 5.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in the phrase 作息时间 (work-rest schedule) or 作息规律 (regular routine).

vocabulary.english: to fight a battle, to engage in combat
vocabulary.mnemonic: To do/make (作) war (战). Generals moving pieces on a map.
vocabulary.etymology: 作 (engage in) + 战 (war, battle). To engage in warfare.

examples.chinese: 这支部队有着丰富的山地作战经验。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī bùduì yǒu zhe fēngfù de shāndì zuòzhàn jīngyàn.
examples.english: This troop has rich experience in mountain combat.

examples.chinese: 他们正在电脑前进行模拟作战。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zhèngzài diànnǎo qián jìnxíng mónǐ zuòzhàn.
examples.english: They are conducting simulated combat exercises on the computer.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A formal military term. Can also be used metaphorically for difficult projects or competitions (e.g., 营销作战 'marketing campaign').

vocabulary.mnemonic: Excellent (佳) cooked dishes (肴). Food that makes you say "wow".
vocabulary.etymology: 佳 (excellent, good) + 肴 (cooked dish, meat). Literally "excellent dishes".

examples.chinese: 妈妈做了一桌子佳肴等着我们。
examples.pinyin: Māma zuò le yī zhuōzi jiāyáo děng zhe wǒmen.
examples.english: Mom cooked a whole table of delicious food waiting for us.

examples.chinese: 这家店的招牌菜堪称佳肴。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de zhāopái cài kānchēng jiāyáo.
examples.english: This restaurant's signature dish can be called a true delicacy.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A slightly literary or formal term for exceptionally good food. Used for praise.

vocabulary.mnemonic: To provide (供) and give (给). Keeping the shelves stocked.
vocabulary.etymology: 供 (offer, supply) + 给 (give). A formal term for providing what is needed.

examples.chinese: 这个水库负责供给全市的饮用水。
examples.pinyin: Zhège shuǐkù fùzé gōngjǐ quán shì de yǐnyòngshuǐ.
examples.english: This reservoir is responsible for supplying drinking water to the entire city.

examples.chinese: 市场的供给大于需求，所以东西便宜。
examples.pinyin: Shìchǎng de gōngjǐ dà yú xūqiú, suǒyǐ dōngxi piányí.
examples.english: Market supply exceeds demand, so things are cheap.

vocabulary.usage_notes: An economic or formal term for the act of supplying goods or resources. Often paired with 需求 (demand).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 出 (go out) + 动 (move) → Moving Out! Like a fire truck rolling out of the station.
vocabulary.etymology: Literal combination: 出 (to go out, to exit) + 动 (to move, to act). The term likely evolved from military or logistical contexts.

examples.chinese: 警察出动了，应该出大事了。
examples.pinyin: Jǐng chá chū dòng le, yīng gāi chū dà shì le.
examples.english: The police have been dispatched; something big must have happened.

examples.chinese: 我们明天出动三辆车。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men míng tiān chū dòng sān liàng chē.
examples.english: We'll send out three cars tomorrow.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for organized groups like police, military, or emergency services.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 出台 literally means 'come on stage.' Imagine a new law (演员) stepping onto the stage of public life.
vocabulary.etymology: Figurative: 出 (to come out) + 台 (stage). Suggests something being presented publicly on a figurative platform.

examples.chinese: 新规定下个月出台。
examples.pinyin: Xīn guī dìng xià gè yuè chū tái.
examples.english: The new regulations will be enacted next month.

examples.chinese: 政府出台了很多优惠政策。
examples.pinyin: Zhèng fǔ chū tái le hěn duō yōu huì zhèng cè.
examples.english: The government has released many preferential policies.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used almost exclusively for official documents, rules, or policies coming into effect.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 出 (out, emerge) + 名 (name) → Your name is out there, everyone knows it.
vocabulary.etymology: Literal combination: 出 (to emerge) + 名 (name, reputation). To have one's reputation become public.

examples.chinese: 他在我们那儿特别出名。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài wǒ men nà er tè bié chū míng.
examples.english: He's really famous in our area.

examples.chinese: 他因为唱得好而出名。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīn wèi chàng de hǎo ér chū míng.
examples.english: He became famous for singing well.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be used as a predicate adjective or a verb. (他出名了 / He became famous). More casual than 著名.

vocabulary.english: to appear on stage/in a match
vocabulary.mnemonic: 出 (go out) + 场 (field/stage) → Going out onto the stage/playing field.
vocabulary.etymology: Literal combination: 出 (to go out) + 场 (field, arena, stage). To emerge onto a public space.

examples.chinese: 下一个出场的歌手是谁？
examples.pinyin: Xià yī gè chū chǎng de gē shǒu shì shéi?
examples.english: Who is the next singer to appear on stage?

examples.chinese: 那个球星下半场才出场。
examples.pinyin: Nà gè qiú xīng xià bàn chǎng cái chū chǎng.
examples.english: That star player didn't enter the match until the second half.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common in sports (球员出场) and performing arts contexts. Not used for casual appearances.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 出 (out) + 神 (spirit) → Your spirit wandered out of your body, leaving you zoned out.
vocabulary.etymology: Figurative: 出 (to leave) + 神 (spirit, mind). The mind/spirit has wandered off.

examples.chinese: 他听得都出神了。
examples.pinyin: Tā tīng de dōu chū shén le.
examples.english: He was completely spellbound listening.

examples.chinese: 别出神了，老师叫你！
examples.pinyin: Bié chū shén le, lǎo shī jiào nǐ!
examples.english: Stop spacing out, the teacher is calling you!

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used as a state (出神地看着) or a result (看出神了). Very descriptive and common in speech.

vocabulary.english: to go on a trip, to travel
vocabulary.mnemonic: 出 (out) + 行 (to go, to travel) → Go out and travel.
vocabulary.etymology: Literal combination: 出 (to go out) + 行 (to go, to travel).

examples.chinese: 国庆假期你打算出行吗？
examples.pinyin: Guó qìng jià qī nǐ dǎ suàn chū xíng ma?
examples.english: Do you plan to travel during the National Day holiday?

examples.chinese: 出行前记得检查天气。
examples.pinyin: Chū xíng qián jì de jiǎn chá tiān qì.
examples.english: Remember to check the weather before you travel.

vocabulary.usage_notes: More formal/planning-oriented than 出去玩儿. Often used in official contexts (出行提示) or for general travel planning.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 出 (out) + 访 (visit) → Go out to visit (another country). Like a president visiting abroad.
vocabulary.etymology: Literal combination: 出 (to go out) + 访 (to visit, to call on).

examples.chinese: 主席下周将出访欧洲。
examples.pinyin: Zhǔ xí xià zhōu jiāng chū fǎng Ōu zhōu.
examples.english: The chairman will make an official visit to Europe next week.

examples.chinese: 这是他今年第三次出访。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì tā jīn nián dì sān cì chū fǎng.
examples.english: This is his third official visit abroad this year.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Highly formal and used for high-level, official visits, especially by diplomats, leaders, or delegations.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 出 (exit) + 路 (road) → The road that leads you out of a difficult situation.
vocabulary.etymology: Literal combination: 出 (to exit) + 路 (road, path). A figurative path leading out.

examples.chinese: 你觉得我们还有什么出路？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ jué de wǒ men hái yǒu shén me chū lù?
examples.english: Do you think we have any way out left?

examples.chinese: 对于毕业生来说，这是一个好出路。
examples.pinyin: Duì yú bì yè shēng lái shuō, zhè shì yī gè hǎo chū lù.
examples.english: This is a good career path for graduates.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used figuratively for finding solutions, career paths, or escape from predicaments.

vocabulary.english: to show up personally, to intervene
vocabulary.mnemonic: 出 (out) + 面 (face) → To put your face out there personally to deal with something.
vocabulary.etymology: Literal combination: 出 (to appear) + 面 (face). To show one's face, implying personal involvement.

examples.chinese: 这事得老板出面才行。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì děi lǎo bǎn chū miàn cái xíng.
examples.english: For this matter, the boss needs to intervene personally.

examples.chinese: 他亲自出面道歉了。
examples.pinyin: Tā qīn zì chū miàn dào qiàn le.
examples.english: He showed up personally to apologize.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Implies someone with authority or responsibility takes personal action to handle a situation.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 分 (divide) + 工 (work) → Work is divided. Think of a group project where you 'divide and conquer'.
vocabulary.etymology: Literal combination: 分 (to divide) + 工 (work, labor).

examples.chinese: 我们分一下工吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men fēn yī xià gōng ba.
examples.english: Let's divide up the work.

examples.chinese: 社会分工越来越细。
examples.pinyin: Shè huì fēn gōng yuè lái yuè xì.
examples.english: The division of labor in society is becoming more and more detailed.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common in work and project contexts. Can be used as a verb (分工合作).

vocabulary.english: to split, to divide; a split
vocabulary.mnemonic: 分 (divide) + 裂 (crack/split) → Dividing and cracking apart, like a cracked egg or a broken team.
vocabulary.etymology: Literal combination: 分 (to divide) + 裂 (to crack, to split).

examples.chinese: 那个政党内部已经分裂了。
examples.pinyin: Nà gè zhèng dǎng nèi bù yǐ jīng fēn liè le.
examples.english: That political party has already split internally.

examples.chinese: 细胞分裂是生长的过程。
examples.pinyin: Xì bāo fēn liè shì shēng zhǎng de guò chéng.
examples.english: Cell division is a process of growth.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can describe physical (cells) or social/political (organizations, countries) division, often with negative connotations.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 切 (cut, close to) + 实 (real, solid) → Cut close to reality = practical and solid, not just talk.
vocabulary.etymology: Figurative: 切 (to cut close to, to correspond to) + 实 (reality, solid). Corresponding to reality.

examples.chinese: 我们需要一个切实可行的计划。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men xū yào yī gè qiè shí kě xíng de jì huà.
examples.english: We need a practical and feasible plan.

examples.chinese: 你要切实地改进你的方法。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào qiè shí de gǎi jìn nǐ de fāng fǎ.
examples.english: You need to concretely improve your method.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often modifies nouns like '措施', '行动', '计划'. Emphasizes actions being grounded in reality and effective.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 刑 (punishment) + 事 (matter) → Matters related to punishment (by law) = criminal cases.
vocabulary.etymology: Literal combination: 刑 (punishment, penalty) + 事 (matter, affair). Affairs of punishment/crime.

examples.chinese: 这是一起严重的刑事案件。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yī qǐ yán zhòng de xíng shì àn jiàn.
examples.english: This is a serious criminal case.

examples.chinese: 他面临刑事指控。
examples.pinyin: Tā miàn lín xíng shì zhǐ kòng.
examples.english: He faces criminal charges.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used almost exclusively as an attributive before nouns like '案件', '法律', '责任'. Opposite of 民事 (civil).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 刚 (just, exactly) + 好 (good) → Just good, just right. Like Goldilocks finding the 'just right' porridge.
vocabulary.etymology: Literal combination: 刚 (just, exactly) + 好 (good, well).

examples.chinese: 我刚好也想给你打电话。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gāng hǎo yě xiǎng gěi nǐ dǎ diàn huà.
examples.english: I was just about to call you too (what a coincidence).

examples.chinese: 这双鞋大小刚好。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shuāng xié dà xiǎo gāng hǎo.
examples.english: These shoes fit just right.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Expresses coincidence, perfect timing, or exact suitability. More common in spoken Chinese than 恰好.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 创 (create) + 办 (handle, run) → Create and run something from scratch → to found.
vocabulary.etymology: Literal combination: 创 (to create, to initiate) + 办 (to do, to manage).

examples.chinese: 他五年前创办了这家公司。
examples.pinyin: Tā wǔ nián qián chuàng bàn le zhè jiā gōng sī.
examples.english: He founded this company five years ago.

examples.chinese: 这个协会是她一手创办的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè xié huì shì tā yī shǒu chuàng bàn de.
examples.english: She single-handedly established this association.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Focuses on the initial act of setting up an organization, school, enterprise, etc. Founder is 创办人.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 创 (create) + 建 (build) → Create and build. Think of building a city in a video game.
vocabulary.etymology: Literal combination: 创 (to create) + 建 (to build, to construct).

examples.chinese: 我们正在创建一个新的数据库。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men zhèng zài chuàng jiàn yī gè xīn de shù jù kù.
examples.english: We are creating a new database.

examples.chinese: 他为创建和平环境做出了贡献。
examples.pinyin: Tā wèi chuàng jiàn hé píng huán jìng zuò chū le gòng xiàn.
examples.english: He contributed to creating a peaceful environment.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Broader than 创办. Can be used for abstract things (文明, 理论) or concrete systems, but less for personal businesses.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 创 (create) + 意 (idea) → Creative ideas. Picture a lightbulb moment.
vocabulary.etymology: Literal combination: 创 (to create) + 意 (idea, thought).

examples.chinese: 这个广告很有创意。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè guǎng gào hěn yǒu chuàng yì.
examples.english: This advertisement is very creative.

examples.chinese: 我们需要一些新的创意。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men xū yào yī xiē xīn de chuàng yì.
examples.english: We need some new creative ideas.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very common word in modern contexts like marketing, design, and art. Can be an adjective (创意产业).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 初 (beginning, first) + 等 (level) → The first level, like grade school math.
vocabulary.etymology: Literal combination: 初 (initial, beginning) + 等 (grade, level).

examples.chinese: 这是初等数学的内容。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì chū děng shù xué de nèi róng.
examples.english: This is elementary math content.

examples.chinese: 他只受过初等教育。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhǐ shòu guò chū děng jiào yù.
examples.english: He only received a primary education.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Formal term, often used in educational or academic contexts (初等教育, 初等函数). Less common in casual talk than 初级.

vocabulary.english: to judge, to sentence, to decide
vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine a judge 判 (Pàn) hitting the gavel to make a final decision. The left part looks like a sword (刀) cutting a case in half.
vocabulary.etymology: Pictophonetic: 刂 (knife, related to judgment/cutting) + 半 (half). Possibly suggests splitting/cutting a case to decide. Classical meaning is to decide or distinguish.

examples.chinese: 法官判他三年徒刑。
examples.pinyin: Fǎ guān pàn tā sān nián tú xíng.
examples.english: The judge sentenced him to three years in prison.

examples.chinese: 这事我不好判谁对谁错。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ bù hǎo pàn shéi duì shéi cuò.
examples.english: It's hard for me to judge who's right and who's wrong in this matter.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 核心义是裁决、决定。常见于法律 (判刑)、体育 (裁判判罚)、比赛 (判定胜负) 等语境。

vocabulary.mnemonic: Left part is grain (禾), right part is knife (刂). Grain cut by a knife is useful and profitable. Or, a sharp knife (利刃) is useful.
vocabulary.etymology: Pictophonetic: 禾 (grain) + 刂 (knife). Original meaning was sharp (like a knife). Extended to mean benefit (a sharp tool is useful/profitable).

examples.chinese: 做生意就是为了求利。
examples.pinyin: Zuò shēng yì jiù shì wèi le qiú lì.
examples.english: The purpose of doing business is to seek profit.

examples.chinese: 这把刀很利。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bǎ dāo hěn lì.
examples.english: This knife is very sharp.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 作为名词常指利益、利润；作为形容词指锋利、顺利。是许多复合词的核心字。

vocabulary.english: to scrape, to shave, to blow (wind)
vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine a tongue (舌, actually not present in the character) inside a container (刂 is a knife?) scraping something clean. Or, the wind 刮 your face.
vocabulary.etymology: Pictophonetic: 舌 (tongue, phonetic component in some older forms?) + 刂 (knife). Original meaning to scrape with a knife. Extended to wind blowing (as if scraping the land).

examples.chinese: 外面刮大风了。
examples.pinyin: Wài miàn guā dà fēng le.
examples.english: It's blowing a gale outside.

examples.chinese: 我每天早上都要刮胡子。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān zǎo shang dōu yào guā hú zi.
examples.english: I have to shave every morning.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 核心义是物体表面接触并移动。可指自然现象 (刮风)、个人护理 (刮胡子)、清洁 (刮掉污渍)。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 到 (arrive) + 期 (period/deadline) → The deadline has arrived. Your library books are due!
vocabulary.etymology: Literal combination: 到 (to arrive) + 期 (period, deadline).

examples.chinese: 我的护照下个月到期。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de hù zhào xià gè yuè dào qī.
examples.english: My passport expires next month.

examples.chinese: 房租到期了，得续约。
examples.pinyin: Fáng zū dào qī le, děi xù yuē.
examples.english: The rent is due; we need to renew the lease.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Describes the state when a contract, membership, visa, or subscription reaches its end date.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Looks like a person (人) under a knife (刀) holding a ticket? Actually, it's from 卷. Think of a rolled-up (卷) piece of paper that is your ticket.
vocabulary.etymology: Phonetic loan/simplification: Originally related to 卷 (to roll up). A券 was likely a rolled-up document or contract, later meaning certificate/ticket.

examples.chinese: 我有两张电影券。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǒu liǎng zhāng diàn yǐng quàn.
examples.english: I have two movie tickets/vouchers.

examples.chinese: 用这个优惠券可以打八折。
examples.pinyin: Yòng zhè gè yōu huì quàn kě yǐ dǎ bā zhé.
examples.english: You can get 20% off with this coupon.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often refers to paper vouchers or tickets for specific purposes (优惠券, 礼券). Note pronunciation: quàn (not juàn).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Sounds like 'chà nà' – think 'CHA!' (surprise) + 'NAH!' (quick denial) – both are over in an instant. It's a Buddhist loanword.
vocabulary.etymology: Phonetic loan from Sanskrit 'kṣaṇa', meaning the shortest measurable moment in time. 刹 is a temple (from刹多罗), 那 is phonetic.

examples.chinese: 在事故发生的那一刹那，他吓呆了。
examples.pinyin: Zài shì gù fā shēng de nà yī chà nà, tā xià dāi le.
examples.english: At the instant the accident happened, he was stunned.

examples.chinese: 幸福有时只在一刹那。
examples.pinyin: Xìng fú yǒu shí zhǐ zài yī chà nà.
examples.english: Happiness is sometimes just a fleeting moment.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Poetic/literary, often used with 一 (一刹那). Describes an extremely short, almost immeasurable moment.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 刻 (a moment) + 不容 (not allow) + 缓 (slow/delay) → Not a moment is allowed for delay → It's a life-or-death emergency!
vocabulary.etymology: Literal breakdown: 刻 (a short time, a moment), 不 (not), 容 (to allow), 缓 (to delay). Not allowing a moment's delay.

examples.chinese: 病人情况危急，抢救刻不容缓。
examples.pinyin: Bìng rén qíng kuàng wēi jí, qiǎng jiù kè bù róng huǎn.
examples.english: The patient's condition is critical; resuscitation is extremely urgent.

examples.chinese: 解决环境污染问题刻不容缓。
examples.pinyin: Jiě jué huán jìng wū rǎn wèn tí kè bù róng huǎn.
examples.english: Solving environmental pollution is a matter of extreme urgency.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A four-character idiom expressing the highest level of urgency, often used in formal or critical contexts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think '前 (front) 方 (direction)' = the direction in front of you.
vocabulary.etymology: 前 originally depicted a foot in a boat moving forward. 方 means direction or region.

examples.chinese: 前方路口左转。
examples.pinyin: Qián fāng lù kǒu zuǒ zhuǎn.
examples.english: Turn left at the intersection ahead.

examples.chinese: 我们的目标就在前方。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men de mù biāo jiù zài qián fāng.
examples.english: Our goal is just ahead.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used to indicate a location or direction ahead, common in navigation and motivational contexts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 前 (forward) + 来 (come) = come forward, i.e., come here.
vocabulary.etymology: 来 originally depicted wheat, later borrowed for its sound to mean 'come'. Combined with 前 (forward) to indicate direction of coming.

examples.chinese: 欢迎大家前来参观。
examples.pinyin: Huān yíng dà jiā qián lái cān guān.
examples.english: Everyone is welcome to come and visit.

examples.chinese: 他专程前来看望我。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhuān chéng qián lái kàn wàng wǒ.
examples.english: He made a special trip to come see me.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Slightly more formal than just 来, often used in invitations or announcements.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It looks like a person (人) holding a dagger (刂) over a container (佥) - a weapon!
vocabulary.etymology: Simplified from 劍. The phonetic component is 僉 (qiān), the semantic is 刂 (knife).

examples.chinese: 他收藏了一把古代的剑。
examples.pinyin: Tā shōu cáng le yī bǎ gǔ dài de jiàn.
examples.english: He collects an ancient sword.

examples.chinese: 这部电影里有很多精彩的剑术对决。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diàn yǐng lǐ yǒu hěn duō jīng cǎi de jiàn shù duì jué.
examples.english: There are many exciting sword fight scenes in this movie.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of a '剧' as a '巨大的' (huge) story.
vocabulary.etymology: Simplified from 劇. The left component 虍 might suggest fierceness (intense emotions), right 刂 (knife) suggests decisive action.

examples.chinese: 我昨晚追了一部新剧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuó wǎn zhuī le yī bù xīn jù.
examples.english: I binge-watched a new drama last night.

examples.chinese: 这个剧情太精彩了！
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge jù qíng tài jīng cǎi le!
examples.english: The plot of this show is so exciting!

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often combined as in 电视剧 (TV drama), 话剧 (stage play).

vocabulary.english: to cut the ribbon (at an opening)
vocabulary.mnemonic: 剪 (cut) + 彩 (colorful ribbon) = cutting the colorful ribbon.
vocabulary.etymology: 剪 uses 刀 (knife) and 前 (phonetic). 彩 means color or splendid pattern.

examples.chinese: 市长将为新超市剪彩。
examples.pinyin: Shì zhǎng jiāng wèi xīn chāo shì jiǎn cǎi.
examples.english: The mayor will cut the ribbon for the new supermarket.

examples.chinese: 剪彩仪式在上午十点举行。
examples.pinyin: Jiǎn cǎi yí shì zài shàng wǔ shí diǎn jǔ xíng.
examples.english: The ribbon-cutting ceremony will be held at 10 a.m.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Specifically refers to the ceremony of cutting a ribbon to inaugurate an event or building.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of a '副'班长 - the assistant class monitor, second in command.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted splitting something with a knife (刂), leading to meanings of 'secondary' or 'assistant'.

examples.chinese: 他是公司的副总经理。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì gōng sī de fù zǒng jīng lǐ.
examples.english: He is the deputy general manager of the company.

examples.chinese: 我需要买一副新耳机。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xū yào mǎi yī fù xīn ěr jī.
examples.english: I need to buy a new pair of headphones.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As a measure word, used for pairs/sets (眼镜, 手套, 扑克牌). As an adjective, opposite of 正 (main).

vocabulary.english: to strive to, to try hard to
vocabulary.mnemonic: 力 (strength) + 图 (plan) = using your strength according to a plan to achieve something.
vocabulary.etymology: 力 depicts a muscle, meaning strength. 图 originally meant a map or plan.

examples.chinese: 球队力图在下半场扳平比分。
examples.pinyin: Qiú duì lì tú zài xià bàn chǎng bān píng bǐ fēn.
examples.english: The team is striving to equalize the score in the second half.

examples.chinese: 政府力图解决交通拥堵问题。
examples.pinyin: Zhèng fǔ lì tú jiě jué jiāo tōng yōng dǔ wèn tí.
examples.english: The government is striving to solve the traffic congestion problem.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Slightly more formal/ambitious than just 努力, implying a directed effort towards a specific goal.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 办事 (handle affairs) + 处 (place) = the place where affairs are handled.
vocabulary.etymology: 办 (to handle) + 事 (matter) + 处 (place).

examples.chinese: 我们公司在上海设了一个办事处。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men gōng sī zài Shàng hǎi shè le yī gè bàn shì chù.
examples.english: Our company has set up an office in Shanghai.

examples.chinese: 你需要去签证办事处办理手续。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xū yào qù qiān zhèng bàn shì chù bàn lǐ shǒu xù.
examples.english: You need to go to the visa agency to process the paperwork.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often refers to a branch office or a specialized agency handling specific affairs.

vocabulary.english: to work (in an office), to do office work
vocabulary.mnemonic: 办 (handle) + 公 (public/official matters) = handle official work.
vocabulary.etymology: 办 originally meant to handle or manage. 公 means public or official.

examples.chinese: 我一般九点开始办公。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yī bān jiǔ diǎn kāi shǐ bàn gōng.
examples.english: I usually start work at 9 o'clock.

examples.chinese: 今天可以在家办公吗？
examples.pinyin: Jīn tiān kě yǐ zài jiā bàn gōng ma?
examples.english: Can I work from home today?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used in compounds like 办公室 (office), 办公桌 (desk).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 办 (run/manage) + 学 (school/learning) = run a school.
vocabulary.etymology: 办 (to handle) + 学 (learning).

examples.chinese: 他们集资在乡村办学。
examples.pinyin: Tā men jí zī zài xiāng cūn bàn xué.
examples.english: They pooled funds to run a school in the village.

examples.chinese: 这所大学的办学理念很先进。
examples.pinyin: Zhè suǒ dà xué de bàn xué lǐ niàn hěn xiān jìn.
examples.english: This university's educational philosophy is very advanced.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to the activity of establishing and operating an educational institution.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 加 (add) + 盟 (alliance) = add yourself to an alliance.
vocabulary.etymology: 加 means to add. 盟 originally referred to a blood oath or covenant between parties.

examples.chinese: 他加盟了一家著名的咖啡连锁店。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiā méng le yī jiā zhù míng de kā fēi lián suǒ diàn.
examples.english: He joined a famous coffee chain as a franchisee.

examples.chinese: 这个创业项目欢迎有志者加盟。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge chuàng yè xiàng mù huān yíng yǒu zhì zhě jiā méng.
examples.english: This startup project welcomes motivated people to join.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used in business contexts, especially for franchises (加盟店).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 动 (move) + 画 (picture) = moving pictures.
vocabulary.etymology: 动 (to move) + 画 (picture, painting).

examples.chinese: 我小时候最爱看日本动画。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎo shí hou zuì ài kàn Rì běn dòng huà.
examples.english: I loved watching Japanese animation when I was a kid.

examples.chinese: 这部动画的特效做得太棒了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù dòng huà de tè xiào zuò de tài bàng le.
examples.english: The special effects in this cartoon are amazing.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used as 动画片. 动漫 refers more broadly to anime and manga culture.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 勉 (endeavor) + 励 (encourage) = encourage someone to endeavor.
vocabulary.etymology: 勉 means to strive or endeavor. 励 means to encourage or stimulate.

examples.chinese: 老师经常勉励我们要好好学习。
examples.pinyin: Lǎo shī jīng cháng miǎn lì wǒ men yào hǎo hǎo xué xí.
examples.english: The teacher often encourages us to study hard.

examples.chinese: 朋友的勉励给了我很大的信心。
examples.pinyin: Péng you de miǎn lì gěi le wǒ hěn dà de xìn xīn.
examples.english: My friend's encouragement gave me a lot of confidence.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Slightly more formal and earnest than casual 鼓励.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 勤 (diligent) + 俭 (frugal) = the classic virtue of diligence and frugality.
vocabulary.etymology: 勤 means diligent, industrious. 俭 means frugal, economical.

examples.chinese: 爷爷奶奶一辈子都很勤俭。
examples.pinyin: Yé ye nǎi nai yī bèi zi dōu hěn qín jiǎn.
examples.english: Grandpa and grandma have been hardworking and thrifty all their lives.

examples.chinese: 勤俭是中华民族的传统美德。
examples.pinyin: Qín jiǎn shì Zhōng huá mín zú de chuán tǒng měi dé.
examples.english: Being hardworking and thrifty is a traditional virtue of the Chinese nation.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A highly valued traditional virtue, often used together as a fixed phrase.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 勤 (diligent) + 恳 (sincere/earnest) = diligent with a sincere heart.
vocabulary.etymology: 勤 means diligent. 恳 means sincere, earnest.

examples.chinese: 他在工作上非常勤恳。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài gōng zuò shàng fēi cháng qín kěn.
examples.english: He is very diligent and conscientious at work.

examples.chinese: 我们需要勤恳的员工。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men xū yào qín kěn de yuán gōng.
examples.english: We need diligent and conscientious employees.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Emphasizes both effort and a serious, dedicated attitude.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The character looks a bit like a spoon with something (丶) in it.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally a pictograph of a spoon with something in it. The dot represents the contents.

examples.chinese: 给我拿一把勺子喝汤。
examples.pinyin: Gěi wǒ ná yī bǎ sháo zi hē tāng.
examples.english: Get me a spoon to drink the soup.

examples.chinese: 这个炒菜的勺有点重。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge chǎo cài de sháo yǒu diǎn zhòng.
examples.english: This wok ladle is a bit heavy.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used as 勺子 in spoken language. Can refer to any spoon or ladle.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 包 (wrap up) + 庇 (shelter) = wrap up and shelter a misdeed.
vocabulary.etymology: 包 means to wrap or cover. 庇 means to shelter or protect.

examples.chinese: 你不能包庇你弟弟的错误。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bù néng bāo bì nǐ dì di de cuò wù.
examples.english: You can't cover up for your younger brother's mistake.

examples.chinese: 包庇罪犯是违法的。
examples.pinyin: Bāo bì zuì fàn shì wéi fǎ de.
examples.english: Sheltering a criminal is illegal.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Strongly negative connotation. Used when protecting someone who has done wrong.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 化 (melt/change) + 解 (untie) = melt away or untie a problem.
vocabulary.etymology: 化 means to change or melt. 解 means to untie or explain.

examples.chinese: 他巧妙地化解了这场尴尬。
examples.pinyin: Tā qiǎo miào de huà jiě le zhè chǎng gān gà.
examples.english: He cleverly resolved this awkward situation.

examples.chinese: 我们应该想办法化解矛盾。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men yīng gāi xiǎng bàn fǎ huà jiě máo dùn.
examples.english: We should find a way to resolve the conflict.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for abstract conflicts, crises, or negative emotions.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 匪 (bandit) + 徒 (follower) = a follower of banditry, a gangster.
vocabulary.etymology: 匪 originally meant a basket, later borrowed phonetically for 'bandit'. 徒 means follower or person.

examples.chinese: 警察终于抓住了那几个匪徒。
examples.pinyin: Jǐng chá zhōng yú zhuā zhù le nà jǐ gè fěi tú.
examples.english: The police finally caught those gangsters.

examples.chinese: 这部电影讲的是警匪之间的斗争。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diàn yǐng jiǎng de shì jǐng fěi zhī jiān de dòu zhēng.
examples.english: This movie is about the struggle between the police and bandits.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Somewhat dated/literary. Common in news or historical/crime drama contexts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 区 (area) + 分 (divide) = divide into areas, i.e., tell them apart.
vocabulary.etymology: 区 originally meant a hidden container, later 'area'. 分 means to divide.

examples.chinese: 你能区分这两款手机吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng qū fēn zhè liǎng kuǎn shǒu jī ma?
examples.english: Can you distinguish between these two phone models?

examples.chinese: 要学会区分事实和观点。
examples.pinyin: Yào xué huì qū fēn shì shí hé guān diǎn.
examples.english: You need to learn to differentiate between facts and opinions.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in the pattern '区分A和B'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 医 (medical) + 药 (drug) = medical drugs, the field of medicine.
vocabulary.etymology: 医 originally depicted an arrow in a quiver, related to healing wounds. 药 is herbs in a container.

examples.chinese: 他在一家医药公司工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yī jiā yī yào gōng sī gōng zuò.
examples.english: He works at a pharmaceutical company.

examples.chinese: 现代医药发展得很快。
examples.pinyin: Xiàn dài yī yào fā zhǎn de hěn kuài.
examples.english: Modern medicine is developing very quickly.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to the industry, field, or products of medicine and drugs.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 升 (rise) + 值 (value) = value rises.
vocabulary.etymology: 升 depicts a ladle, meaning to rise. 值 means value or worth.

examples.chinese: 最近人民币升值了。
examples.pinyin: Zuì jìn Rén mín bì shēng zhí le.
examples.english: The RMB has appreciated recently.

examples.chinese: 这块地未来肯定会升值。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuài dì wèi lái kěn dìng huì shēng zhí.
examples.english: This piece of land will definitely appreciate in value in the future.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Mostly used in economic/financial contexts for currencies, assets, etc. Opposite is 贬值.

vocabulary.english: to advance to a higher level school
vocabulary.mnemonic: 升 (go up) + 学 (school) = go up to the next level of school.
vocabulary.etymology: 升 (to rise) + 学 (learning, school).

examples.chinese: 孩子马上要升学了，压力很大。
examples.pinyin: Hái zi mǎ shàng yào shēng xué le, yā lì hěn dà.
examples.english: The child is about to advance to a higher school, and the pressure is huge.

examples.chinese: 升学率是衡量中学质量的一个指标。
examples.pinyin: Shēng xué lǜ shì héng liáng zhōng xué zhì liàng de yī gè zhǐ biāo.
examples.english: The advancement rate to higher education is an indicator of a middle school's quality.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used for transitions like middle school to high school, high school to university.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 升 (go up) + 级 (level) = go up a level.
vocabulary.etymology: 升 (to rise) + 级 (level, rank).

examples.chinese: 我需要升级一下电脑的系统。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xū yào shēng jí yī xià diàn nǎo de xì tǒng.
examples.english: I need to upgrade my computer's operating system.

examples.chinese: 游戏里打怪可以升级。
examples.pinyin: Yóu xì lǐ dǎ guài kě yǐ shēng jí.
examples.english: You can level up by fighting monsters in the game.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very versatile: used for technology, software, games, conflicts (e.g., 冲突升级), etc.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 半 (half) + 决赛 (final) = the match that's half-way to the final.
vocabulary.etymology: 半 means half. 决 means decide. 赛 means competition.

examples.chinese: 我们的球队进入了半决赛。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men de qiú duì jìn rù le bàn jué sài.
examples.english: Our team has advanced to the semifinals.

examples.chinese: 今晚有两场精彩的半决赛。
examples.pinyin: Jīn wǎn yǒu liǎng chǎng jīng cǎi de bàn jué sài.
examples.english: There are two exciting semifinal matches tonight.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common in sports and competition contexts. Often shortened to 半决赛.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine a group (会) of people working together (协). It's a club or society.
vocabulary.etymology: 协 (xié) originally depicted three forces combined, meaning 'unite, assist'. 会 (huì) meant 'gather, meet'.

measure_word.example: 一个协会 (yī gè xié huì)

examples.chinese: 我加入了学校的篮球协会。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā rù le xué xiào de lán qiú xié huì.
examples.english: I joined the school's basketball association.

examples.chinese: 这个协会经常组织志愿活动。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè xié huì jīng cháng zǔ zhī zhì yuàn huó dòng.
examples.english: This association often organizes volunteer activities.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very common for clubs, NGOs, and professional groups.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of offering a helpful hand (协) to aid (助) someone.
vocabulary.etymology: 协 (xié) means 'unite, assist'. 助 (zhù) means 'help, aid', showing a hand (力) adding strength.

examples.chinese: 你能协助我完成这个项目吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng xié zhù wǒ wán chéng zhè gè xiàng mù ma?
examples.english: Can you assist me in finishing this project?

examples.chinese: 感谢你一直以来对我的协助。
examples.pinyin: Gǎn xiè nǐ yǐ zhí yǐ lái duì wǒ de xié zhù.
examples.english: Thank you for your assistance all along.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Slightly more formal/cooperative than just 帮助.

vocabulary.mnemonic: To work together (协) and discuss (商) to reach an agreement.
vocabulary.etymology: 协 (xié) is 'unite'. 商 (shāng) means 'discuss, commerce', related to deliberating.

examples.chinese: 这件事我们需要好好协商一下。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì wǒ men xū yào hǎo hǎo xié shāng yī xià.
examples.english: We need to negotiate this matter properly.

examples.chinese: 经过友好协商，问题解决了。
examples.pinyin: Jīng guò yǒu hǎo xié shāng, wèn tí jiě jué le.
examples.english: After friendly consultation, the problem was solved.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for formal discussions between parties.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Making different parts work together (协) in an orderly (调) way.
vocabulary.etymology: 协 (xié) is 'unite'. 调 (tiáo) means 'blend, adjust', from words related to speech and harmony.

examples.chinese: 他在团队中负责协调大家的工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài tuán duì zhōng fù zé xié tiáo dà jiā de gōng zuò.
examples.english: He is responsible for coordinating everyone's work in the team.

examples.chinese: 这两种颜色搭配得很协调。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liǎng zhǒng yán sè dā pèi de hěn xié tiáo.
examples.english: These two colors are matched very harmoniously.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can describe both actions (verb) and a state of harmony (adjective).

vocabulary.mnemonic: It's a single (单) person hitting/playing (打) the ball.
vocabulary.etymology: 单 (dān) means 'single, alone'. 打 (dǎ) means 'hit, strike'.

measure_word.example: 一场单打比赛 (yī chǎng dān dǎ bǐ sài)

examples.chinese: 我更喜欢看网球单打比赛。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gèng xǐ huān kàn wǎng qiú dān dǎ bǐ sài.
examples.english: I prefer watching tennis singles matches.

examples.chinese: 这次羽毛球赛他报的是单打。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì yǔ máo qiú sài tā bào de shì dān dǎ.
examples.english: He signed up for singles in this badminton tournament.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in the context of racket sports (tennis, badminton, table tennis).

vocabulary.mnemonic: A field of knowledge that is both wide (博大) and deep (精深).
vocabulary.etymology: 博 (bó) 'broad, extensive', 大 (dà) 'great', 精 (jīng) 'refined, essence', 深 (shēn) 'deep'.

examples.chinese: 中国传统文化真是博大精深。
examples.pinyin: Zhōng guó chuán tǒng wén huà zhēn shì bó dà jīng shēn.
examples.english: Traditional Chinese culture is truly broad and profound.

examples.chinese: 这门学问博大精深，需要终身学习。
examples.pinyin: Zhè mén xué wèn bó dà jīng shēn, xū yào zhōng shēn xué xí.
examples.english: This field of study is vast and profound, requiring lifelong learning.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A set phrase, almost always used to praise a culture, field of study, or philosophy.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Like a soldier standing (占) and grabbing (据) a position, holding it.
vocabulary.etymology: 占 (zhàn) means 'divine, occupy'. 据 (jù) means 'according to, seize', originally related to grasping.

examples.chinese: 他的书占据了桌子的三分之一。
examples.pinyin: Tā de shū zhàn jù le zhuō zi de sān fēn zhī yī.
examples.english: His books occupy one third of the desk.

examples.chinese: 这个新闻占据了各大媒体的头条。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè xīn wén zhàn jù le gè dà méi tǐ de tóu tiáo.
examples.english: This news occupied the headlines of all major media outlets.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be used for physical space, time, or abstract things like attention/market share.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A place where you lie down (卧) as a bed/铺位 (铺).
vocabulary.etymology: 卧 (wò) means 'lie down, crouch'. 铺 (pù) means 'bed, plank bed, shop'.

measure_word.example: 一张卧铺票 (yī zhāng wò pù piào)

examples.chinese: 我买的是硬卧，睡一觉就到了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi de shì yìng wò, shuì yī jiào jiù dào le.
examples.english: I bought a hard sleeper ticket, I'll sleep and then arrive.

examples.chinese: 卧铺比坐票贵，但是舒服多了。
examples.pinyin: Wò pù bǐ zuò piào guì, dàn shì shū fu duō le.
examples.english: Sleeper berths are more expensive than seats, but much more comfortable.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly seen as 硬卧 (hard sleeper) and 软卧 (soft sleeper) on Chinese trains.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Pressing down to leave a mark, like a stamp or printed page.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted a hand pressing down on a kneeling person, conveying the idea of pressing/impressing. Evolved to mean 'seal, print'.

measure_word.example: 一个手印 (yī gè shǒu yìn)

examples.chinese: 你能帮我把这份文件印十份吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng bāng wǒ bǎ zhè fèn wén jiàn yìn shí fèn ma?
examples.english: Can you help me print ten copies of this document?

examples.chinese: 合同上需要盖公司的印。
examples.pinyin: Hé tong shàng xū yào gài gōng sī de yìn.
examples.english: The company's seal needs to be stamped on the contract.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As a verb, it's the casual word for 'to print'. As a noun, it often means a seal or stamp.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A dangerous (危) turning point or opportunity (机).
vocabulary.etymology: 危 (wēi) means 'danger, peril'. 机 (jī) here means 'crucial point, opportunity', from its meaning of 'pivot'.

measure_word.example: 一场危机 (yī chǎng wēi jī)

examples.chinese: 公司目前面临一场财务危机。
examples.pinyin: Gōng sī mù qián miàn lín yī chǎng cái wù wēi jī.
examples.english: The company is currently facing a financial crisis.

examples.chinese: 这次危机也是一个转机。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì wēi jī yě shì yī gè zhuǎn jī.
examples.english: This crisis is also a turning point.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very common word for serious problems in finance, relationships, health, etc.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Turns the sentence: what you expected... '却是'... what is actually true.
vocabulary.etymology: 却 (què) means 'step back, decline, yet'. 是 (shì) is the verb 'to be'. Together they form a contrastive phrase.

examples.chinese: 他说很简单，我试了却是很难。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuō hěn jiǎn dān, wǒ shì le què shì hěn nán.
examples.english: He said it was easy, but when I tried it, it was actually very hard.

examples.chinese: 外面很热，屋里却是很凉快。
examples.pinyin: Wài miàn hěn rè, wū lǐ què shì hěn liáng kuai.
examples.english: It's very hot outside, but inside it's actually quite cool.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used to present a contrasting fact, often with a slight sense of surprise. Placed after the subject.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A factory (厂) that sells (商) goods.
vocabulary.etymology: 厂 (chǎng) means 'factory, works'. 商 (shāng) means 'commerce, merchant'.

measure_word.example: 一家厂商 (yī jiā chǎng shāng)

examples.chinese: 我们直接联系了手机厂商。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men zhí jiē lián xì le shǒu jī chǎng shāng.
examples.english: We contacted the phone manufacturer directly.

examples.chinese: 这个产品的厂商在上海。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè chǎn pǐn de chǎng shāng zài Shàng hǎi.
examples.english: The manufacturer of this product is in Shanghai.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common in business and consumer contexts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The dynasty/generation (代) that has passed through history (历).
vocabulary.etymology: 历 (lì) is short for 历史 (lìshǐ, history), meaning 'to pass through'. 代 (dài) means 'generation, era'.

examples.chinese: 故宫收藏了历代的许多珍宝。
examples.pinyin: Gù gōng shōu cáng le lì dài de xǔ duō zhēn bǎo.
examples.english: The Palace Museum houses many treasures from successive dynasties.

examples.chinese: 这个问题历代统治者都遇到过。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè wèn tí lì dài tǒng zhì zhě dōu yù dào guò.
examples.english: Rulers of all dynasties have encountered this problem.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used when talking about history, especially Chinese imperial history.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Money (钱) given to suppress (压) the bad spirits of the old year (岁).
vocabulary.etymology: 压 (yā) 'suppress', 岁 (suì) 'year (of age)', 钱 (qián) 'money'. It originates from the belief it protects children in the new year.

measure_word.example: 一笔压岁钱 (yī bǐ yā suì qián)

examples.chinese: 过年最开心的就是收到压岁钱！
examples.pinyin: Guò nián zuì kāi xīn de jiù shì shōu dào yā suì qián!
examples.english: The happiest part of Chinese New Year is receiving lucky money!

examples.chinese: 你今年收了多少压岁钱？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ jīn nián shōu le duō shǎo yā suì qián?
examples.english: How much lucky money did you get this year?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Specifically refers to money in red envelopes given to children during Spring Festival.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Pressing (压) and extracting juice (榨), like squeezing a lemon or exploiting workers.
vocabulary.etymology: 压 (yā) 'press down'. 榨 (zhà) 'extract, squeeze (oil, juice)'.

examples.chinese: 这家工厂压榨员工，工资很低。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōng chǎng yā zhà yuán gōng, gōng zī hěn dī.
examples.english: This factory exploits its workers with very low wages.

examples.chinese: 这个机器是用来压榨橄榄油的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè jī qì shì yòng lái yā zhà gǎn lǎn yóu de.
examples.english: This machine is used to press olive oil.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Literally for extracting liquids, but very commonly used metaphorically for harsh exploitation of people.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Being pressed down (压) and forced (迫) by a powerful force.
vocabulary.etymology: 压 (yā) 'press down'. 迫 (pò) 'compel, force, urgent'.

examples.chinese: 历史上，人民长期受到压迫。
examples.pinyin: Lì shǐ shàng, rén mín cháng qī shòu dào yā pò.
examples.english: Historically, the people suffered long-term oppression.

examples.chinese: 不要用你的权力去压迫别人。
examples.pinyin: Bù yào yòng nǐ de quán lì qù yā pò bié rén.
examples.english: Don't use your power to oppress others.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A strong word for political, social, or personal domination.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A feeling of being sick (厌) and having evil/badness (恶) towards something.
vocabulary.etymology: 厌 (yàn) means 'be disgusted with, be tired of'. 恶 (wù) is the pronunciation for 'dislike, hate' (different from è 'evil').

examples.chinese: 我特别厌恶别人在公共场所抽烟。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ tè bié yàn wù bié rén zài gōng gòng chǎng suǒ chōu yān.
examples.english: I especially detest people smoking in public places.

examples.chinese: 他对这种虚伪的行为感到厌恶。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì zhè zhǒng xū wěi de xíng wéi gǎn dào yàn wù.
examples.english: He feels loathing towards this kind of hypocritical behavior.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Stronger and more formal than 讨厌. It's a deep dislike.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A place (所) for... well, a place for the toilet. 'Ce Suo' sounds like 'say so' as in 'I need to go, if you say so!'
vocabulary.etymology: 厕 (cè) originally meant 'side, adjunct' and later referred to a side room for waste. 所 (suǒ) is a nominalizing suffix meaning 'place'.

measure_word.example: 一间厕所 (yī jiān cè suǒ)

examples.chinese: 请问，厕所在哪里？
examples.pinyin: Qǐng wèn, cè suǒ zài nǎ lǐ?
examples.english: Excuse me, where is the toilet?

examples.chinese: 这个公园的厕所很干净。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè gōng yuán de cè suǒ hěn gān jìng.
examples.english: The toilets in this park are very clean.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The most common and direct word for toilet. 卫生间/洗手间 are slightly more polite alternatives.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The source, like the original (原) map of a place.
vocabulary.etymology: The character depicts a spring (厂) flowing from a cliff (泉), representing 'source, origin'.

examples.chinese: 这是我原定的计划。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ yuán dìng de jì huà.
examples.english: This is my original plan.

examples.chinese: 他原是我的同事，现在辞职了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yuán shì wǒ de tóng shì, xiàn zài cí zhí le.
examples.english: He was formerly my colleague, but has now resigned.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used as a prefix (原计划, 原价) or in set phrases. Can also be a surname (Yuán).

vocabulary.mnemonic: The original (原) party who tells/complains (告) to the court.
vocabulary.etymology: 原 (yuán) 'original'. 告 (gào) 'tell, accuse, sue'.

measure_word.example: 一位原告 (yī wèi yuán gào)

examples.chinese: 原告要求被告赔偿损失。
examples.pinyin: Yuán gào yāo qiú bèi gào péi cháng sǔn shī.
examples.english: The plaintiff demanded that the defendant compensate for the losses.

examples.chinese: 法院今天听取了原告的陈述。
examples.pinyin: Fǎ yuàn jīn tiān tīng qǔ le yuán gào de chén shù.
examples.english: The court heard the plaintiff's statement today.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Legal term. The opposite is 被告 (defendant).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Going back to the original (原) understanding/consideration (谅) before the mistake.
vocabulary.etymology: 原 (yuán) 'original, source'. 谅 (liàng) 'understand, excuse'.

examples.chinese: 我知道错了，请你原谅我。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhī dào cuò le, qǐng nǐ yuán liàng wǒ.
examples.english: I know I was wrong, please forgive me.

examples.chinese: 这次我可以原谅你，但下不为例。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì wǒ kě yǐ yuán liàng nǐ, dàn xià bù wéi lì.
examples.english: I can forgive you this time, but don't let it happen again.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The standard word for asking for or granting forgiveness.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A kitchen (厨) master/teacher (师).
vocabulary.etymology: 厨 (chú) means 'kitchen'. 师 (shī) means 'master, teacher'.

measure_word.example: 一位厨师 (yī wèi chú shī)

examples.chinese: 这家餐厅的厨师是四川人。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cān tīng de chú shī shì Sì chuān rén.
examples.english: The chef at this restaurant is from Sichuan.

examples.chinese: 我的梦想是成为一名厨师。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de mèng xiǎng shì chéng wéi yī míng chú shī.
examples.english: My dream is to become a chef.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Respectful term for a professional cook.

vocabulary.english: to remove, to get rid of
vocabulary.mnemonic: To go (去) and make it drop/fall off (掉).
vocabulary.etymology: 去 (qù) 'go, remove'. 掉 (diào) 'fall, drop, lose'.

examples.chinese: 请把图片上的水印去掉。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ tú piàn shàng de shuǐ yìn qù diào.
examples.english: Please remove the watermark from the picture.

examples.chinese: 你应该去掉这个坏习惯。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yīng gāi qù diào zhè gè huài xí guàn.
examples.english: You should get rid of this bad habit.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very common and casual for removing anything physical or abstract.

vocabulary.mnemonic: To take part in (参) and display (展) at an exhibition.
vocabulary.etymology: 参 (cān) 'participate, join'. 展 (zhǎn) 'unfold, exhibit'.

examples.chinese: 我们公司每年都会参展广交会。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men gōng sī měi nián dōu huì cān zhǎn Guǎng jiāo huì.
examples.english: Our company participates in the Canton Fair every year.

examples.chinese: 参展商需要提前布置好展位。
examples.pinyin: Cān zhǎn shāng xū yào tí qián bù zhì hǎo zhǎn wèi.
examples.english: Exhibitors need to set up their booths in advance.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Specific to trade shows, art exhibitions, etc.

vocabulary.mnemonic: To take part in (参) a contest/match (赛).
vocabulary.etymology: 参 (cān) 'participate, join'. 赛 (sài) 'contest, match'.

examples.chinese: 一共有二十支队伍参赛。
examples.pinyin: Yī gòng yǒu èr shí zhī duì wu cān sài.
examples.english: There are twenty teams participating in the competition in total.

examples.chinese: 你想参赛的话，今天就要报名了。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng cān sài de huà, jīn tiān jiù yào bào míng le.
examples.english: If you want to enter the competition, you need to sign up today.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for entering races, games, contests, etc.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of two people (双) hitting a ball back and forth in a tennis doubles match.
vocabulary.etymology: 双 means 'pair' or 'two', 打 means 'to hit' or 'to play' (a sport). Combined, it refers to a game played by two pairs.

examples.chinese: 明天的网球比赛，我报名参加双打。
examples.pinyin: Míng tiān de wǎng qiú bǐ sài, wǒ bào míng cān jiā shuāng dǎ.
examples.english: For tomorrow's tennis match, I signed up for doubles.

examples.chinese: 我们俩配合得不错，双打应该能赢。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men liǎ pèi hé de bú cuò, shuāng dǎ yīng gāi néng yíng.
examples.english: We cooperate well, we should be able to win the doubles.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used primarily for racket sports like tennis, badminton, and table tennis.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It's the 'reverse (反) of this (之)' – flipping the situation you just described.
vocabulary.etymology: 反 means 'reverse' or 'opposite', 之 is a classical Chinese pronoun meaning 'it' or 'this'. Together, they mean 'the opposite of this'.

examples.chinese: 努力复习通常能考好，反之，就可能不及格。
examples.pinyin: Nǔ lì fù xí tōng cháng néng kǎo hǎo, fǎn zhī, jiù kě néng bù jí gé.
examples.english: Studying hard usually leads to good grades; conversely, you might fail.

examples.chinese: 你喜欢就去，反之，不喜欢就别勉强。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xǐ huān jiù qù, fǎn zhī, bù xǐ huān jiù bié miǎn qiǎng.
examples.english: Go if you like it; on the other hand, don't force yourself if you don't.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used to introduce a contrasting or opposite statement. Common in both writing and formal speech.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of a force that wants to act (动) in reverse (反), opposing progress.
vocabulary.etymology: 反 means 'oppose' or 'against', 动 means 'move' or 'act'. Historically, it described political forces opposing revolutionary change.

examples.chinese: 那是一股反动的思潮。
examples.pinyin: Nà shì yī gǔ fǎn dòng de sī cháo.
examples.english: That is a reactionary trend of thought.

examples.chinese: 这个词有很强的历史和政治色彩。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge cí yǒu hěn qiáng de lì shǐ hé zhèng zhì sè cǎi.
examples.english: This word carries strong historical and political connotations.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A politically charged term. Use with caution and awareness of context. Common in historical/political discourse.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Your action makes a sound (响) that bounces back (反) to you as public reaction.
vocabulary.etymology: 反 can mean 'back' or 'in return', 响 means 'sound' or 'echo'. Combined, it evokes the idea of an echo or sound coming back, i.e., a response.

examples.chinese: 这部电影在社会上引起了很大的反响。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diàn yǐng zài shè huì shang yǐn qǐ le hěn dà de fǎn xiǎng.
examples.english: This movie has caused a huge response in society.

examples.chinese: 你发的帖子反响怎么样？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ fā de tiě zi fǎn xiǎng zěn me yàng?
examples.english: How was the response to the post you made?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for public or widespread reactions to events, speeches, art, etc.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Light hits a surface and is sent back (反) or shot (射) away.
vocabulary.etymology: 反 means 'in reverse' or 'back', 射 means 'to shoot' or 'project'. The term describes something being projected back.

examples.chinese: 湖面反射着夕阳的光芒。
examples.pinyin: Hú miàn fǎn shè zhe xī yáng de guāng máng.
examples.english: The lake surface reflects the glow of the setting sun.

examples.chinese: 医生检查了我的膝跳反射。
examples.pinyin: Yī shēng jiǎn chá le wǒ de xī tiào fǎn shè.
examples.english: The doctor checked my knee-jerk reflex.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used in both physics (light/sound) and biology/medicine (reflexes).

vocabulary.mnemonic: You oppose (反) and fight against (抗) something.
vocabulary.etymology: 反 means 'oppose', 抗 means 'resist' or 'fight'. The combination intensifies the meaning of active opposition.

examples.chinese: 人民反抗暴政。
examples.pinyin: Rén mín fǎn kàng bào zhèng.
examples.english: The people resist tyranny.

examples.chinese: 别反抗了，乖乖听话。
examples.pinyin: Bié fǎn kàng le, guāi guāi tīng huà.
examples.english: Stop resisting and be obedient.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Implies a stronger, more active form of opposition than just '反对'.

vocabulary.english: to ask in return; rhetorical question
vocabulary.mnemonic: Instead of answering, you flip the question back (反) and ask (问) them one.
vocabulary.etymology: 反 means 'back' or 'in return', 问 means 'to ask'. It's the act of asking a question back.

examples.chinese: 他没回答，反而反问我：“你觉得呢？”
examples.pinyin: Tā méi huí dá, fǎn ér fǎn wèn wǒ: “Nǐ jué de ne?”
examples.english: He didn't answer, but instead asked me in return, 'What do you think?'

examples.chinese: 你这不是在反问吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhè bú shì zài fǎn wèn ma?
examples.english: Aren't you just asking a rhetorical question?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be a genuine counter-question or a rhetorical device expressing doubt or emphasis.

vocabulary.english: to space out; to stare blankly
vocabulary.mnemonic: Your brain seems to have gone on strike (呆), and you're just in a daze (发).
vocabulary.etymology: 发 here indicates the onset of a state, 呆 means 'stupid' or 'wooden'. It describes entering a state of mental blankness.

examples.chinese: 上课别发呆，认真听讲！
examples.pinyin: Shàng kè bié fā dāi, rèn zhēn tīng jiǎng!
examples.english: Don't space out in class, pay attention!

examples.chinese: 我刚才看着窗外发了一会儿呆。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gāng cái kàn zhe chuāng wài fā le yī huì er dāi.
examples.english: I was just staring out the window spacing out for a while.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very common, casual word for daydreaming or zoning out.

vocabulary.english: to get angry; to fly into a rage
vocabulary.mnemonic: You 'emit' (发) 'anger' (怒).
vocabulary.etymology: 发 indicates the outbreak or expression of an emotion, 怒 means 'anger'. It means to become/show anger.

examples.chinese: 老板看到报告后发怒了。
examples.pinyin: Lǎo bǎn kàn dào bào gào hòu fā nù le.
examples.english: The boss flew into a rage after seeing the report.

examples.chinese: 他对孩子发怒是不对的。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì hái zi fā nù shì bú duì de.
examples.english: It's wrong for him to get angry at the child.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Slightly more formal/literary than '生气', but still common. Emphasizes the outburst.

vocabulary.mnemonic: An organization sends out (发) and gives (放) things like money or supplies.
vocabulary.etymology: 发 means 'to send out', 放 means 'to release' or 'to let go'. Together they mean to send out and release items to people.

examples.chinese: 公司每月5号发放工资。
examples.pinyin: Gōng sī měi yuè wǔ hào fā fàng gōng zī.
examples.english: The company distributes salaries on the 5th of each month.

examples.chinese: 政府向灾区发放救灾物资。
examples.pinyin: Zhèng fǔ xiàng zāi qū fā fàng jiù zāi wù zī.
examples.english: The government is issuing disaster relief supplies to the affected area.
