vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for organized distribution of items by authorities, companies, or institutions.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A part of your body 'develops' (发) 'flame' (炎, which looks like two fires).
vocabulary.etymology: 发 indicates the onset or occurrence, 炎 means 'inflammation' or 'flame' (from two 火 'fire' characters stacked). It describes the flaring up of inflammation.

examples.chinese: 我的牙龈发炎了，好疼。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de yá yín fā yán le, hǎo téng.
examples.english: My gums are inflamed, it hurts so much.

examples.chinese: 伤口没处理好，发炎了。
examples.pinyin: Shāng kǒu méi chǔ lǐ hǎo, fā yán le.
examples.english: The wound wasn't treated properly and got infected/inflamed.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very common medical term in everyday life for any kind of inflammation.

vocabulary.mnemonic: To 'produce' (发) 'electricity' (电).
vocabulary.etymology: 发 here means 'to generate' or 'produce', 电 means 'electricity'.

examples.chinese: 这座水电站发的电够整个城市用。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò shuǐ diàn zhàn fā de diàn gòu zhěng gè chéng shì yòng.
examples.english: The electricity generated by this hydropower station is enough for the whole city.

examples.chinese: 他们在讨论用太阳能发电。
examples.pinyin: Tā men zài tǎo lùn yòng tài yáng néng fā diàn.
examples.english: They are discussing using solar power to generate electricity.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The general verb for power generation.

vocabulary.english: to have an attack (of illness); onset of disease
vocabulary.mnemonic: A disease 'erupts' (发) or 'happens' (病).
vocabulary.etymology: 发 indicates the onset or outbreak, 病 means 'disease' or 'illness'. It refers to the moment an illness manifests or recurs.

examples.chinese: 他心脏病突然发病，被送进了医院。
examples.pinyin: Tā xīn zàng bìng tū rán fā bìng, bèi sòng jìn le yī yuàn.
examples.english: He had a sudden heart attack and was taken to the hospital.

examples.chinese: 这种病一般在春季发病。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng bìng yī bān zài chūn jì fā bìng.
examples.english: This disease usually has its onset in spring.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for sudden or acute episodes of chronic or serious diseases.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The person (人) who speaks out (发言) on behalf of a group.
vocabulary.etymology: A compound of 发言 (to speak; to make a statement) + 人 (person).

examples.chinese: 外交部发言人在记者会上回答了问题。
examples.pinyin: Wài jiāo bù fā yán rén zài jì zhě huì shang huí dá le wèn tí.
examples.english: The foreign ministry spokesperson answered questions at the press conference.

examples.chinese: 公司发言人说他们正在调查此事。
examples.pinyin: Gōng sī fā yán rén shuō tā men zhèng zài diào chá cǐ shì.
examples.english: The company spokesperson said they are investigating the matter.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for official representatives of governments, companies, organizations, etc.

vocabulary.mnemonic: To 'send forth' (发) and 'rise up' (起) a new activity.
vocabulary.etymology: 发 means 'to start' or 'send out', 起 means 'to rise' or 'begin'. Together they mean to cause something to begin.

examples.chinese: 是他发起了这次募捐活动。
examples.pinyin: Shì tā fā qǐ le zhè cì mù juān huó dòng.
examples.english: He was the one who initiated this fundraising campaign.

examples.chinese: 球队在最后五分钟发起了猛烈的进攻。
examples.pinyin: Qiú duì zài zuì hòu wǔ fēn zhōng fā qǐ le měng liè de jìn gōng.
examples.english: The team launched a fierce attack in the last five minutes.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for starting activities, campaigns, attacks, movements, etc.

vocabulary.mnemonic: You go to 'take' (取) 'money' (款).
vocabulary.etymology: 取 means 'to take', 款 means 'funds' or 'money'. It specifically means taking money out of an account.

examples.chinese: 我要去银行取款。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yào qù yín háng qǔ kuǎn.
examples.english: I need to go to the bank to withdraw money.

examples.chinese: 现在用手机银行就能取款预约。
examples.pinyin: Xiàn zài yòng shǒu jī yín háng jiù néng qǔ kuǎn yù yuē.
examples.english: Now you can schedule a withdrawal using mobile banking.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The standard term for withdrawing cash from a bank account.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The machine (机) for withdrawing (取款) money.
vocabulary.etymology: A compound of 取款 (withdraw money) + 机 (machine).

examples.chinese: 前面便利店旁边有台取款机。
examples.pinyin: Qián miàn biàn lì diàn páng biān yǒu tái qǔ kuǎn jī.
examples.english: There's an ATM next to the convenience store ahead.

examples.chinese: 这台取款机坏了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tái qǔ kuǎn jī huài le.
examples.english: This ATM is out of order.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very common. 'ATM' itself is also widely understood and used.

vocabulary.english: to suffer; to have a hard time
vocabulary.mnemonic: You 'receive' (受) 'punishment' or 'blame' (罪).
vocabulary.etymology: 受 means 'to receive' or 'undergo', 罪 originally meant 'crime' or 'blame', here extended to mean 'hardship' or 'suffering'.

examples.chinese: 这么热的天气没空调，真是受罪。
examples.pinyin: Zhè me rè de tiān qì méi kōng tiáo, zhēn shì shòu zuì.
examples.english: It's such suffering to have no air conditioning in this hot weather.

examples.chinese: 跟着他爬山，我可受了大罪了。
examples.pinyin: Gēn zhe tā pá shān, wǒ kě shòu le dà zuì le.
examples.english: Hiking with him, I really had a terrible time.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very colloquial and expressive word for enduring discomfort or hardship, often used hyperbolically.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Something changes (变) its shape (形).
vocabulary.etymology: 变 means 'to change', 形 means 'shape' or 'form'.

examples.chinese: 这个塑料盒子受热变形了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge sù liào hé zi shòu rè biàn xíng le.
examples.english: This plastic box deformed from the heat.

examples.chinese: 看！那个机器人变形了！
examples.pinyin: Kàn! Nà ge jī qì rén biàn xíng le!
examples.english: Look! That robot is transforming!

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be negative (deform) or neutral/fantasy (transform, like Transformers).

vocabulary.mnemonic: To 'change' (变) and 'exchange' (换) one thing for another.
vocabulary.etymology: 变 means 'to change', 换 means 'to exchange'. Together they emphasize a switch or alteration.

examples.chinese: 你可以自由变换电脑桌面的背景。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kě yǐ zì yóu biàn huàn diàn nǎo zhuō miàn de bèi jǐng.
examples.english: You can freely change your computer desktop background.

examples.chinese: 他不停地变换话题。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù tíng de biàn huàn huà tí.
examples.english: He kept changing the subject.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for changing between different options, states, or methods.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A sudden 'change' (变) in your life's 'circumstances' (故), usually for the worse.
vocabulary.etymology: 变 means 'change', 故 means 'incident' or 'event'. It refers to an unexpected, often negative, event.

examples.chinese: 一场家庭变故改变了他的性格。
examples.pinyin: Yī chǎng jiā tíng biàn gù gǎi biàn le tā de xìng gé.
examples.english: A family misfortune changed his personality.

examples.chinese: 计划赶不上变化，总会有变故。
examples.pinyin: Jì huà gǎn bú shàng biàn huà, zǒng huì yǒu biàn gù.
examples.english: Plans can't keep up with changes; there are always unforeseen events.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to significant, disruptive events, often with a negative connotation.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A formal 'change' (变) and 'replacement' (更). Used for plans, rules, etc.
vocabulary.etymology: 变 means 'change', 更 means 'to change' or 'replace'. It's a somewhat redundant compound emphasizing alteration.

examples.chinese: 会议时间有变更，请注意通知。
examples.pinyin: Huì yì shí jiān yǒu biàn gēng, qǐng zhù yì tōng zhī.
examples.english: The meeting time has been changed, please note the notice.

examples.chinese: 如需变更行程，请提前联系。
examples.pinyin: Rú xū biàn gēng xíng chéng, qǐng tí qián lián xì.
examples.english: If you need to alter the itinerary, please contact us in advance.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common in formal, official, or business contexts for changes to plans, rules, data, etc.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A test (试) you take with your mouth (口).
vocabulary.etymology: 口 means 'mouth', 试 means 'test' or 'exam'.

examples.chinese: 我明天的英语课有口试。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ míng tiān de yīng yǔ kè yǒu kǒu shì.
examples.english: I have an oral exam in my English class tomorrow.

examples.chinese: 别紧张，口试没那么难。
examples.pinyin: Bié jǐn zhāng, kǒu shì méi nà me nán.
examples.english: Don't be nervous, the oral exam isn't that hard.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The standard term for a spoken test, common in language learning.

vocabulary.mnemonic: From ancient (古) times, representing a standard (典) of excellence.
vocabulary.etymology: 古 means 'ancient', 典 means 'canon' or 'standard'. It refers to things from antiquity that are considered exemplary.

examples.chinese: 我喜欢听古典音乐。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐ huān tīng gǔ diǎn yīn yuè.
examples.english: I like listening to classical music.

examples.chinese: 这座建筑很有古典美。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò jiàn zhù hěn yǒu gǔ diǎn měi.
examples.english: This building has a classical beauty.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for classical music, literature, art, architecture, etc., often with a sense of tradition and refinement.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It points to an 'additional' thing, separate from the one just mentioned.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally meant 'to separate'. Evolved to mean 'another' or 'additional'.

examples.chinese: 这件事我们另找时间谈吧。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì wǒ men lìng zhǎo shí jiān tán ba.
examples.english: Let's find another time to talk about this.

examples.chinese: 这份是你的，另那份是他的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fèn shì nǐ de, lìng nà fèn shì tā de.
examples.english: This portion is yours, and that other portion is his.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used as a modifier before nouns (另一个人) or in set phrases like '另请高明', '另当别论'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine your throat doing the '吞' wave to '咽' down food.
vocabulary.etymology: 吞 depicts a person with a big mouth; 咽 originally meant throat.

examples.chinese: 吃药片的时候要小心吞咽。
examples.pinyin: Chī yào piàn de shí hou yào xiǎo xīn tūn yàn.
examples.english: Be careful swallowing when taking pills.

examples.chinese: 他太紧张了，连口水都难以下咽。
examples.pinyin: Tā tài jǐn zhāng le, lián kǒu shuǐ dōu nán yǐ xià yàn.
examples.english: He was so nervous he could barely swallow his saliva.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for the physical act of swallowing solid or liquid.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Listen (听) and then take (取) in the information.
vocabulary.etymology: 听 means to listen; 取 means to take or obtain.

examples.chinese: 老板会认真听取员工的反馈。
examples.pinyin: Lǎo bǎn huì rèn zhēn tīng qǔ yuán gōng de fǎn kuì.
examples.english: The boss will seriously listen to the employees' feedback.

examples.chinese: 做决定前，最好多听取一下别人的看法。
examples.pinyin: Zuò jué dìng qián, zuì hǎo duō tīng qǔ yī xià bié rén de kàn fǎ.
examples.english: Before making a decision, it's best to listen to others' opinions.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for listening to advice, opinions, or reports, implying consideration.

vocabulary.english: to set out on a journey
vocabulary.mnemonic: Open (启) the door and embark on the road (程).
vocabulary.etymology: 启 means to open or start; 程 means journey or distance.

examples.chinese: 我们明早六点启程去机场。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men míng zǎo liù diǎn qǐ chéng qù jī chǎng.
examples.english: We set out for the airport at six tomorrow morning.

examples.chinese: 他刚刚启程，估计下午才能到。
examples.pinyin: Tā gāng gāng qǐ chéng, gū jì xià wǔ cái néng dào.
examples.english: He just set out, so he probably won't arrive until the afternoon.

vocabulary.usage_notes: More formal/literary than '出发', but still common for planned trips.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 吸 (suck in) poison (毒).
vocabulary.etymology: 吸 means to inhale or suck; 毒 means poison or drugs.

examples.chinese: 吸毒会严重危害你的健康和家庭。
examples.pinyin: Xī dú huì yán zhòng wēi hài nǐ de jiàn kāng hé jiā tíng.
examples.english: Taking drugs will seriously harm your health and family.

examples.chinese: 他因为吸毒被抓起来了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīn wèi xī dú bèi zhuā qǐ lái le.
examples.english: He was arrested for taking drugs.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers specifically to illegal drug use. Often used in serious contexts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It takes many '周' (circuits) and '折' (turns/folds) to get it done.
vocabulary.etymology: 周 means circuit or circumference; 折 means to break or bend.

examples.chinese: 办这个签证费了不少周折。
examples.pinyin: Bàn zhè gè qiān zhèng fèi le bù shǎo zhōu zhé.
examples.english: Getting this visa involved a lot of twists and turns.

examples.chinese: 事情虽然有点周折，但最终还是办成了。
examples.pinyin: Shì qing suī rán yǒu diǎn zhōu zhé, dàn zuì zhōng hái shì bàn chéng le.
examples.english: Although there were some complications, it was eventually done.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common in phrases like '费周折', '经过周折'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Money or goods make a weekly (周) turn (转).
vocabulary.etymology: 周 means cycle; 转 means to turn or revolve.

examples.chinese: 我们公司最近资金周转有点困难。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men gōng sī zuì jìn zī jīn zhōu zhuǎn yǒu diǎn kùn nán.
examples.english: Our company is having some difficulty with cash flow recently.

examples.chinese: 这批货周转得很快。
examples.pinyin: Zhè pī huò zhōu zhuǎn de hěn kuài.
examples.english: This batch of goods has a very fast turnover.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Mostly used in business/finance contexts for the flow of capital or inventory.

vocabulary.english: ah; oh (expressing surprise, sigh, or laughter)
vocabulary.mnemonic: The sound of an exhale or a light laugh: 'he'.
vocabulary.etymology: Pictophonetic; 口 (mouth) radical indicates sound. Originally meant to breathe out.

examples.chinese: 呵，你居然还知道回来啊？
examples.pinyin: Hē, nǐ jū rán hái zhī dào huí lái a?
examples.english: Oh, so you actually know how to come back?

examples.chinese: 他呵了一口气，在玻璃上画了个笑脸。
examples.pinyin: Tā hē le yī kǒu qì, zài bō li shàng huà le gè xiào liǎn.
examples.english: He breathed out a puff of air and drew a smiley face on the glass.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in informal writing to express emotion. Can also be the verb 'to breathe out' (呵气).

vocabulary.mnemonic: It sounds like 'shen yin' — the noise you make when in pain.
vocabulary.etymology: Both characters contain the 口 (mouth) radical, indicating sound. Associated with vocal expressions of pain.

examples.chinese: 他头疼得一直在呻吟。
examples.pinyin: Tā tóu téng de yī zhí zài shēn yín.
examples.english: His head hurt so much he kept groaning.

examples.chinese: 别老是呻吟了，想想办法吧！
examples.pinyin: Bié lǎo shì shēn yín le, xiǎng xiǎng bàn fǎ ba!
examples.english: Stop moaning all the time and think of a solution!

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for sounds made due to physical pain, discomfort, or sometimes emotional suffering.

vocabulary.english: to whistle, to howl (wind, bullet, etc.)
vocabulary.mnemonic: The wind calls out (呼) with a sharp whistle (啸).
vocabulary.etymology: 呼 means to call out; 啸 means to whistle or howl.

examples.chinese: 北风在窗外呼啸了一整夜。
examples.pinyin: Běi fēng zài chuāng wài hū xiào le yī zhěng yè.
examples.english: The north wind howled outside the window all night.

examples.chinese: 子弹从我们头顶呼啸而过。
examples.pinyin: Zǐ dàn cóng wǒ men tóu dǐng hū xiào ér guò.
examples.english: Bullets whistled past over our heads.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Describes a loud, sharp, often sustained sound made by fast-moving air or objects.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It's your '命' to live one 'life'.
vocabulary.etymology: Depicts a person kneeling and receiving orders,引申为 life or fate.

examples.chinese: 这都是命，没办法。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dōu shì mìng, méi bàn fǎ.
examples.english: This is all fate, there's nothing to be done.

examples.chinese: 医生救了他一命。
examples.pinyin: Yī shēng jiù le tā yī mìng.
examples.english: The doctor saved his life.

examples.chinese: 老板下了命令，必须今天完成。
examples.pinyin: Lǎo bǎn xià le mìng lìng, bì xū jīn tiān wán chéng.
examples.english: The boss gave the order that it must be finished today.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Context determines meaning: life (生命), fate (命运), or command (命令). Very common character.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Both characters have the mouth (口) radical — it's all about mouth action.
vocabulary.etymology: Both characters contain 口 (mouth). 咀 means to taste or chew; 嚼 means to masticate.

examples.chinese: 吃饭要细嚼慢咽，好好咀嚼。
examples.pinyin: Chī fàn yào xì jiáo màn yàn, hǎo hǎo jǔ jué.
examples.english: You should eat slowly and chew your food well.

examples.chinese: 他在一边默默地咀嚼着这个坏消息。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yī biān mò mò de jǔ jué zhe zhè gè huài xiāo xi.
examples.english: He was silently chewing over this piece of bad news.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be used literally for chewing food, or figuratively for pondering/considering something deeply.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Sounds like 'za' — '咋整?' meaning 'How to deal with this?'
vocabulary.etymology: A colloquial character, often used in northern dialects. Possibly a fusion of sounds.

examples.chinese: 你这是咋了？脸色这么差。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhè shì zǎ le? Liǎn sè zhè me chà.
examples.english: What's wrong with you? You look so pale.

examples.chinese: 明天到底咋安排？
examples.pinyin: Míng tiān dào dǐ zǎ ān pái?
examples.english: How are we actually arranging things for tomorrow?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very casual, common in northern Chinese speech. Equivalent to '怎么' or '为什么'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: When everyone has grain (禾) to eat and can all talk (谐), society is harmonious.
vocabulary.etymology: 和 originally meant harmony in music/peace; 谐 means in accord or harmonious.

examples.chinese: 我们希望建立一个和谐的社会。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men xī wàng jiàn lì yī gè hé xié de shè huì.
examples.english: We hope to build a harmonious society.

examples.chinese: 他们一家人相处得非常和谐。
examples.pinyin: Tā men yī jiā rén xiāng chǔ de fēi cháng hé xié.
examples.english: Their family gets along very harmoniously.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very positive and commonly used word in modern Chinese, describing relationships, societies, or environments.

vocabulary.mnemonic: You seek (咨) and ask for (询) advice.
vocabulary.etymology: 咨 means to consult or take counsel; 询 means to ask.

examples.chinese: 有什么问题可以咨询我们的客服。
examples.pinyin: Yǒu shén me wèn tí kě yǐ zī xún wǒ men de kè fú.
examples.english: If you have any questions, you can consult our customer service.

examples.chinese: 我需要做个法律咨询。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xū yào zuò gè fǎ lǜ zī xún.
examples.english: I need to get some legal advice.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common in professional/service contexts (e.g., 心理咨询, 留学咨询). More formal than '问'.

vocabulary.english: to gnash one's teeth (with anger or hatred)
vocabulary.mnemonic: Picture someone so angry they bite (咬) their teeth (牙) and grind (切) them together.
vocabulary.etymology: Literally: bite + teeth + cut + teeth. Describes the physical act of grinding teeth.

examples.chinese: 听到那个消息，他气得咬牙切齿。
examples.pinyin: Tīng dào nà gè xiāo xi, tā qì de yǎo yá qiè chǐ.
examples.english: When he heard the news, he was so angry he gnashed his teeth.

examples.chinese: 他对那个骗子恨得咬牙切齿。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì nà gè piàn zi hèn de yǎo yá qiè chǐ.
examples.english: He hated that swindler with a gnashing of teeth.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A vivid idiom describing extreme anger, hatred, or frustration.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A product's quality (品) plaque or signboard (牌).
vocabulary.etymology: 品 means product or grade; 牌 means plaque, tablet, or card.

examples.chinese: 我比较喜欢买这个品牌的衣服。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǐ jiào xǐ huān mǎi zhè gè pǐn pái de yī fu.
examples.english: I prefer to buy clothes from this brand.

examples.chinese: 建立一个好的品牌需要很长时间。
examples.pinyin: Jiàn lì yī gè hǎo de pǐn pái xū yào hěn cháng shí jiān.
examples.english: Building a good brand takes a very long time.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very common in shopping and business contexts. Slightly more formal/commercial than '牌子'.

vocabulary.english: wow! whoa! (expressing surprise, admiration, or sometimes distress)
vocabulary.mnemonic: The sound 'wa' you make when you see something amazing.
vocabulary.etymology: A phonetic character (口 + 圭). Imitative of a cry or exclamation.

examples.chinese: 哇，你的新手机真酷！
examples.pinyin: Wā, nǐ de xīn shǒu jī zhēn kù!
examples.english: Wow, your new phone is so cool!

examples.chinese: 哇，好烫！
examples.pinyin: Wā, hǎo tàng!
examples.english: Whoa, that's hot!

vocabulary.usage_notes: Extremely common and versatile interjection in spoken Chinese, similar to English 'wow'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A sound (声) that rings out (响).
vocabulary.etymology: 响 means sound or echo; 声 means sound or voice.

examples.chinese: 外面传来一阵奇怪的响声。
examples.pinyin: Wài miàn chuán lái yī zhèn qí guài de xiǎng shēng.
examples.english: A strange sound came from outside.

examples.chinese: 别弄出那么大的响声，孩子在睡觉。
examples.pinyin: Bié nòng chū nà me dà de xiǎng shēng, hái zi zài shuì jiào.
examples.english: Don't make such a loud noise, the child is sleeping.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to a specific instance or type of sound, often a noticeable or loud one.

vocabulary.english: ouch!; oh dear! (expressing pain, surprise, or regret)
vocabulary.mnemonic: Sounds like 'ai yo' — the noise you make when you stub your toe.
vocabulary.etymology: Phonetic characters expressing a sigh or exclamation.

examples.chinese: 哎哟，我不小心撞到桌子了。
examples.pinyin: Āi yō, wǒ bù xiǎo xīn zhuàng dào zhuō zi le.
examples.english: Ouch, I accidentally bumped into the table.

examples.chinese: 哎哟，我把你的杯子打碎了，真对不起！
examples.pinyin: Āi yō, wǒ bǎ nǐ de bēi zi dǎ suì le, zhēn duì bu qǐ!
examples.english: Oh dear, I broke your cup, I'm so sorry!

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very common, expressive two-syllable interjection in daily speech.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A little (小) mouth (口) that makes a sharp sound.
vocabulary.etymology: 口 (mouth) radical + 肖 (resemble). Something that makes a mouth-like sound.

examples.chinese: 裁判吹了一声哨，比赛开始了。
examples.pinyin: Cái pàn chuī le yī shēng shào, bǐ sài kāi shǐ le.
examples.english: The referee blew the whistle, and the match began.

examples.chinese: 他在边境的哨所工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài biān jìng de shào suǒ gōng zuò.
examples.english: He works at a border sentry post.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can refer to the object (whistle), the sound, or a guard post (哨所).

vocabulary.mnemonic: The study (学) of wisdom (哲).
vocabulary.etymology: 哲 means wise or sagacious; 学 means study or learning.

examples.chinese: 他对中国古代哲学很感兴趣。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì Zhōng guó gǔ dài zhé xué hěn gǎn xìng qù.
examples.english: He is very interested in ancient Chinese philosophy.

examples.chinese: 你这话说得太有哲学了。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhè huà shuō de tài yǒu zhé xué le.
examples.english: What you said is very philosophical.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The academic subject. Can also be used informally to describe deeply thoughtful remarks.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A child (子) is fed (哺) with milk (乳).
vocabulary.etymology: 哺 means to feed; 乳 means milk or breast.

examples.chinese: 哺乳期的妈妈需要多补充营养。
examples.pinyin: Bǔ rǔ qī de mā ma xū yào duō bǔ chōng yíng yǎng.
examples.english: Mothers who are breastfeeding need to get more nutrition.

examples.chinese: 鲸鱼是哺乳动物。
examples.pinyin: Jīng yú shì bǔ rǔ dòng wù.
examples.english: Whales are mammals.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Technical/formal term for breastfeeding. Also appears in '哺乳动物' (mammal).

vocabulary.mnemonic: What comes from your mouth (口) and is '沫' (foam).
vocabulary.etymology: 唾 means to spit; 沫 means foam or bubble.

examples.chinese: 说话说太多，唾沫都快说干了。
examples.pinyin: Shuō huà shuō tài duō, tuò mo dōu kuài shuō gān le.
examples.english: I've talked so much my saliva is almost dry.

examples.chinese: 别随地吐唾沫，不卫生。
examples.pinyin: Bié suí dì tǔ tuò mo, bù wèi shēng.
examples.english: Don't spit saliva everywhere, it's unhygienic.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Colloquial term for saliva. Can have a slightly negative connotation compared to '口水'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A commercial (商) city (城) full of shops.
vocabulary.etymology: 商 means commerce or merchant; 城 means city or walled enclosure.

examples.chinese: 周末我们常去那个大商城逛街。
examples.pinyin: Zhōu mò wǒ men cháng qù nà gè dà shāng chéng guàng jiē.
examples.english: We often go to that big shopping mall to hang out on weekends.

examples.chinese: 我在淘宝商城买了很多东西。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài Táo bǎo shāng chéng mǎi le hěn duō dōng xi.
examples.english: I bought a lot of things on Taobao Mall.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly refers to both physical shopping malls and large online shopping platforms (e.g., 天猫商城).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Sounds like 'sha' — short for '什么'.
vocabulary.etymology: A colloquial character, common in northern dialects. Likely a contraction of 什么.

examples.chinese: 你刚才说啥？我没听清。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ gāng cái shuō shá? Wǒ méi tīng qīng.
examples.english: What did you just say? I didn't hear clearly.

examples.chinese: 这有啥好奇怪的？
examples.pinyin: Zhè yǒu shá hǎo qí guài de?
examples.english: What's so strange about this?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Extremely casual and common in spoken Mandarin, especially in the north. Direct replacement for '什么' in questions.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of being at a dead end (只) and finally having to (得) turn back. You have to do it.
vocabulary.etymology: 只 (only, merely) + 得 (must, have to). Combined meaning of 'only can do this'.

examples.chinese: 公交车没了，我只得走回家。
examples.pinyin: Gōngjiāo chē méi le, wǒ zhǐ dé zǒu huí jiā.
examples.english: The bus was gone, so I had no choice but to walk home.

examples.chinese: 他没接电话，我只得给他留言。
examples.pinyin: Tā méi jiē diànhuà, wǒ zhǐ dé gěi tā liú yán.
examples.english: He didn't answer the phone, so I had no choice but to leave him a message.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Emphasizes a lack of alternatives. Similar to 只好 but slightly more formal in feeling.

vocabulary.english: just go ahead and; feel free to
vocabulary.mnemonic: Picture a manager saying "只管去做!" — you only need to manage (管) this one thing, don't worry about the rest.
vocabulary.etymology: 只 (only) + 管 (to manage, to be in charge). Combined sense of 'just take charge (of doing it)'.

examples.chinese: 你只管吃，碗我来洗。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhǐ guǎn chī, wǎn wǒ lái xǐ.
examples.english: You just go ahead and eat, I'll wash the dishes.

examples.chinese: 有什么问题只管问我。
examples.pinyin: Yǒu shénme wèntí zhǐ guǎn wèn wǒ.
examples.english: If you have any questions, feel free to ask me.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used to encourage someone to do something without hesitation or worry. Similar to 尽管, but 只管 is more about action.

vocabulary.english: be absorbed in; only care about
vocabulary.mnemonic: You're so focused, you only (只) care (顾) about one thing, like staring at your phone.
vocabulary.etymology: 只 (only) + 顾 (to look after, to care for). Means 'to only pay attention to'.

examples.chinese: 他顾着玩游戏，都忘了吃饭。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhǐ gù zhe wán yóuxì, dōu wàng le chī fàn.
examples.english: He was so absorbed in playing games that he forgot to eat.

examples.chinese: 别只顾自己，也想想别人。
examples.pinyin: Bié zhǐ gù zìjǐ, yě xiǎng xiǎng biérén.
examples.english: Don't only care about yourself, think about others too.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often has a slightly negative connotation of neglecting other things or people.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It's a lamp (灯) that sits on your desk or table (台).
vocabulary.etymology: 台 (platform, table) + 灯 (lamp). A lamp for a table or desk.

examples.chinese: 晚上看书，我喜欢开那盏小台灯。
examples.pinyin: Wǎnshang kànshū, wǒ xǐhuan kāi nà zhǎn xiǎo táidēng.
examples.english: When I read at night, I like to turn on that small desk lamp.

examples.chinese: 我新买了一个可以调光的台灯。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xīn mǎi le yī gè kěyǐ tiáo guāng de táidēng.
examples.english: I just bought a new desk lamp with adjustable brightness.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very common household item. Note: In Taiwan, the traditional form 檯燈 emphasizes the 'table' meaning.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The person in charge (长) of a government department or '司'.
vocabulary.etymology: 司 (to administer, department) + 长 (chief, head). The head of an administrative department.

examples.chinese: 教育部的那位司长很年轻。
examples.pinyin: Jiàoyù bù de nà wèi sīzhǎng hěn niánqīng.
examples.english: The director-general of that department in the Ministry of Education is very young.

examples.chinese: 这个会议由王司长主持。
examples.pinyin: Zhège huìyì yóu Wáng sīzhǎng zhǔchí.
examples.english: This meeting is chaired by Director-General Wang.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A specific government/bureaucratic title. Not used in casual settings to refer to just any 'boss'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: You exhale air (气) with a sound to express that you're tired, sad, or annoyed. You 'sigh'.
vocabulary.etymology: 叹 (to sigh, to exclaim) + 气 (air, breath). The act of emitting a sighing breath.

examples.chinese: 他看到成绩单，深深地叹了一口气。
examples.pinyin: Tā kàn dào chéngjī dān, shēn shēn de tàn le yī kǒu qì.
examples.english: He looked at his report card and let out a deep sigh.

examples.chinese: 别老叹气了，问题总能解决的。
examples.pinyin: Bié lǎo tànqì le, wèntí zǒng néng jiějué de.
examples.english: Stop sighing all the time, the problem can always be solved.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very common verb-object compound. Can be separated: 叹了一口气.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine a meeting where each (各) person stretches out (抒) their own (己) view (见).
vocabulary.etymology: 各 (each) + 抒 (to express) + 己 (self) + 见 (view, opinion). Literally 'each expresses self's view'.

examples.chinese: 讨论会上，大家各抒己见，气氛很热烈。
examples.pinyin: Tǎolùn huì shàng, dàjiā gè shū jǐ jiàn, qìfēn hěn rèliè.
examples.english: At the discussion, everyone expressed their own opinions, and the atmosphere was very lively.

examples.chinese: 这个问题没有标准答案，欢迎各抒己见。
examples.pinyin: Zhège wèntí méiyǒu biāozhǔn dá'àn, huānyíng gè shū jǐ jiàn.
examples.english: There's no standard answer to this question; everyone is welcome to express their own views.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A formal idiom used to describe a free exchange of ideas, often in meetings or debates.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The numbers add up (算) and come together (合) in your favor — it's a good deal!
vocabulary.etymology: 合 (to combine, to suit) + 算 (to calculate). A calculation that comes out favorably.

examples.chinese: 买三送一，太合算了！
examples.pinyin: Mǎi sān sòng yī, tài hésuàn le!
examples.english: Buy three, get one free — such a good deal!

examples.chinese: 跑这么远就为吃碗面，不合算。
examples.pinyin: Pǎo zhème yuǎn jiù wèi chī wǎn miàn, bù hésuàn.
examples.english: It's not worth it to go so far just for a bowl of noodles.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very common when shopping or evaluating if an effort is worth the reward. Similar to 划算.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A document that brings parties together (合) in an agreement (约).
vocabulary.etymology: 合 (to combine, to agree) + 约 (agreement, appointment). A joint agreement.

examples.chinese: 签工作合约之前，一定要仔细看条款。
examples.pinyin: Qiān gōngzuò héyuē zhīqián, yīdìng yào zǐxì kàn tiáokuǎn.
examples.english: Before signing an employment contract, you must read the terms carefully.

examples.chinese: 我们的租房合约下个月到期。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de zūfáng héyuē xià gè yuè dàoqī.
examples.english: Our rental contract expires next month.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Slightly more formal than 合同, but they are largely interchangeable in modern usage.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Clothes that suit (合) your body (身) perfectly.
vocabulary.etymology: 合 (to suit, to fit) + 身 (body). Fitting the body.

examples.chinese: 这件衬衫你穿起来很合身。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn chènshān nǐ chuān qǐlai hěn héshēn.
examples.english: This shirt fits you very well.

examples.chinese: 裤子有点长，不太合身。
examples.pinyin: Kùzi yǒudiǎn cháng, bú tài héshēn.
examples.english: The pants are a bit long; they don't fit very well.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used exclusively for clothing. Its opposite is 不合身.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Sounds like 'Gee, lucky!' Something that brings good fortune.
vocabulary.etymology: 吉 (lucky, auspicious) + 利 (benefit, sharp). Combined to mean 'auspicious and beneficial'.

examples.chinese: 红色在中国文化里是吉利的颜色。
examples.pinyin: Hóngsè zài Zhōngguó wénhuà lǐ shì jílì de yánsè.
examples.english: Red is an auspicious color in Chinese culture.

examples.chinese: 说点吉利的话，别老提倒霉事。
examples.pinyin: Shuō diǎn jílì de huà, bié lǎo tí dǎoméi shì.
examples.english: Say something auspicious, don't keep mentioning unlucky things.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often refers to words, colors, dates, or objects believed to bring good luck, especially during festivals or important events.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'xiáng' sounds like '祥', which is the same character used in '吉祥' — often seen in blessings and New Year decorations.
vocabulary.etymology: 吉 (lucky) + 祥 (propitious, auspicious). A double-character term reinforcing the meaning of good fortune.

examples.chinese: 过年的时候，家家户户都贴吉祥的对联。
examples.pinyin: Guònián de shíhou, jiā jiā hù hù dōu tiē jíxiáng de duìlián.
examples.english: During Chinese New Year, every household pastes auspicious couplets.

examples.chinese: 祝你吉祥如意！
examples.pinyin: Zhù nǐ jíxiáng rúyì!
examples.english: I wish you good fortune and happiness!

vocabulary.usage_notes: Slightly more formal and literary than 吉利. Often used in fixed phrases like 吉祥物 (mascot) or 吉祥如意.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Picture something hanging from a hook — the character even looks like a rope with a weight on it.
vocabulary.etymology: Pictograph origin, depicting a rope with something attached, meaning to hang or suspend.

examples.chinese: 把衣服吊在衣柜里。
examples.pinyin: Bǎ yīfu diào zài yīguì lǐ.
examples.english: Hang the clothes in the wardrobe.

examples.chinese: 工人们正在吊装空调外机。
examples.pinyin: Gōngrénmen zhèngzài diàozhuāng kōngtiáo wàijī.
examples.english: The workers are hoisting and installing the outdoor AC unit.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very common verb for hanging objects. Also used in compounds like 吊车 (crane), 吊死 (to hang oneself).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of two people under one roof (the character's shape) — they are the 'same' or 'together'.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted a mouth (口) speaking through a tube, conveying the idea of 'together' or 'same'. Simplified form retains the core shape.

examples.chinese: 我们同一年毕业。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen tóng yī nián bìyè.
examples.english: We graduated in the same year.

examples.chinese: 我同他一起去。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ tóng tā yīqǐ qù.
examples.english: I'll go with him.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Extremely common. As a preposition meaning 'with', it's more formal/written than 跟 or 和 in spoken Mandarin.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It's the 'same one' — 同 (same) + 一 (one).
vocabulary.etymology: 同 (same) + 一 (one). Literally 'same one'.

examples.chinese: 他们俩来自同一个城市。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen liǎ láizì tóng yī gè chéngshì.
examples.english: They are both from the same city.

examples.chinese: 这不是同一回事。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bú shì tóng yī huí shì.
examples.english: This is not the same matter.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Emphasizes singularity and sameness. Often followed by a measure word + noun.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'same period' on a calendar — 同 (same) + 期 (period).
vocabulary.etymology: 同 (same) + 期 (period, term).

examples.chinese: 今年三月的销量比去年同期增长了10%。
examples.pinyin: Jīnnián sān yuè de xiāoliàng bǐ qùnián tóngqī zēngzhǎng le 10%.
examples.english: Sales this March increased by 10% compared to the same period last year.

examples.chinese: 我们是大学同期的毕业生。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen shì dàxué tóngqī de bìyè shēng.
examples.english: We are graduates from the same university cohort.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common in business, economics, and academic contexts for period-to-period comparisons.

vocabulary.mnemonic: People from the same womb (胞) — either literally siblings or figuratively fellow citizens.
vocabulary.etymology: 同 (same) + 胞 (womb, placenta). Literally 'from the same womb'.

examples.chinese: 港澳同胞回乡证
examples.pinyin: Gǎng Ào tóngbāo huíxiāng zhèng
examples.english: Home Visit Permit for Hong Kong and Macao Compatriots

examples.chinese: 他们是亲同胞，长得特别像。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen shì qīn tóngbāo, zhǎng dé tèbié xiàng.
examples.english: They are biological siblings and look very much alike.

vocabulary.usage_notes: In political/social contexts, it emphasizes shared Chinese heritage. In family contexts, it's a formal term for siblings.

vocabulary.mnemonic: People walking the same (同) path or line of work (行).
vocabulary.etymology: 同 (same) + 行 (line, profession; to walk). The meaning changes with pronunciation: tóngháng (same trade) vs tóngxíng (to travel together).

examples.chinese: 他在一次行业会议上遇到了几位同行。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yī cì hángyè huìyì shàng yù dào le jǐ wèi tóngháng.
examples.english: He met several people from the same profession at an industry conference.

examples.chinese: 明天我将与他同行去上海。
examples.pinyin: Míngtiān wǒ jiāng yǔ tā tóngxíng qù Shànghǎi.
examples.english: Tomorrow I will travel to Shanghai with him.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Crucially has two pronunciations/meanings: tóngháng (noun: colleague in the same field), tóngxíng (verb: to travel together).

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'name' (名) and 'meaning' (义) you use to label something or someone.
vocabulary.etymology: 名 (name, fame) + 义 (meaning, righteousness). The name and justification for something.

examples.chinese: 他以个人名义捐了一笔钱。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǐ gèrén míngyì juān le yī bǐ qián.
examples.english: He donated a sum of money in his personal name.

examples.chinese: 他只是公司的名义负责人，不管具体事务。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhǐ shì gōngsī de míngyì fùzérén, bù guǎn jùtǐ shìwù.
examples.english: He is only the nominal head of the company and doesn't handle specific affairs.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in phrases like 以...名义 (in the name of...) or 名义上 (nominally, in name only).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Your 'name' (名) in the 'order' (次) — like on a results list.
vocabulary.etymology: 名 (name) + 次 (order, sequence). The order of names in a list.

examples.chinese: 他这次考试的名次提高了很多。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhè cì kǎoshì de míngcì tígāo le hěnduō.
examples.english: His ranking improved a lot in this exam.

examples.chinese: 比赛很激烈，名次随时可能变化。
examples.pinyin: Bǐsài hěn jīliè, míngcì suíshí kěnéng biànhuà.
examples.english: The competition is intense; the placings could change at any time.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for contests, exams, sports — any situation with a ranked list.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A place famous (名) for its beautiful scenery that wins (胜) everyone's admiration.
vocabulary.etymology: 名 (famous) + 胜 (scenic spot, victory). A famous scenic site.

examples.chinese: 杭州有很多名胜古迹。
examples.pinyin: Hángzhōu yǒu hěnduō míngshèng gǔjī.
examples.english: Hangzhou has many famous scenic spots and historical sites.

examples.chinese: 来北京一定要去那些著名的名胜看看。
examples.pinyin: Lái Běijīng yīdìng yào qù nàxiē zhùmíng de míngshèng kàn kan.
examples.english: When you come to Beijing, you must visit those famous scenic spots.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Almost always used in the compound 名胜古迹 (famous scenic spots and historical sites).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Your 'name' (名) and the 'praise' (誉) people give it — that's your reputation.
vocabulary.etymology: 名 (name, fame) + 誉 (praise, reputation). The praise associated with one's name.

examples.chinese: 他是一位名誉很好的教授。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yī wèi míngyù hěn hǎo de jiàoshòu.
examples.english: He is a professor with a very good reputation.

examples.chinese: 公司很注重自己的名誉。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī hěn zhùzhòng zìjǐ de míngyù.
examples.english: The company places great importance on its reputation.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be positive or negative (名誉扫地 — to have one's reputation ruined). Also used in titles like 名誉主席 (honorary chairman).

vocabulary.mnemonic: The fixed number of 'names' (名) that can fill the available slots (额).
vocabulary.etymology: 名 (name) + 额 (quota, forehead). The quota of names/people.

examples.chinese: 这个培训班只有三十个名额，报满为止。
examples.pinyin: Zhège péixùn bān zhǐ yǒu sānshí gè míng'é, bào mǎn wéizhǐ.
examples.english: This training course only has thirty places, first come first served.

examples.chinese: 我们公司今年招聘名额增加了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen gōngsī jīnnián zhāopìn míng'é zēngjiā le.
examples.english: Our company's hiring quota has increased this year.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for limits in admissions, jobs, competitions, events, etc.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A person who 'gives'吝 (lin) 'color' 啬 (se)? No, they're so stingy they won't even give you the right colors!
vocabulary.etymology: Both characters individually carry meanings related to regret, grudge, or miserliness, combining to intensify the meaning.

examples.chinese: 他对朋友特别吝啬，从不请客。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì péngyou tèbié lìnsè, cóng bù qǐngkè.
examples.english: He's very stingy with his friends and never treats them.

examples.chinese: 别那么吝啬，分享一点你的零食嘛。
examples.pinyin: Bié nàme lìnsè, fēnxiǎng yīdiǎn nǐ de língshí ma.
examples.english: Don't be so stingy, share some of your snacks.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Stronger and more negative than 小气. Describes someone who is unwilling to spend money or share resources.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The character looks like a big mouth (口) with something going down into a stomach. You swallow it whole.
vocabulary.etymology: Pictophonetic: 口 (mouth) suggests meaning, 天 (tiān) suggests sound in ancient times. The idea is putting something from the mouth to the stomach.

examples.chinese: 吃药片要用水吞下去。
examples.pinyin: Chī yào piàn yào yòng shuǐ tūn xiàqù.
examples.english: You need water to swallow the pill.

examples.chinese: 大公司吞并了好几家小公司。
examples.pinyin: Dà gōngsī tūnbìng le hǎo jǐ jiā xiǎo gōngsī.
examples.english: The big company swallowed up/merged several small companies.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be literal (swallow food) or figurative (a big company swallows a smaller one).

vocabulary.mnemonic: When you're 'done' and just want to add a friendly 'la' at the end.
vocabulary.etymology: A phonetic loan character used to represent the colloquial final particle sound.

examples.chinese: 我来啦！
examples.pinyin: Wǒ lái lā!
examples.english: I'm coming/I'm here!

examples.chinese: 天气真好啦。
examples.pinyin: Tiānqì zhēn hǎo lā.
examples.english: The weather is really nice (isn't it).

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in place of or combined with '了 (le)' to sound more casual and emotional.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine a 'loud speaker' (啰) that won't stop 'talking' (唆).
vocabulary.etymology: Repetition of characters for 'talk' or 'voice', emphasizing excessive speech.

examples.chinese: 他讲话太啰唆了。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiǎnghuà tài luōsuo le.
examples.english: He talks way too much / is so long-winded.

examples.chinese: 别啰唆了，赶紧走吧。
examples.pinyin: Bié luōsuo le, gǎnjǐn zǒu ba.
examples.english: Stop nagging, let's go quickly.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used to complain about someone being verbose or nagging.

vocabulary.english: to gasp; to catch one's breath
vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of 'mouth' (口 in 喘) and 'air' (气) — your mouth gasping for air.
vocabulary.etymology: 喘 (breathe heavily) + 气 (air/breath).

examples.chinese: 让我先喘口气。
examples.pinyin: Ràng wǒ xiān chuǎn kǒu qì.
examples.english: Let me catch my breath first.

examples.chinese: 他跑得喘不过气来。
examples.pinyin: Tā pǎo de chuǎn bú guò qì lái.
examples.english: He ran so fast he couldn't catch his breath.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used after physical exertion.

vocabulary.english: loved to see and hear; widely popular
vocabulary.mnemonic: Something you're HAPPY to HEAR and LOVE to SEE.
vocabulary.etymology: 喜 (delight) + 闻 (hear) + 乐 (love) + 见 (see). A four-character idiom.

examples.chinese: 春节晚会是大家喜闻乐见的节目。
examples.pinyin: Chūnjié wǎnhuì shì dàjiā xǐ wén lè jiàn de jiémù.
examples.english: The Spring Festival Gala is a show everyone loves to watch.

examples.chinese: 这种正能量的故事，老百姓都喜闻乐见。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng zhèng néngliàng de gùshì, lǎobǎixìng dōu xǐ wén lè jiàn.
examples.english: This kind of uplifting story is something ordinary people love to see.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Describes things that are widely welcomed and appreciated by the public.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Sounds exactly like the English 'hi'.
vocabulary.etymology: A phonetic loan character for the casual greeting sound.

examples.chinese: 嗨，好久不见！
examples.pinyin: Hāi, hǎojiǔ bú jiàn!
examples.english: Hey, long time no see!

examples.chinese: 嗨，大家玩得开心吗？
examples.pinyin: Hāi, dàjiā wán de kāixīn ma?
examples.english: Hey everyone, having fun?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very casual greeting, common among younger people and influenced by English.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The sound you make when you're thinking ('en' with your mouth closed).
vocabulary.etymology: A phonetic character representing a nasal sound of agreement, thought, or acknowledgment.

examples.chinese: 嗯，我觉得可以。
examples.pinyin: Ēn, wǒ juéde kěyǐ.
examples.english: Mm-hmm, I think that's okay.

examples.chinese: 嗯... 让我想一想。
examples.pinyin: Ēn... ràng wǒ xiǎng yī xiǎng.
examples.english: Hmm... let me think about it.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Tone changes meaning: first tone (ēn) for thinking, second tone (én) for questioning, fourth tone (èn) for agreement/acknowledgment.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Sounds like '吵 (chǎo)杂' — a mix of '吵' (noisy) and '杂' (miscellaneous) noise.
vocabulary.etymology: 嘈 (noise of many voices) + 杂 (mixed, miscellaneous).

examples.chinese: 早上的菜市场很嘈杂。
examples.pinyin: Zǎoshang de cài shìchǎng hěn cáozá.
examples.english: The morning vegetable market is very noisy.

examples.chinese: 这里太嘈杂了，我听不见你说话。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ tài cáozá le, wǒ tīng bú jiàn nǐ shuōhuà.
examples.english: It's too noisy here, I can't hear you.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Describes an unpleasant, chaotic mix of sounds, not just loudness.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine a 'plus' (嘉 has a 加) 'guest' (宾) — an extra special guest.
vocabulary.etymology: 嘉 (fine, good) + 宾 (guest).

examples.chinese: 今天我们请来了几位特别的嘉宾。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān wǒmen qǐng lái le jǐ wèi tèbié de jiābīn.
examples.english: Today we've invited some special guests.

examples.chinese: 有请颁奖嘉宾上台！
examples.pinyin: Yǒu qǐng bānjiǎng jiābīn shàng tái!
examples.english: Let's welcome the awards presenter to the stage!

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used for guests on TV shows, ceremonies, weddings, etc.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Adds a 'ma' that says 'it's obvious, duh'.
vocabulary.etymology: A phonetic character used as a modal particle.

examples.chinese: 这很简单嘛。
examples.pinyin: Zhè hěn jiǎndān má.
examples.english: This is simple (obviously).

examples.chinese: 想去就去嘛。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎng qù jiù qù má.
examples.english: If you want to go, just go (what's stopping you?).

vocabulary.usage_notes: Softens a statement, implies something is obvious or reasonable, often used persuasively.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of the FOUR (四) DIRECTIONS (处) — covering all places.
vocabulary.etymology: 四 (four) + 处 (place). Literally 'four places', meaning all directions/places.

examples.chinese: 小狗在公园里四处乱跑。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo gǒu zài gōngyuán lǐ sìchù luàn pǎo.
examples.english: The puppy is running around everywhere in the park.

examples.chinese: 我四处看了看，没找到他。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ sìchù kàn le kàn, méi zhǎodào tā.
examples.english: I looked all around but didn't find him.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Similar to '到处 (dàochù)', often used with verbs of movement or looking.

vocabulary.english: the four limbs; arms and legs
vocabulary.mnemonic: FOUR (四) LIMBS (肢).
vocabulary.etymology: 四 (four) + 肢 (limb).

examples.chinese: 做完运动，我的四肢都酸了。
examples.pinyin: Zuò wán yùndòng, wǒ de sìzhī dōu suān le.
examples.english: After exercising, all my limbs are sore.

examples.chinese: 他四肢发达，头脑简单。
examples.pinyin: Tā sìzhī fādá, tóunǎo jiǎndān.
examples.english: He's brawny but not very bright. (idiom: all brawn, no brains)

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers collectively to both arms and legs.

vocabulary.mnemonic: You 'return' (回) an 'answer' (应).
vocabulary.etymology: 回 (return) + 应 (answer, respond).

examples.chinese: 他发了消息，但我还没回应。
examples.pinyin: Tā fā le xiāoxi, dàn wǒ hái méi huíyìng.
examples.english: He sent a message, but I haven't responded yet.

examples.chinese: 大家对这件事的回应很热烈。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā duì zhè jiàn shì de huíyìng hěn rèliè.
examples.english: The public's response to this matter has been very enthusiastic.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be a verbal or non-verbal reaction to something.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'reason' is 'inside' (囗) the 'big' (大) situation.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted a mat or cushion one depends/sits on,引申为原因.

examples.chinese: 因天气原因，比赛取消了。
examples.pinyin: Yīn tiānqì yuányīn, bǐsài qǔxiāo le.
examples.english: Because of the weather, the match was cancelled.

examples.chinese: 事出有因。
examples.pinyin: Shì chū yǒu yīn.
examples.english: There's a reason for everything happening. (idiom)

vocabulary.usage_notes: More formal/written than '因为'. Often seen in fixed phrases or formal writing.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'cause' (因) and 'prime' (素) ingredients.
vocabulary.etymology: 因 (cause) + 素 (basic element).

measure_word.example: 一个重要因素 (yī gè zhòngyào yīnsù)

examples.chinese: 价格是影响决定的一个重要因素。
examples.pinyin: Jiàgé shì yǐngxiǎng juédìng de yī gè zhòngyào yīnsù.
examples.english: Price is an important factor influencing the decision.

examples.chinese: 成功有很多因素。
examples.pinyin: Chénggōng yǒu hěnduō yīnsù.
examples.english: Success depends on many factors.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A neutral term for any contributing element in a situation.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A 'group' (团) that 'pairs up' (队).
vocabulary.etymology: 团 (group, circle) + 队 (line, team).

examples.chinese: 我们有一个很棒的工作团队。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yǒu yī gè hěn bàng de gōngzuò tuánduì.
examples.english: We have a great work team.

examples.chinese: 团队合作很重要。
examples.pinyin: Tuánduì hézuò hěn zhòngyào.
examples.english: Teamwork is very important.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used in work, sports, and project contexts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A 'walled' (囗) place with 'trees' (元) — a garden.
vocabulary.etymology: 囗 (enclosure) + 袁 (old form, contributed sound, later simplified to 元). Originally an enclosed area for growing plants/trees.

examples.chinese: 我家后面有一个小菜园。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā hòumiàn yǒu yī gè xiǎo càiyuán.
examples.english: There's a small vegetable garden behind my house.

examples.chinese: 这个植物园很漂亮。
examples.pinyin: Zhège zhíwùyuán hěn piàoliang.
examples.english: This botanical garden is very beautiful.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used as part of compound words for specific types of gardens/parks.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A 'garden' (园) 'plot of land' (地) for growing things.
vocabulary.etymology: 园 (garden) + 地 (land).

examples.chinese: 我们在郊区租了一块园地种菜。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài jiāoqū zū le yī kuài yuándì zhòng cài.
examples.english: We rented a garden plot in the suburbs to grow vegetables.

examples.chinese: 这个网站是文学爱好者的园地。
examples.pinyin: Zhège wǎngzhàn shì wénxué àihào zhě de yuándì.
examples.english: This website is a forum for literature lovers.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be literal (garden) or metaphorical (a field for activities, e.g., '读者园地' Reader's Corner).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Something 'solidified' (固) and 'already has' (有) it.
vocabulary.etymology: 固 (solid, fixed) + 有 (to have).

examples.chinese: 每个人都有固有的习惯。
examples.pinyin: Měi gè rén dōu yǒu gùyǒu de xíguàn.
examples.english: Everyone has inherent habits.

examples.chinese: 这是文化固有的特点。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wénhuà gùyǒu de tèdiǎn.
examples.english: This is an intrinsic characteristic of the culture.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Describes qualities that are built-in, natural, and not acquired.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Our COUNTRY (国) PRODUCED (产) it.
vocabulary.etymology: 国 (country) + 产 (produce).

examples.chinese: 我买的这辆车是国产的。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi de zhè liàng chē shì guóchǎn de.
examples.english: The car I bought is domestically produced.

examples.chinese: 现在很多国产电影很好看。
examples.pinyin: Xiànzài hěnduō guóchǎn diànyǐng hěn hǎokàn.
examples.english: Nowadays many domestically produced movies are great.

vocabulary.usage_notes: In a Chinese context, often specifically means 'Made in China'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The COUNTRY's (国) MEETING (会) — the big meeting for the country.
vocabulary.etymology: 国 (country, state) + 会 (meeting, assembly).

examples.chinese: 美国国会通过了新的法案。
examples.pinyin: Měiguó Guóhuì tōngguò le xīn de fǎ'àn.
examples.english: The U.S. Congress passed the new bill.

examples.chinese: 国会大厦前有很多人。
examples.pinyin: Guóhuì Dàshà qián yǒu hěnduō rén.
examples.english: There are many people in front of the Capitol building.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Usually refers to the legislative body of a foreign country (e.g., US Congress). For China's legislature, '全国人民代表大会' is used.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The COUNTRY's (国) AFFAIRS (务) COURT/YARD (院).
vocabulary.etymology: 国 (state) + 务 (affairs) + 院 (courtyard, institution).

examples.chinese: 中国的国务院总理发表了讲话。
examples.pinyin: Zhōngguó de Guówùyuàn Zǒnglǐ fābiǎo le jiǎnghuà.
examples.english: The Premier of China's State Council gave a speech.

examples.chinese: 美国国务院发布了旅行警告。
examples.pinyin: Měiguó Guówùyuàn fābù le lǚxíng jǐnggào.
examples.english: The U.S. State Department issued a travel warning.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Context determines meaning: In China, it's the chief administrative authority. In US context, it's the Department of State.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The COUNTRY's (国) BANNER/FLAG (旗).
vocabulary.etymology: 国 (country) + 旗 (flag, banner).

examples.chinese: 每天早上学校都会升国旗。
examples.pinyin: Měitiān zǎoshang xuéxiào dōu huì shēng guóqí.
examples.english: Every morning the school raises the national flag.

examples.chinese: 奥运会上，运动员们举着国旗入场。
examples.pinyin: Àoyùnhuì shàng, yùndòngyuán men jǔ zhe guóqí rùchǎng.
examples.english: At the Olympics, athletes enter the stadium carrying their national flags.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The COUNTRY's (国) SONG (歌).
vocabulary.etymology: 国 (country) + 歌 (song).

examples.chinese: 比赛开始前要奏国歌。
examples.pinyin: Bǐsài kāishǐ qián yào zòu guógē.
examples.english: The national anthem is played before the match begins.

examples.chinese: 你会唱中国国歌吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ huì chàng Zhōngguó guógē ma?
examples.english: Can you sing the Chinese national anthem?

vocabulary.mnemonic: The COUNTRY's (国) RULER (王).
vocabulary.etymology: 国 (country, kingdom) + 王 (king).

examples.chinese: 很久以前，这个国家有一位善良的国王。
examples.pinyin: Hěn jiǔ yǐqián, zhège guójiā yǒu yī wèi shànliáng de guówáng.
examples.english: A long time ago, this country had a kind king.

examples.chinese: 英国国王发表了电视讲话。
examples.pinyin: Yīngguó guówáng fābiǎo le diànshì jiǎnghuà.
examples.english: The King of the United Kingdom gave a televised speech.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of 'diagrams/charts' (图) and 'writings' (书) — books!
vocabulary.etymology: 图 (diagram, picture) + 书 (book, writing).

examples.chinese: 学校图书馆有很多儿童图书。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào túshūguǎn yǒu hěnduō értóng túshū.
examples.english: The school library has many children's books.

examples.chinese: 这是一家专门卖图书的网站。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yī jiā zhuānmén mài túshū de wǎngzhàn.
examples.english: This is a website specializing in selling books.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used as a collective noun or in compounds like '图书馆 (library)', '图书管理员 (librarian)'. More formal than just '书'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: If it's 'da bu liao' (big-not-over), it's not a big deal! It's a shrug in word form.
vocabulary.etymology: Literally 'big' + 'not' + 'to finish/end'. Means something is not beyond a big, but manageable, scope.

examples.chinese: 别担心，大不了我们明天再去一次。
examples.pinyin: Bié dān xīn, dà bù liǎo wǒ men míng tiān zài qù yī cì.
examples.english: Don't worry, at worst we'll go again tomorrow.

examples.chinese: 这没什么大不了的，别放在心上。
examples.pinyin: Zhè méi shén me dà bù liǎo de, bié fàng zài xīn shàng.
examples.english: It's nothing serious, don't take it to heart.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used to downplay a problem's significance. Can be used alone as '没什么大不了的'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'Big Envoy' (大使 - big + envoy) who represents a country.
vocabulary.etymology: 大 (big/great) + 使 (envoy/messenger). An envoy of high rank.

examples.chinese: 中国大使出席了那场活动。
examples.pinyin: Zhōng guó dà shǐ chū xí le nà chǎng huó dòng.
examples.english: The Chinese ambassador attended that event.

examples.chinese: 他是驻法国的大使。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì zhù Fǎ guó de dà shǐ.
examples.english: He is the ambassador to France.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Use 'great strength' (大力) to push something forward vigorously.
vocabulary.etymology: 大 (big/great) + 力 (strength/force). Means great strength, used adverbially.

examples.chinese: 公司会大力支持这个新项目。
examples.pinyin: Gōng sī huì dà lì zhī chí zhè ge xīn xiàng mù.
examples.english: The company will vigorously support this new project.

examples.chinese: 我们要大力发展教育。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men yào dà lì fā zhǎn jiào yù.
examples.english: We must vigorously develop education.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used before verbs like '支持', '发展', '推广'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A 'Great Teacher' (大师) who is at the top of their field.
vocabulary.etymology: 大 (big/great) + 师 (teacher/master). A teacher of the highest level.

examples.chinese: 他是一位书法大师。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yī wèi shū fǎ dà shī.
examples.english: He is a calligraphy master.

examples.chinese: 这位大师的厨艺非常了不起。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi dà shī de chú yì fēi cháng liǎo bù qǐ.
examples.english: This master chef's culinary skills are amazing.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for fields like art, music, martial arts, crafts, etc.

vocabulary.english: large quantities of / large numbers of
vocabulary.mnemonic: A 'big batch' (大批) of something arriving all at once.
vocabulary.etymology: 大 (big) + 批 (batch/lot). A large batch.

examples.chinese: 今天超市来了大批新鲜水果。
examples.pinyin: Jīn tiān chāo shì lái le dà pī xīn xiān shuǐ guǒ.
examples.english: A large quantity of fresh fruit arrived at the supermarket today.

examples.chinese: 大批游客涌入了那个小镇。
examples.pinyin: Dà pī yóu kè yǒng rù le nà ge xiǎo zhèn.
examples.english: Large numbers of tourists flooded into that small town.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Usually modifies nouns like 商品, 货物, 人员, 游客.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'big rice' (大米) grains you eat as a staple food.
vocabulary.etymology: 大 (big) + 米 (rice/grain). Refers to the husked, edible rice grains, as opposed to 小米 (millet).

examples.chinese: 这袋大米有十公斤。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dài dà mǐ yǒu shí gōng jīn.
examples.english: This bag of rice weighs ten kilograms.

examples.chinese: 我们家最喜欢吃东北大米。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men jiā zuì xǐ huān chī dōng běi dà mǐ.
examples.english: Our family likes to eat Northeast China rice the most.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to uncooked rice. Cooked rice is 米饭.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'big street' (大街) where all the shops and people are.
vocabulary.etymology: 大 (big) + 街 (street). A major, wide street.

examples.chinese: 我家就在那条大街的旁边。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā jiù zài nà tiáo dà jiē de páng biān.
examples.english: My home is right next to that main street.

examples.chinese: 周末的时候，这条大街上很热闹。
examples.pinyin: Zhōu mò de shí hou, zhè tiáo dà jiē shàng hěn rè nào.
examples.english: On weekends, this avenue is very lively.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A 'big contest' (大赛), like the Olympics or a championship.
vocabulary.etymology: 大 (big) + 赛 (competition/match). A large-scale competition.

examples.chinese: 他准备参加全国钢琴大赛。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhǔn bèi cān jiā quán guó gāng qín dà sài.
examples.english: He is preparing to participate in the national piano competition.

examples.chinese: 这场足球大赛吸引了很多观众。
examples.pinyin: Zhè chǎng zú qiú dà sài xī yǐn le hěn duō guān zhòng.
examples.english: This major football tournament attracted a lot of spectators.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Implies the competition is significant in scale or importance.

vocabulary.english: boulevard / main road / the Great Way (philosophy)
vocabulary.mnemonic: A 'big path' (大道) you can drive straight down.
vocabulary.etymology: 大 (big) + 道 (road/path/way). Literally a large road; also a philosophical concept of the supreme principle.

examples.chinese: 沿着这条大道一直走就能到火车站。
examples.pinyin: Yán zhe zhè tiáo dà dào yī zhí zǒu jiù néng dào huǒ chē zhàn.
examples.english: Go straight along this boulevard and you'll reach the train station.

examples.chinese: 他总在思考人生的大道。
examples.pinyin: Tā zǒng zài sī kǎo rén shēng de dà dào.
examples.english: He is always contemplating the great way of life.

vocabulary.usage_notes: In modern speech, it usually refers to a physical wide road. The philosophical use is more literary.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Everything 'under the sky' (天下) is the whole world.
vocabulary.etymology: 天 (sky/heaven) + 下 (under/below). Literally 'under heaven', an ancient Chinese concept for the known world.

examples.chinese: 他想走遍天下，看遍所有的风景。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng zǒu biàn tiān xià, kàn biàn suǒ yǒu de fēng jǐng.
examples.english: He wants to travel all over the world and see all the scenery.

examples.chinese: 天下没有免费的午餐。
examples.pinyin: Tiān xià méi yǒu miǎn fèi de wǔ cān.
examples.english: There's no such thing as a free lunch (in this world).

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in proverbs and set phrases. Implies a vast, all-encompassing scope.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The joy (乐) of heavenly (天) relationships (伦) - the pure happiness of being with family.
vocabulary.etymology: 天伦 (heaven-ordained relationships, i.e., family bonds) + 之 (of) + 乐 (joy/happiness). Happiness derived from family relationships.

examples.chinese: 春节是享受天伦之乐的好时候。
examples.pinyin: Chūn jié shì xiǎng shòu tiān lún zhī lè de hǎo shí hou.
examples.english: Chinese New Year is a good time to enjoy family happiness.

examples.chinese: 退休后，他最大的愿望就是享受天伦之乐。
examples.pinyin: Tuì xiū hòu, tā zuì dà de yuàn wàng jiù shì xiǎng shòu tiān lún zhī lè.
examples.english: After retirement, his biggest wish is to enjoy the pleasures of family life.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A fixed, somewhat literary idiom. Used to describe the deep contentment of family life.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'heavenly hall' (天堂) where angels live.
vocabulary.etymology: 天 (heaven/sky) + 堂 (hall). The hall of heaven.

examples.chinese: 这个地方美得像天堂一样。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge dì fāng měi de xiàng tiān táng yī yàng.
examples.english: This place is as beautiful as paradise.

examples.chinese: 对于爱书的人来说，图书馆就是天堂。
examples.pinyin: Duì yú ài shū de rén lái shuō, tú shū guǎn jiù shì tiān táng.
examples.english: For book lovers, the library is heaven.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can refer to the religious concept or metaphorically to any perfect place.

vocabulary.mnemonic: As it is 'naturally so' (天然), straight from heaven (天) and nature (然).
vocabulary.etymology: 天 (heaven/nature) + 然 (suffix meaning '-ly' or 'so'). Means 'as from/of nature'.

examples.chinese: 这个湖是一个天然游泳池。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge hú shì yī gè tiān rán yóu yǒng chí.
examples.english: This lake is a natural swimming pool.

examples.chinese: 她喜欢用天然的化妆品。
examples.pinyin: Tā xǐ huān yòng tiān rán de huà zhuāng pǐn.
examples.english: She likes to use natural cosmetics.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used to describe things not man-made or processed.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'sun's energy' (太阳能) that powers panels.
vocabulary.etymology: 太阳 (sun) + 能 (energy). Energy from the sun.

examples.chinese: 我们家的热水是用太阳能的。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men jiā de rè shuǐ shì yòng tài yáng néng de.
examples.english: Our household's hot water uses solar energy.

examples.chinese: 太阳能是一种清洁能源。
examples.pinyin: Tài yáng néng shì yī zhǒng qīng jié néng yuán.
examples.english: Solar energy is a type of clean energy.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Your head (头) aches (疼), either literally or because of a problem.
vocabulary.etymology: 头 (head) + 疼 (ache/pain). Literal or metaphorical head pain.

examples.chinese: 我昨晚没睡好，今天有点头疼。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuó wǎn méi shuì hǎo, jīn tiān yǒu diǎn tóu téng.
examples.english: I didn't sleep well last night, I have a bit of a headache today.

examples.chinese: 这个项目真让人头疼。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge xiàng mù zhēn ràng rén tóu téng.
examples.english: This project is really troublesome (a headache).

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can describe a physical condition or a frustrating situation.

vocabulary.english: to mix in / to be mingled with
vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine things being 'pinched and mixed' (夹杂) together.
vocabulary.etymology: 夹 (to press from both sides/clip) + 杂 (miscellaneous/mixed). To clip or press miscellaneous things together.

examples.chinese: 他的普通话里夹杂着一点南方口音。
examples.pinyin: Tā de pǔ tōng huà lǐ jiā zá zhe yī diǎn nán fāng kǒu yīn.
examples.english: His Mandarin is mixed with a bit of a southern accent.

examples.chinese: 雨水里夹杂着冰雹。
examples.pinyin: Yǔ shuǐ lǐ jiā zá zhe bīng báo.
examples.english: The rain was mixed with hail.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for things that are not purely one thing, but have other elements mixed in.

vocabulary.english: to seize / to take by force
vocabulary.mnemonic: A bird (隹， in the traditional form 奪) flying away with something in its claws - it's been seized!
vocabulary.etymology: The simplified form 夺 is derived from the traditional 奪, which combines 大 (big/forceful) with 隹 (bird) and 寸 (hand), suggesting a bird seized by hand, i.e., to seize.

examples.chinese: 他从我手里夺走了那本书。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóng wǒ shǒu lǐ duó zǒu le nà běn shū.
examples.english: He snatched that book from my hand.

examples.chinese: 我们的队伍夺得了第一名。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men de duì wǔ duó dé le dì yī míng.
examples.english: Our team seized first place (won first place).

vocabulary.usage_notes: Implies force, competition, or effort. Often used in sports (夺冠) or conflicts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: To 'seize and take' (夺取) something, like capturing a flag.
vocabulary.etymology: 夺 (to seize) + 取 (to take). To seize and take away.

examples.chinese: 军队成功夺取了那座城市。
examples.pinyin: Jūn duì chéng gōng duó qǔ le nà zuò chéng shì.
examples.english: The army successfully captured that city.

examples.chinese: 他们想方设法夺取市场的领导地位。
examples.pinyin: Tā men xiǎng fāng shè fǎ duó qǔ shì chǎng de lǐng dǎo dì wèi.
examples.english: They tried every way to seize the market leadership position.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Stronger and more formal than just 夺. Often used in military, political, or competitive contexts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Something 'strange and marvelous' (奇妙) that makes you say 'wow'.
vocabulary.etymology: 奇 (strange/rare) + 妙 (wonderful/exquisite). Strange and wonderful.

examples.chinese: 大自然有很多奇妙的现象。
examples.pinyin: Dà zì rán yǒu hěn duō qí miào de xiàn xiàng.
examples.english: Nature has many marvelous phenomena.

examples.chinese: 我觉得魔术表演非常奇妙。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jué de mó shù biǎo yǎn fēi cháng qí miào.
examples.english: I think magic shows are very wonderful.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Describes things that are fascinatingly unusual or beautifully complex.

vocabulary.mnemonic: You 'offer and present' (奉献) your time, effort, or love selflessly.
vocabulary.etymology: 奉 (to offer/to respect) + 献 (to present/to offer). To respectfully offer something.

examples.chinese: 他把一生都奉献给了科学研究。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ yī shēng dōu fèng xiàn gěi le kē xué yán jiū.
examples.english: He dedicated his whole life to scientific research.

examples.chinese: 这种无私的奉献精神值得我们学习。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng wú sī de fèng xiàn jīng shén zhí dé wǒ men xué xí.
examples.english: This kind of selfless dedication is worth learning from.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Has a noble, self-sacrificing connotation. Often used for careers, charity, or love.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Someone 'spreading' (揍 minus 扌) music into the air - they are playing an instrument.
vocabulary.etymology: The character depicts hands (廾, variant of 扌) offering something (本义 uncertain). Evolved to mean 'to present' (奏折) and 'to play music'.

examples.chinese: 他会奏好几种乐器。
examples.pinyin: Tā huì zòu hǎo jǐ zhǒng yuè qì.
examples.english: He can play several kinds of musical instruments.

examples.chinese: 这个方法果然奏效了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge fāng fǎ guǒ rán zòu xiào le.
examples.english: This method actually worked (achieved an effect).

vocabulary.usage_notes: As 'to play', it's often combined with 演 (演奏). As 'to achieve', it's used in 奏效 (to be effective).

vocabulary.mnemonic: To 'run and dash' (奔跑) - the full action of running.
vocabulary.etymology: 奔 (to run quickly) + 跑 (to run). To run swiftly.

examples.chinese: 孩子们在草地上快乐地奔跑。
examples.pinyin: Hái zi men zài cǎo dì shàng kuài lè de bēn pǎo.
examples.english: The children are running happily on the grass.

examples.chinese: 听到这个消息，他奔跑着去找她。
examples.pinyin: Tīng dào zhè ge xiāo xi, tā bēn pǎo zhe qù zhǎo tā.
examples.english: Upon hearing this news, he ran to find her.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Emphasizes the action of running, often with energy or purpose.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A horse 'running and extending' (奔驰) at full speed.
vocabulary.etymology: 奔 (to run quickly) + 驰 (to gallop/speed). To run at high speed.

examples.chinese: 骏马在草原上奔驰。
examples.pinyin: Jùn mǎ zài cǎo yuán shàng bēn chí.
examples.english: The fine horses gallop across the grassland.

examples.chinese: 汽车在高速公路上奔驰。
examples.pinyin: Qì chē zài gāo sù gōng lù shàng bēn chí.
examples.english: The car speeds along the highway.

vocabulary.usage_notes: More poetic and vivid than 奔跑, often used for vehicles or horses moving swiftly. Also the brand name 'Mercedes-Benz'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A 'prize and gift' (奖赏) given as a reward.
vocabulary.etymology: 奖 (prize/award) + 赏 (to bestow/a reward). An award or bestowal.

examples.chinese: 这是他努力工作的奖赏。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì tā nǔ lì gōng zuò de jiǎng shǎng.
examples.english: This is the reward for his hard work.

examples.chinese: 老板奖赏了那个优秀的员工。
examples.pinyin: Lǎo bǎn jiǎng shǎng le nà ge yōu xiù de yuán gōng.
examples.english: The boss rewarded that outstanding employee.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be material or immaterial. Slightly more formal than 奖励.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'milk cow' (奶牛) that gives us milk.
vocabulary.etymology: 奶 (milk) + 牛 (cow/ox). A cow bred for milk production.

examples.chinese: 农场上养了五十头奶牛。
examples.pinyin: Nóng chǎng shàng yǎng le wǔ shí tóu nǎi niú.
examples.english: The farm keeps fifty dairy cows.

examples.chinese: 奶牛每天都要挤两次奶。
examples.pinyin: Nǎi niú měi tiān dōu yào jǐ liǎng cì nǎi.
examples.english: Dairy cows need to be milked twice a day.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Specifically refers to female cattle raised for milk. The milk itself is 牛奶.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It's the pen with a round (圆) tiny bead (珠) at the tip that rolls and writes.
vocabulary.etymology: 圆 (round) + 珠 (bead/ball) + 笔 (pen/writing tool). Literally 'round-bead pen' describing the ball mechanism.

examples.chinese: 能借我你的圆珠笔用一下吗？
examples.pinyin: Néng jiè wǒ nǐ de yuánzhūbǐ yòng yīxià ma?
examples.english: Can I borrow your ballpoint pen for a moment?

examples.chinese: 这种圆珠笔写起来特别顺滑。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng yuánzhūbǐ xiě qǐlái tèbié shùnhuá.
examples.english: This kind of ballpoint pen writes very smoothly.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The standard everyday pen in China. Less formal than a fountain pen (钢笔).

vocabulary.mnemonic: The holy (圣) birth (诞) festival (节)!
vocabulary.etymology: 圣 (holy/saint) + 诞 (birth) + 节 (festival). A direct translation of 'Christmas', the festival celebrating the birth of Jesus Christ.

examples.chinese: 圣诞节你打算怎么过？
examples.pinyin: Shèngdànjié nǐ dǎsuàn zěnme guò?
examples.english: How do you plan to spend Christmas?

examples.chinese: 很多商场圣诞节期间会打折。
examples.pinyin: Hěn duō shāngchǎng Shèngdànjié qījiān huì dǎzhé.
examples.english: Many shopping malls have sales during Christmas.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A major imported festival in China, celebrated more commercially and socially than religiously.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The room (室) that's under (下) the ground (地).
vocabulary.etymology: 地 (ground/earth) + 下 (under/below) + 室 (room). Literally 'ground-below-room'.

examples.chinese: 我们家的地下室堆满了旧东西。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen jiā de dìxiàshì duī mǎn le jiù dōngxi.
examples.english: Our basement is piled full of old stuff.

examples.chinese: 太热了，去地下室凉快会儿吧。
examples.pinyin: Tài rè le, qù dìxiàshì liángkuài huìr ba.
examples.english: It's too hot, let's go cool off in the basement for a bit.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for storage or as a utility space. In cities, some are converted into apartments or shops.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'situation' or 'form' (势) of the land (地).
vocabulary.etymology: 地 (land/ground) + 势 (situation/power/form). The configuration or features of the land's surface.

examples.chinese: 这里地势平坦，适合建房子。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ dìshì píngtǎn, shìhé jiàn fángzi.
examples.english: The terrain here is flat, suitable for building houses.

examples.chinese: 比赛因为地势复杂，难度增加了。
examples.pinyin: Bǐsài yīnwèi dìshì fùzá, nándù zēngjiā le.
examples.english: The race became more difficult because of the complex terrain.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Describes the physical lay of the land, like high, low, flat, or steep.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'name' (名) of a 'place' (地).
vocabulary.etymology: 地 (place/land) + 名 (name). A straightforward compound meaning 'place-name'.

examples.chinese: 这个地名太难记了，我老是忘。
examples.pinyin: Zhège dìmíng tài nán jì le, wǒ lǎo shì wàng.
examples.english: This place name is too hard to remember; I always forget it.

examples.chinese: 很多地名背后都有历史故事。
examples.pinyin: Hěn duō dìmíng bèihòu dōu yǒu lìshǐ gùshì.
examples.english: Many place names have historical stories behind them.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to the name of any geographical location, big or small.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'board' (板) of the 'ground' (地) you walk on.
vocabulary.etymology: 地 (ground/floor) + 板 (board/plank). Originally referred to wooden floor planks, now can mean floor more generally.

examples.chinese: 小心点，地板刚拖过，有点滑。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn diǎn, dìbǎn gāng tuō guò, yǒudiǎn huá.
examples.english: Be careful, the floor was just mopped and is a bit slippery.

examples.chinese: 我想给客厅换新的木地板。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng gěi kètīng huàn xīn de mù dìbǎn.
examples.english: I want to replace the living room with new wooden flooring.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly refers to the finished, indoor walking surface of a room. Can also mean a floor of a building in some contexts (e.g., '一楼地板' for 'first floor'), but 层 is more standard.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A specific 'piece of ground' (地) used as an 'open space' (场).
vocabulary.etymology: 场 (open space/grounds) + 地 (land/ground). Emphasizes the land area designated for a specific activity.

examples.chinese: 我们公司年会租了一个很大的场地。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen gōngsī niánhuì zū le yī gè hěn dà de chǎngdì.
examples.english: Our company rented a very large venue for the annual party.

examples.chinese: 施工场地，闲人免进。
examples.pinyin: Shīgōng chǎngdì, xiánrén miǎn jìn.
examples.english: Construction site, no unauthorized entry.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Focuses on the physical space where an event or activity happens (sports, construction, event).

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'scene' or 'view' (景) of the 'stage' (场).
vocabulary.etymology: 场 (stage/scene) + 景 (view/scenery). A term from drama, now used for any visual setting or situation.

examples.chinese: 电影里那个离别的场景让我哭了。
examples.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ nàgè líbié de chǎngjǐng ràng wǒ kū le.
examples.english: The farewell scene in the movie made me cry.

examples.chinese: 突然下起大雨，街上出现了混乱的场景。
examples.pinyin: Tūrán xià qǐ dàyǔ, jiē shàng chūxiàn le hǔnluàn de chǎngjǐng.
examples.english: It suddenly started pouring, creating a chaotic scene on the street.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for visual, cinematic, or descriptive settings. Can be real or imagined.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'building' (馆) that houses a large 'ground' or 'arena' (场).
vocabulary.etymology: 场 (grounds/arena) + 馆 (building/hall). A compound referring to a building or complex designed for events.

examples.chinese: 演唱会的场馆能容纳两万人。
examples.pinyin: Yǎnchànghuì de chǎngguǎn néng róngnà liǎng wàn rén.
examples.english: The concert venue can hold twenty thousand people.

examples.chinese: 奥运会的主场馆非常壮观。
examples.pinyin: Àoyùnhuì de zhǔ chǎngguǎn fēicháng zhuàngguān.
examples.english: The main stadium for the Olympics is spectacular.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers specifically to a building or indoor facility used for sports, exhibitions, concerts, etc. More formal and specific than '场地'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It's the part of the earth (土) that's worn (皮) into an incline! Think of dirt (土) sliding down a slippery skin (皮) of a hill.
vocabulary.etymology: Composed of 土 (earth/soil) and 皮 (skin). Its origin is not definitively agreed upon; one theory suggests a slope's surface is like the 'skin' of the earth.

examples.chinese: 前面有个大坡，骑车得用点力。
examples.pinyin: Qiánmiàn yǒu gè dà pō, qíchē děi yòng diǎn lì.
examples.english: There's a big slope ahead; you'll need to pedal harder.

examples.chinese: 把车停在坡上记得拉手刹。
examples.pinyin: Bǎ chē tíng zài pō shàng jìde lā shǒushā.
examples.english: Remember to use the handbrake when parking on a slope.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A common word for any incline, gentle or steep.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine a line hanging straight down (垂) until it hits (直) the ground at a right angle.
vocabulary.etymology: 垂 (to hang down/droop) + 直 (straight/upright). Together they convey the idea of something hanging or extending straight down, forming a right angle.

examples.chinese: 这面墙砌得不太垂直。
examples.pinyin: Zhè miàn qiáng qì dé bù tài chuízhí.
examples.english: This wall wasn't built very vertically.

examples.chinese: 画一条线，让它和底边垂直。
examples.pinyin: Huà yī tiáo xiàn, ràng tā hé dǐbiān chuízhí.
examples.english: Draw a line so that it's perpendicular to the base.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used in both everyday (hanging things straight) and technical/mathematical contexts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: You put something in the ground (土) and it stays (里) there.
vocabulary.etymology: Composed of 土 (earth) and 里 (inside). The basic and vivid idea of putting something 'inside the earth'.

examples.chinese: 小狗喜欢把骨头埋在花园里。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎogǒu xǐhuan bǎ gǔtou mái zài huāyuán lǐ.
examples.english: The puppy likes to bury bones in the garden.

examples.chinese: 他把自己的感情深深地埋在心里。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ zìjǐ de gǎnqíng shēnshēn de mái zài xīnlǐ.
examples.english: He buried his feelings deep in his heart.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be literal (burying objects) or figurative (hiding feelings, memories).

vocabulary.mnemonic: A formal act of 'burying' (埋) with a 'funeral' or 'interment' (葬).
vocabulary.etymology: 埋 (to bury) + 葬 (to inter/bury, specifically for the dead). A formal compound specifically for burial rites.

examples.chinese: 他被埋葬在故乡的山坡上。
examples.pinyin: Tā bèi máizàng zài gùxiāng de shānpō shàng.
examples.english: He was buried on a hillside in his hometown.

examples.chinese: 那个古老的习俗早已被历史埋葬。
examples.pinyin: Nàgè gǔlǎo de xísú zǎo yǐ bèi lìshǐ máizàng.
examples.english: That ancient custom has long been buried by history.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Primarily used for the burial of the deceased. More formal and solemn than '埋'. Can be used metaphorically.

vocabulary.english: urban and rural areas / town and country
vocabulary.mnemonic: The combination of the 'city' (城) and the 'countryside' (乡).
vocabulary.etymology: 城 (city/walled town) + 乡 (village/countryside). A compound representing the two primary types of human settlements.

examples.chinese: 城乡之间的生活水平还有差距。
examples.pinyin: Chéngxiāng zhī jiān de shēnghuó shuǐpíng hái yǒu chājù.
examples.english: There is still a gap in living standards between urban and rural areas.

examples.chinese: 这个政策是为了促进城乡协调发展。
examples.pinyin: Zhège zhèngcè shì wèile cùjìn chéngxiāng xiétiáo fāzhǎn.
examples.english: This policy is meant to promote coordinated development between town and country.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used as a combined concept, often in discussions about differences, integration, or development.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The specific 'district' or 'area' (区) within a 'city' (城).
vocabulary.etymology: 城 (city) + 区 (district/area). Refers to the urban core or an administrative district of a city.

examples.chinese: 老城区的房子比较贵。
examples.pinyin: Lǎo chéngqū de fángzi bǐjiào guì.
examples.english: Houses in the old city district are relatively expensive.

examples.chinese: 我们公司在新城区。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen gōngsī zài xīn chéngqū.
examples.english: Our company is located in the new urban district.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Contrasts with suburbs (郊区) or rural areas. Often used in administrative or geographical contexts.
