examples.english: This country practices a democratic system.

examples.chinese: 我们需要一个更民主的决策过程。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men xū yào yí gè gèng mín zhǔ de jué cè guò chéng.
examples.english: We need a more democratic decision-making process.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be used as a noun (追求民主) or an adjective (民主国家).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 'People' (民) who do 'labor' (工), often moving from rural areas.
vocabulary.etymology: 民 (mín): the people, commoners; 工 (gōng): work, laborer.

measure_word.example: 一个民工 (yí gè mín gōng)

examples.chinese: 很多民工春节前返乡。
examples.pinyin: Hěn duō mín gōng chūn jié qián fǎn xiāng.
examples.english: Many migrant workers return home before the Spring Festival.

examples.chinese: 这个建筑工地有很多民工。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge jiàn zhù gōng dì yǒu hěn duō mín gōng.
examples.english: There are many migrant workers on this construction site.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly refers to rural workers who move to cities for work. The term is neutral but can have socio-economic connotations.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'will' (意) of the 'people' (民).
vocabulary.etymology: 民 (mín): the people; 意 (yì): meaning, opinion, will.

examples.chinese: 最新的民意调查结果出来了。
examples.pinyin: Zuì xīn de mín yì diào chá jié guǒ chū lái le.
examples.english: The latest public opinion poll results are out.

examples.chinese: 政府需要考虑民意。
examples.pinyin: Zhèng fǔ xū yào kǎo lǜ mín yì.
examples.english: The government needs to consider public opinion.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in formal or political contexts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 'People's' (民) 'song' (歌).
vocabulary.etymology: 民 (mín): the people, folk; 歌 (gē): song.

measure_word.example: 一首民歌 (yì shǒu mín gē)

examples.chinese: 他喜欢唱陕北民歌。
examples.pinyin: Tā xǐ huān chàng Shǎn běi mín gē.
examples.english: He likes to sing Shaanbei folk songs.

examples.chinese: 这是一首很有名的中国民歌。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yì shǒu hěn yǒu míng de Zhōng guó mín gē.
examples.english: This is a very famous Chinese folk song.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 'People's' (民) 'police' (警).
vocabulary.etymology: 民 (mín): the people; 警 (jǐng): police, to warn.

measure_word.example: 一位民警 (yí wèi mín jǐng)

examples.chinese: 有位民警在路口指挥交通。
examples.pinyin: Yǒu wèi mín jǐng zài lù kǒu zhǐ huī jiāo tōng.
examples.english: A police officer is directing traffic at the intersection.

examples.chinese: 遇到困难可以找民警帮忙。
examples.pinyin: Yù dào kùn nán kě yǐ zhǎo mín jǐng bāng máng.
examples.english: You can ask the police for help if you're in trouble.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Specifically refers to civil police (as opposed to armed police 武警). A common term in mainland China.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 'Energy' (气) 'skill' (功) — the skill of cultivating life energy.
vocabulary.etymology: 气 (qì): vital energy, breath; 功 (gōng): skill, achievement.

examples.chinese: 我爷爷每天早上都练气功。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yé ye měi tiān zǎo shang dōu liàn qì gōng.
examples.english: My grandpa practices qigong every morning.

examples.chinese: 练气功对身体有好处。
examples.pinyin: Liàn qì gōng duì shēn tǐ yǒu hǎo chù.
examples.english: Practicing qigong is good for your health.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A holistic system of coordinated body posture, movement, breathing, and meditation.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'pressure' (压) of the 'air' (气).
vocabulary.etymology: 气 (qì): air, gas; 压 (yā): to press, pressure.

examples.chinese: 今天气压很低，感觉有点闷。
examples.pinyin: Jīn tiān qì yā hěn dī, gǎn jué yǒu diǎn mēn.
examples.english: The air pressure is low today, it feels a bit stuffy.

examples.chinese: 飞机起飞时，气压变化会让耳朵不舒服。
examples.pinyin: Fēi jī qǐ fēi shí, qì yā biàn huà huì ràng ěr duo bù shū fu.
examples.english: When the plane takes off, the change in air pressure can make your ears uncomfortable.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A scientific term commonly used in weather forecasts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Your 'spirit' (气) that makes you want to '概' (embrace, generalize) challenges.
vocabulary.etymology: 气 (qì): spirit, energy; 概 (gài): general idea, attitude.

examples.chinese: 他很有男子汉气概。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn yǒu nán zǐ hàn qì gài.
examples.english: He has a very manly spirit.

examples.chinese: 面对困难，他表现出了非凡的气概。
examples.pinyin: Miàn duì kùn nán, tā biǎo xiàn chū le fēi fán de qì gài.
examples.english: Faced with difficulties, he displayed extraordinary mettle.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used to praise someone's admirable and strong character, especially in the face of adversity.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'feeling' (氛) in the 'air' (气) of a place.
vocabulary.etymology: 气 (qì): air, atmosphere; 氛 (fēn): vapor, aura (often used in words about atmosphere).

measure_word.example: 一种气氛 (yì zhǒng qì fēn)

examples.chinese: 派对的气氛特别好。
examples.pinyin: Pài duì de qì fēn tè bié hǎo.
examples.english: The party atmosphere was great.

examples.chinese: 会议气氛很紧张。
examples.pinyin: Huì yì qì fēn hěn jǐn zhāng.
examples.english: The meeting atmosphere was very tense.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Describes the mood or feeling of a place or event.

vocabulary.english: complexion, color in one's face (indicating health)
vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'color' (色) of your 'energy/breath' (气) showing on your face.
vocabulary.etymology: 气 (qì): vital energy; 色 (sè): color.

examples.chinese: 你最近气色不错啊！
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zuì jìn qì sè bú cuò a!
examples.english: Your complexion looks great recently!

examples.chinese: 他生病了，气色很差。
examples.pinyin: Tā shēng bìng le, qì sè hěn chà.
examples.english: He's sick and looks very pale/unwell.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used to comment on someone's apparent health based on their facial appearance.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of 'H2O' — 'H' is Hydrogen, the lightest gas.
vocabulary.etymology: A modern character created for science. 气 (air) radical + 巠 (jīng, phonetic).

examples.chinese: 氢气比空气轻。
examples.pinyin: Qīng qì bǐ kōng qì qīng.
examples.english: Hydrogen gas is lighter than air.

examples.chinese: 氢是宇宙中最丰富的元素。
examples.pinyin: Qīng shì yǔ zhòu zhōng zuì fēng fù de yuán sù.
examples.english: Hydrogen is the most abundant element in the universe.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A scientific term. In daily life, mostly heard in compounds like 氢气.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'gas' (气) that helps things 'nourish/grow' (氧).
vocabulary.etymology: 氧 (yǎng): to nourish (associated with life-sustaining properties); 气 (qì): gas.

examples.chinese: 潜水员需要携带氧气瓶。
examples.pinyin: Qián shuǐ yuán xū yào xié dài yǎng qì píng.
examples.english: Divers need to carry oxygen tanks.

examples.chinese: 森林是地球的氧气工厂。
examples.pinyin: Sēn lín shì dì qiú de yǎng qì gōng chǎng.
examples.english: Forests are the Earth's oxygen factories.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common term, especially in medical (吸氧气) and environmental contexts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 'Water' (水) mixed with 'mud' (泥) that becomes hard like rock.
vocabulary.etymology: 水 (shuǐ): water; 泥 (ní): mud, paste.

measure_word.example: 一袋水泥 (yí dài shuǐ ní)

examples.chinese: 工地上堆了好多袋水泥。
examples.pinyin: Gōng dì shang duī le hǎo duō dài shuǐ ní.
examples.english: There are many bags of cement piled up on the construction site.

examples.chinese: 水泥还没干，别踩上去。
examples.pinyin: Shuǐ ní hái méi gān, bié cǎi shàng qù.
examples.english: The cement isn't dry yet, don't step on it.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The powder itself. Mixed with sand and water, it becomes concrete (混凝土).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 'Seek' (求) a 'job/position' (职).
vocabulary.etymology: 求 (qiú): to seek, to request; 职 (zhí): position, job.

examples.chinese: 他最近正在忙着求职。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuì jìn zhèng zài máng zhe qiú zhí.
examples.english: He's been busy job hunting lately.

examples.chinese: 写好简历是求职的第一步。
examples.pinyin: Xiě hǎo jiǎn lì shì qiú zhí de dì yī bù.
examples.english: Writing a good resume is the first step in job hunting.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used as a verb. 求职者 means 'job seeker'.

vocabulary.english: to slander, to smear, to vilify
vocabulary.mnemonic: To 'stain/dirty' (污) someone's name with 'false claims' (蔑).
vocabulary.etymology: 污 (wū): dirty, filth; 蔑 (miè): to disregard, to slight (implying contempt).

examples.chinese: 他在网上污蔑我，我要起诉他。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài wǎng shàng wū miè wǒ, wǒ yào qǐ sù tā.
examples.english: He slandered me online; I'm going to sue him.

examples.chinese: 这种污蔑之词，根本没人信。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng wū miè zhī cí, gēn běn méi rén xìn.
examples.english: No one believes this kind of vilification.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Stronger and more negative than just 'criticize'. Implies the use of false or malicious statements.

vocabulary.english: to bathe, to bask in (e.g., sunlight)
vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of it as 'M'opping yourself with 'W'ater (mù yù). Both characters contain the water radical (氵).
vocabulary.etymology: 沐 (mù): to wash hair; 浴 (yù): to bathe the body. Together they mean a full bath.

examples.chinese: 他喜欢沐浴在午后的阳光里。
examples.pinyin: Tā xǐ huān mù yù zài wǔ hòu de yáng guāng lǐ.
examples.english: He likes to bask in the afternoon sun.

examples.chinese: 运动完，沐浴一下真舒服。
examples.pinyin: Yùn dòng wán, mù yù yí xià zhēn shū fu.
examples.english: After exercise, taking a bath feels really good.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be literal (to bathe) or figurative (to be immersed in something positive like love, glory, sunlight). Slightly more literary than 洗澡.

vocabulary.english: to have or not have; to have? (asking if something exists/is done)
vocabulary.mnemonic: You have? No have? 'You mei you?' is literally the way to ask 'do you have...?' or 'did you...?'.
vocabulary.etymology: Direct combination of 有 (to have) and 没有 (to not have), creating an A-not-A question format.

examples.chinese: 你有没有带手机？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu méi yǒu dài shǒu jī?
examples.english: Did you bring your phone?

examples.chinese: 他有没有女朋友？
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu méi yǒu nǚ péng you?
examples.english: Does he have a girlfriend?

vocabulary.usage_notes: The standard way to form yes/no questions in spoken Mandarin. Place it before the main verb or at the end to ask about possession.

vocabulary.english: to take (medicine); to wear (clothes); to submit to
vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of '服' as the action in '服'从 (obey) and '服'务 (serve), or '服'装 (clothing). It's about putting something on or in.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted a hand forcing someone to kneel and serve, conveying the idea of submitting or serving. Extended to mean wearing clothes and taking medicine.

examples.chinese: 你该服药了。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ gāi fú yào le.
examples.english: It's time for you to take your medicine.

examples.chinese: 我真服了你了！
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhēn fú le nǐ le!
examples.english: I'm really speechless/impressed by you! (slang, showing exasperation or admiration)

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common in compounds. The slang expression '服了' expresses being convinced, impressed, or exasperated.

vocabulary.english: to be convinced; to admit (someone is better/right)
vocabulary.mnemonic: When you '服气', your 服 (submission) comes from 气 (genuine feeling/spirit). It's genuine acceptance.
vocabulary.etymology: 服 (to submit) + 气 (spirit, attitude). It means to submit from the heart, to be genuinely convinced.

examples.chinese: 你的技术这么好，我服气。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de jì shù zhè me hǎo, wǒ fú qì.
examples.english: Your skills are so good, I admit it (you're better).

examples.chinese: 他不服气输掉了比赛。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù fú qì shū diào le bǐ sài.
examples.english: He wasn't willing to accept the loss of the match.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used with 不 (bù) to express unwillingness to concede.

vocabulary.english: to catch sight of; to see from a distance
vocabulary.mnemonic: 望 (gaze afar) + 见 (see). It's not just looking, but finally 'seeing' what you were gazing at.
vocabulary.etymology: 望 (to gaze into the distance) + 见 (to see). To see something by looking afar.

examples.chinese: 我在山顶望见了整个城市。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài shān dǐng wàng jiàn le zhěng gè chéng shì.
examples.english: From the mountaintop, I caught sight of the entire city.

examples.chinese: 我一望见他就挥手。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yī wàng jiàn tā jiù huī shǒu.
examples.english: As soon as I saw him in the distance, I waved.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Emphasizes the act of seeing something that is relatively far away, often after some effort of looking.

vocabulary.english: native land; homeland; domestic (as opposed to foreign)
vocabulary.mnemonic: 本 (original) + 土 (soil/land). The 'original soil' you come from.
vocabulary.etymology: 本 (root, original) + 土 (earth, land). Refers to one's native earth or soil.

examples.chinese: 这部电影是针对本土观众的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diàn yǐng shì zhēn duì běn tǔ guān zhòng de.
examples.english: This movie is aimed at the domestic/local audience.

examples.chinese: 保护本土文化很重要。
examples.pinyin: Bǎo hù běn tǔ wén huà hěn zhòng yào.
examples.english: Protecting indigenous culture is important.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often contrasted with '外来' (foreign) or '国际' (international). More formal than 本地.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 本 (this) + 地 (place). 'This place' — right here where we are.
vocabulary.etymology: 本 (this) + 地 (place). Refers to this particular locality.

examples.chinese: 我是本地人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shì běn dì rén.
examples.english: I'm a local.

examples.chinese: 这 app 能用本地文件吗？
examples.pinyin: Zhè app néng yòng běn dì wén jiàn ma?
examples.english: Can this app use local files?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very common word. Less formal than 本土, more focused on the immediate area rather than the whole native country.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 本 (current) + 期 (period). Think of the 'current issue' of a magazine.
vocabulary.etymology: 本 (this) + 期 (period, issue). This period or installment.

examples.chinese: 本期的杂志主题是旅游。
examples.pinyin: Běn qī de zá zhì zhǔ tí shì lǚ yóu.
examples.english: The theme of this issue of the magazine is travel.

examples.chinese: 本期收入比上期多。
examples.pinyin: Běn qī shōu rù bǐ shàng qī duō.
examples.english: The revenue for this period is higher than the last period.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used in media, finance, and reporting. Often followed by 的 (de).

vocabulary.english: essence; intrinsic nature; what something really is
vocabulary.mnemonic: 本 (root) + 质 (quality). The 'root quality' of something, what's under the surface.
vocabulary.etymology: 本 (root, origin) + 质 (substance, quality). The original substance or core quality.

examples.chinese: 问题的本质是沟通不够。
examples.pinyin: Wèn tí de běn zhì shì gōu tōng bú gòu.
examples.english: The essence of the problem is insufficient communication.

examples.chinese: 看人要看本质，不是外表。
examples.pinyin: Kàn rén yào kàn běn zhì, bú shì wài biǎo.
examples.english: Look at a person's character, not their appearance.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A more abstract and philosophical term than 核心 (core). Often used in discussions of truth and character.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 本 (this) + 身 (body/self). The 'this-self', referring back to the subject.
vocabulary.etymology: 本 (this) + 身 (body, self). The very self of something.

examples.chinese: 手机本身没问题，是软件坏了。
examples.pinyin: Shǒu jī běn shēn méi wèn tí, shì ruǎn jiàn huài le.
examples.english: There's nothing wrong with the phone itself; it's the software that's broken.

examples.chinese: 学习本身是快乐的。
examples.pinyin: Xué xí běn shēn shì kuài lè de.
examples.english: Learning, in itself, is a joyful thing.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used to emphasize the subject, often to isolate it from external factors. Placed after the noun it refers to.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It's a 机 (machine) with a 关 (switch/off). It's either a mechanical gadget or a complex organization (like a machine).
vocabulary.etymology: 机 (machine, device) + 关 (to shut, joint, pass). Originally referred to a mechanical device with moving parts or a trigger.

examples.chinese: 这个玩具的机关在哪里？
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè wán jù de jī guān zài nǎ lǐ?
examples.english: Where is the mechanism/button on this toy?

examples.chinese: 他在政府机关工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài zhèng fǔ jī guān gōng zuò.
examples.english: He works in a government office.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Meaning changes with context: physical device, government body, or a clever trap (e.g., 暗藏机关).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 机 (engine/motor) + 动 (moving) + 车 (vehicle). An engine-powered moving vehicle.
vocabulary.etymology: 机动 (motorized, mechanical) + 车 (vehicle). A vehicle propelled by a motor.

examples.chinese: 这条街禁止机动车通行。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo jiē jìn zhǐ jī dòng chē tōng xíng.
examples.english: Motor vehicles are prohibited on this street.

examples.chinese: 中国机动车数量很多。
examples.pinyin: Zhōng guó jī dòng chē shù liàng hěn duō.
examples.english: China has a huge number of motor vehicles.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Official/legal term covering all motor-powered road vehicles. Contrasts with 非机动车 (non-motor vehicles like bicycles).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Picture a 杂货店 (zá huò diàn) — a 'miscellaneous goods store' with everything mixed together.
vocabulary.etymology: Derived from a character showing many birds in a tree, conveying a sense of many different things gathered together.

examples.chinese: 我的抽屉里东西很杂。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de chōu ti lǐ dōng xi hěn zá.
examples.english: The things in my drawer are very miscellaneous.

examples.chinese: 我买了些杂七杂八的东西。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi le xiē zá qī zá bā de dōng xi.
examples.english: I bought a bunch of odds and ends.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in compounds. 杂七杂八 is a common idiom meaning 'all sorts of things'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 木 (wood) + 雚 (bird watching). A wooden scarecrow has the 'authority' in the field. Think of 'power' and 'rights'.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted a weight on a scale (a weight used to balance), hence 'weight, authority'. Evolved to mean power and rights.

examples.chinese: 你有权保持沉默。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu quán bǎo chí chén mò.
examples.english: You have the right to remain silent.

examples.chinese: 他是公司的实权人物。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì gōng sī de shí quán rén wù.
examples.english: He is a person with real power in the company.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A foundational character in legal and political terms. Often distinguishes between 权力 (power/authority) and 权利 (right/entitlement).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 权 (authority) + 力 (force). The 'force of authority' — the power to make decisions and enforce them.
vocabulary.etymology: 权 (authority) + 力 (strength, force). Power as an active force of authority.

examples.chinese: 总统有很大的权力。
examples.pinyin: Zǒng tǒng yǒu hěn dà de quán lì.
examples.english: The president has great power.

examples.chinese: 不要滥用你的权力。
examples.pinyin: Bú yào làn yòng nǐ de quán lì.
examples.english: Don't abuse your power.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to institutional, political, or coercive power (power over others), as opposed to 权利 (rights).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 木 (wood) + 干 (trunk). A wooden trunk or pole. Think of a flag杆 (flagpole).
vocabulary.etymology: 木 (tree, wood) + 干 (trunk). Originally a wooden pole or shaft.

examples.chinese: 电线杆上有一只鸟。
examples.pinyin: Diàn xiàn gān shàng yǒu yì zhī niǎo.
examples.english: There's a bird on the utility pole.

examples.chinese: 他把旗子挂在杆上。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ qí zi guà zài gān shàng.
examples.english: He hung the flag on the pole.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Read as 'gān' for long, slender objects like poles. Read as 'gǎn' for the handle of certain tools (e.g., 笔杆).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 村 (village) + 庄 (farmstead). A village settlement, often in the countryside.
vocabulary.etymology: 村 (village) + 庄 (manor, farmhouse). A cluster of dwellings forming a small rural community.

examples.chinese: 我的爷爷奶奶住在山下的村庄里。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de yé ye nǎi nai zhù zài shān xià de cūn zhuāng lǐ.
examples.english: My grandparents live in a village at the foot of the mountain.

examples.chinese: 这个村庄以出产水果闻名。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè cūn zhuāng yǐ chū chǎn shuǐ guǒ wén míng.
examples.english: This village is famous for its fruit production.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Slightly more formal/literary than 村子, but very common. Evokes a rustic, small-scale community.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of a long 杠 (bar) and a 杆 (rod/pole) — that's a lever, a bar that pivots to move things.
vocabulary.etymology: 杠 (thick pole, bar) + 杆 (rod, pole). A lever is essentially a bar that pivots on a fulcrum.

examples.chinese: 用杠杆可以轻松撬起石头。
examples.pinyin: Yòng gàng gǎn kě yǐ qīng sōng qiào qǐ shí tou.
examples.english: You can easily pry up the stone with a lever.

examples.chinese: 他在投资时用了很高的杠杆。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài tóu zī shí yòng le hěn gāo de gàng gǎn.
examples.english: He used very high leverage in his investment. (financial term)

vocabulary.usage_notes: Also used in economics/finance (leverage). The principle is the same: using a small force to move a larger one.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 条 (strip, item) + 理 (order). Having your items in order, like strips neatly arranged.
vocabulary.etymology: 条 (strip, item) + 理 (to arrange, order). The order and arrangement of items or thoughts.

examples.chinese: 他的报告写得很有条理。
examples.pinyin: Tā de bào gào xiě de hěn yǒu tiáo lǐ.
examples.english: His report is written in a very methodical/logical way.

examples.chinese: 做事要有条理。
examples.pinyin: Zuò shì yào yǒu tiáo lǐ.
examples.english: You need to be methodical when doing things.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Almost always used in the phrase '有条理' (yǒu tiáo lǐ), meaning 'orderly, well-organized'.

vocabulary.english: to come and go; to have dealings/contact with
vocabulary.mnemonic: 来 (come) + 往 (go). People coming and going, which implies interaction and contact.
vocabulary.etymology: 来 (to come) + 往 (to go). The act of coming and going, implying movement and interaction.

examples.chinese: 这条路上来往的车很多。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo lù shàng lái wǎng de chē hěn duō.
examples.english: There's a lot of traffic (cars coming and going) on this road.

examples.chinese: 我们两家一直有来往。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men liǎng jiā yì zhí yǒu lái wǎng.
examples.english: Our two families have always had contact/kept in touch.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can refer to physical traffic or social interaction. For deep friendship, 交往 is more common.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 杰 (hero) + 出 (stand out). A hero who stands out from the crowd.
vocabulary.etymology: 杰 (hero, outstanding person) + 出 (to go out, stand out). To stand out like a hero.

examples.chinese: 他是一位杰出的科学家。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yí wèi jié chū de kē xué jiā.
examples.english: He is an outstanding scientist.

examples.chinese: 她在音乐领域成就杰出。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yīn yuè lǐng yù chéng jiù jié chū.
examples.english: She has achieved eminence in the field of music.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A strong compliment, often used for public figures or major achievements. More formal than 优秀.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 极 (utmost) + 端 (end). The 'utmost end' of a spectrum. Think of the poles of the Earth.
vocabulary.etymology: 极 (extreme point, pole) + 端 (end, extremity). The farthest ends or limits.

examples.chinese: 他的观点有时候很极端。
examples.pinyin: Tā de guān diǎn yǒu shí hou hěn jí duān.
examples.english: His views are sometimes very extreme.

examples.chinese: 我对你表示极端的感谢。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ duì nǐ biǎo shì jí duān de gǎn xiè.
examples.english: I extend my utmost gratitude to you.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be neutral (utmost) or negative (radical, excessive). Often used as 极端地 (extremely).

vocabulary.english: to construct; to build (often abstract systems, theories)
vocabulary.mnemonic: 构 (structure) + 建 (build). To build a structure, especially of ideas or systems.
vocabulary.etymology: 构 (to construct, compose) + 建 (to build, establish). To build or establish a structure.

examples.chinese: 我们要构建一个更完善的系统。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men yào gòu jiàn yí gè gèng wán shàn de xì tǒng.
examples.english: We need to construct a more complete system.

examples.chinese: 这本书旨在构建一个新的理论模型。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū zhǐ zài gòu jiàn yí gè xīn de lǐ lùn mó xíng.
examples.english: This book aims to build a new theoretical model.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common in academic, political, and technical contexts. Often used with abstract nouns like 体系, 模型, 社会.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 果 (fruit) + 树 (tree). Simple! A tree that bears 果 (fruit).
vocabulary.etymology: 果 (fruit) + 树 (tree). A tree cultivated for its fruit.

examples.chinese: 我家的后院种了几棵果树。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā de hòu yuàn zhòng le jǐ kē guǒ shù.
examples.english: We planted a few fruit trees in our backyard.

examples.chinese: 春天果树开花了。
examples.pinyin: Chūn tiān guǒ shù kāi huā le.
examples.english: The fruit trees blossomed in spring.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A general term. Specific trees are often named as [fruit]+树, e.g., 苹果树 (apple tree), 桃树 (peach tree).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 果 (fruit) + 酱 (sauce/paste). Fruit sauce! Think of spreading it on toast.
vocabulary.etymology: 果 (fruit) + 酱 (sauce, paste). A thick, sweet spread made from fruit.

examples.chinese: 早餐我想吃面包涂果酱。
examples.pinyin: Zǎo cān wǒ xiǎng chī miàn bāo tú guǒ jiàng.
examples.english: For breakfast, I want to eat bread with jam.

examples.chinese: 这瓶草莓果酱是自己做的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè píng cǎo méi guǒ jiàng shì zì jǐ zuò de.
examples.english: This jar of strawberry jam is homemade.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common breakfast item. 果酱 is specifically jam (with fruit pieces); smoother spreads are 果冻 (jelly) or 酱 (e.g., 花生酱).

vocabulary.mnemonic: A NEW (新) PERSON (人) joining the group.
vocabulary.etymology: 新 (xīn) means 'new'. 人 (rén) means 'person'. Together, 'new person'.

examples.chinese: 请大家欢迎我们部门的新人！
examples.pinyin: Qǐng dàjiā huānyíng wǒmen bùmén de xīn rén!
examples.english: Please welcome the newcomer to our department!

examples.chinese: 他们下个月办婚礼，是一对新人了。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen xià gè yuè bàn hūnlǐ, shì yī duì xīn rén le.
examples.english: They're getting married next month, they'll be a newlywed couple.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can refer to a new employee, a new member in a community, or a bride and groom.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Something NEW (新) that is RISING (兴) up fast.
vocabulary.etymology: 新 (xīn) 'new'. 兴 (xīng) 'rise, prosper'. Combined: 'newly rising'.

examples.chinese: 深圳是中国的一个新兴大城市。
examples.pinyin: Shēnzhèn shì Zhōngguó de yī gè xīnxīng dà chéngshì.
examples.english: Shenzhen is an emerging major city in China.

examples.chinese: 人工智能是一个新兴领域。
examples.pinyin: Réngōng zhìnéng shì yī gè xīnxīng lǐngyù.
examples.english: Artificial intelligence is an emerging field.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used to describe cities, industries, or technologies that are rapidly growing.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The side/direction (方) and the position/location (位).
vocabulary.etymology: 方 (fāng) 'direction, side'. 位 (wèi) 'position, location'. Combined for 'directional position'.

examples.chinese: 我方向感很差，总是搞不清方位。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ fāngxiàng gǎn hěn chà, zǒngshì gǎo bu qīng fāngwèi.
examples.english: My sense of direction is terrible, I always get disoriented.

examples.chinese: 你能告诉我卫生间在什么方位吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng gàosù wǒ wèishēngjiān zài shénme fāngwèi ma?
examples.english: Can you tell me what direction the restroom is in?

vocabulary.usage_notes: More formal than just 方向. Often used in contexts requiring precise location.

vocabulary.english: to put to use; to display (skills/talents)
vocabulary.mnemonic: To SPREAD (施) OUT (展) your abilities for others to see.
vocabulary.etymology: 施 (shī) 'carry out, apply'. 展 (zhǎn) 'unfold, display'. Combined: 'to put into action and display'.

examples.chinese: 他在新项目里终于可以施展自己的才华了。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài xīn xiàngmù lǐ zhōngyú kěyǐ shīzhǎn zìjǐ de cáihuá le.
examples.english: He can finally put his talents to use in the new project.

examples.chinese: 别拦着他，让他施展一下他的厨艺。
examples.pinyin: Bié lán zhe tā, ràng tā shīzhǎn yīxià tā de chúyì.
examples.english: Don't stop him, let him show off his cooking skills.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for applying and demonstrating one's abilities, often implying a release of pent-up potential.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A SHOP (店) for travelers (旅).
vocabulary.etymology: 旅 (lǚ) 'travel, journey'. 店 (diàn) 'shop, store'. Historically a shop for travelers.

examples.chinese: 我们在山脚下找到一家很温馨的小旅店。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài shānjiǎo xià zhǎodào yī jiā hěn wēnxīn de xiǎo lǚdiàn.
examples.english: We found a very cozy little inn at the foot of the mountain.

examples.chinese: 这家老旅店已经开了三十年了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā lǎo lǚdiàn yǐjīng kāi le sānshí nián le.
examples.english: This old guesthouse has been open for thirty years.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Slightly older or smaller than '宾馆' or '酒店'. Evokes a quaint, smaller-scale feeling.

vocabulary.english: to rotate; to spin; to revolve
vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine a XUAN (旋) causing something to TURN (转).
vocabulary.etymology: 旋 (xuán) 'revolve, circle'. 转 (zhuǎn/zhuàn) 'turn, rotate'. Combined for 'revolve and turn'.

examples.chinese: 地球围绕着太阳旋转。
examples.pinyin: Dìqiú wéirào zhe tàiyáng xuánzhuǎn.
examples.english: The Earth revolves around the sun.

examples.chinese: 别转了，我头都晕了！
examples.pinyin: Bié xuánzhuǎn le, wǒ tóu dōu yūn le!
examples.english: Stop spinning, I'm getting dizzy!

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be used for both literal (planets, objects) and figurative (thoughts, situations) spinning.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A group under a flag (旗) with ARROWS (矢) for protection. Think 'tribe'.
vocabulary.etymology: Pictograph originally representing a flag with arrows underneath, symbolizing a military clan or group.

examples.chinese: 我是汉族人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shì Hànzú rén.
examples.english: I am of Han ethnicity.

examples.chinese: 现在很多年轻人都是手机族。
examples.pinyin: Xiànzài hěnduō niánqīng rén dōu shì shǒujī zú.
examples.english: Nowadays, many young people are phone addicts (the 'phone group').

vocabulary.usage_notes: As a suffix, it's very productive, creating words for groups of people with a shared characteristic (e.g., 上班族 'office workers group', 丁克族 'DINK group').

vocabulary.english: have no way (to do something); not know where to start
vocabulary.mnemonic: Having NO (无) starting point/FOLLOW (从).
vocabulary.etymology: 无 (wú) 'without, not have'. 从 (cóng) 'from, follow'. Combined: 'without a point from which to follow/start'.

examples.chinese: 信息太少了，我无从判断。
examples.pinyin: Xìnxī tài shǎo le, wǒ wúcóng pànduàn.
examples.english: There's too little information, I have no way to judge.

examples.chinese: 他这么一说，我倒无从反驳了。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhème yī shuō, wǒ dǎo wúcóng fǎnbó le.
examples.english: Now that he's said that, I don't know where to start refuting him.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used before verbs to express a lack of basis, method, or starting point for an action.

vocabulary.english: to have nothing to do with; irrelevant
vocabulary.mnemonic: NO (无) CONNECTION/relation (关).
vocabulary.etymology: 无 (wú) 'without, not have'. 关 (guān) 'relation, connection'. Combined: 'without connection'.

examples.chinese: 这是我的私事，与你无关。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ de sīshì, yǔ nǐ wúguān.
examples.english: This is my private matter, it has nothing to do with you.

examples.chinese: 他说的那些话都跟主题无关。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuō de nàxiē huà dōu gēn zhǔtí wúguān.
examples.english: What he said is all irrelevant to the topic.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common pattern: 与/跟/和...无关 (to have nothing to do with...). The opposite is 有关.

vocabulary.mnemonic: NO (无) MOVEMENT (动) in the HEART (衷). Heart doesn't move.
vocabulary.etymology: 无 (wú) 'not'. 动 (dòng) 'move'. 于 (yú) 'at, in'. 衷 (zhōng) 'inner feelings, heart'. Literally 'not moved in the heart'.

examples.chinese: 不管我怎么求他，他都无动于衷。
examples.pinyin: Bùguǎn wǒ zěnme qiú tā, tā dōu wú dòng yú zhōng.
examples.english: No matter how much I begged him, he remained unmoved.

examples.chinese: 看到这么可怜的场景，你怎么能无动于衷？
examples.pinyin: Kàndao zhème kělián de chǎngjǐng, nǐ zěnme néng wú dòng yú zhōng?
examples.english: Seeing such a pitiful scene, how can you be so indifferent?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Describes a complete lack of emotional or sympathetic reaction.

vocabulary.mnemonic: NO (无) EFFECT (效).
vocabulary.etymology: 无 (wú) 'without, not have'. 效 (xiào) 'effect, efficacy'. Combined: 'without effect'.

examples.chinese: 这张优惠券过期了，已经无效。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhāng yōuhuìquàn guòqī le, yǐjīng wúxiào.
examples.english: This coupon is expired and is now invalid.

examples.chinese: 医生说这种药对我的病无效。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng shuō zhè zhǒng yào duì wǒ de bìng wúxiào.
examples.english: The doctor said this medicine is ineffective for my illness.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Opposite of 有效 (effective/valid). Used for documents, methods, arguments, treatments, etc.

vocabulary.english: to make trouble without reason; to be deliberately provocative
vocabulary.mnemonic: With NO REASON (无理), you go TAKE (取) a QUARREL (闹).
vocabulary.etymology: 无 (wú) 'without'. 理 (lǐ) 'reason'. 取 (qǔ) 'take'. 闹 (nào) 'make noise, quarrel'. Literally 'without reason, take a quarrel'.

examples.chinese: 他今天心情不好，故意在这里无理取闹。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīntiān xīnqíng bù hǎo, gùyì zài zhèlǐ wú lǐ qǔ nào.
examples.english: He's in a bad mood today and is deliberately making trouble here for no reason.

examples.chinese: 别理他，他就是想无理取闹引起注意。
examples.pinyin: Bié lǐ tā, tā jiùshì xiǎng wú lǐ qǔ nào yǐnqǐ zhùyì.
examples.english: Ignore him, he just wants to cause a scene to get attention.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A strong phrase criticizing someone for being unreasonable and troublesome.

vocabulary.mnemonic: NO (无) END (穷), NO (无) EXHAUSTION (尽). Double negative for emphasis.
vocabulary.etymology: 无 (wú) 'without'. 穷 (qióng) 'end, limit'. 无 (wú) 'without'. 尽 (jìn) 'exhaust, finish'. A repetitive structure for emphasis.

examples.chinese: 妈妈的爱是无穷无尽的。
examples.pinyin: Māmā de ài shì wú qióng wú jìn de.
examples.english: A mother's love is endless.

examples.chinese: 沙漠看起来无穷无尽。
examples.pinyin: Shāmò kàn qǐlái wú qióng wú jìn.
examples.english: The desert looks boundless.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used to describe something vast in quantity, time, or space that seems to have no limit.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Without (无) SHAME (耻).
vocabulary.etymology: 无 (wú) 'without'. 耻 (chǐ) 'shame, disgrace'. Combined: 'without shame'.

examples.chinese: 他偷了东西还不承认，太无耻了！
examples.pinyin: Tā tōule dōngxi hái bù chéngrèn, tài wúchǐ le!
examples.english: He stole something and still won't admit it, how shameless!

examples.chinese: 我从没见过这么无耻的人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ cóng méi jiànguò zhème wúchǐ de rén.
examples.english: I've never seen such a shameless person.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very strong, negative word for criticizing immoral behavior.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A person with NO (无) DEPENDABILITY/reliance (赖). You can't rely on them.
vocabulary.etymology: 无 (wú) 'without'. 赖 (lài) 'rely on, depend on'. Historically, one who has nothing to rely on,引申为品行不端的人.

examples.chinese: 那个无赖欠钱不还。
examples.pinyin: Nàge wúlài qiàn qián bù huán.
examples.english: That scoundrel owes money and won't pay it back.

examples.chinese: 你别耍无赖，快把东西还给我！
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié shuǎ wúlài, kuài bǎ dōngxi huán gěi wǒ!
examples.english: Don't act like a rascal, give my stuff back!

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to a person who is dishonest, unreasonable, and often uses low tricks. 耍无赖 means 'to act shamelessly'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: NO (无) BORDER/edge (边).
vocabulary.etymology: 无 (wú) 'without'. 边 (biān) 'edge, border, side'. Combined: 'without edges'.

examples.chinese: 站在海边，看着无边的大海。
examples.pinyin: Zhàn zài hǎibiān, kàn zhe wúbiān de dàhǎi.
examples.english: Standing by the sea, looking at the boundless ocean.

examples.chinese: 他给了我无边的支持。
examples.pinyin: Tā gěile wǒ wúbiān de zhīchí.
examples.english: He gave me limitless support.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used literally for vast landscapes (sea, sky, desert) or figuratively for abstract things like love or trouble.

vocabulary.english: day and night; around the clock
vocabulary.mnemonic: SUN (日) and NIGHT (夜). The full cycle.
vocabulary.etymology: 日 (rì) 'sun, day'. 夜 (yè) 'night'. Combined for the complete daily cycle.

examples.chinese: 医护人员日夜不停地工作。
examples.pinyin: Yīhù rényuán rìyè bù tíng de gōngzuò.
examples.english: The medical staff work day and night without stopping.

examples.chinese: 我日夜盼望着假期。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ rìyè pànwàng zhe jiàqī.
examples.english: I look forward to the holiday day and night.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used to emphasize continuous, non-stop action or anticipation.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The LANGUAGE (语) of JAPAN (日).
vocabulary.etymology: 日 (Rì) short for 日本 (Rìběn, Japan). 语 (yǔ) 'language'. Combined: 'language of Japan'.

examples.chinese: 我正在学习日语。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhèngzài xuéxí Rìyǔ.
examples.english: I am studying Japanese.

examples.chinese: 他的日语说得非常流利。
examples.pinyin: Tā de Rìyǔ shuō dé fēicháng liúlì.
examples.english: He speaks Japanese very fluently.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The standard term for the Japanese language. 日文 is also common, especially for written Japanese.

vocabulary.english: morning and evening; sooner or later
vocabulary.mnemonic: MORNING (早) and EVENING (晚). Covers both ends of the day, implying eventual inevitability.
vocabulary.etymology: 早 (zǎo) 'early, morning'. 晚 (wǎn) 'late, evening'. Combined for two opposite times of day.

examples.chinese: 他早晚会明白你的苦心。
examples.pinyin: Tā zǎowǎn huì míngbai nǐ de kǔxīn.
examples.english: He'll understand your good intentions sooner or later.

examples.chinese: 我早晚各刷一次牙。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zǎowǎn gè shuā yī cì yá.
examples.english: I brush my teeth once in the morning and once in the evening.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As an adverb (sooner or later), it expresses certainty about a future event. As a noun, it literally means morning and evening.

vocabulary.mnemonic: TIME (时) DIFFERENCE/GAP (差).
vocabulary.etymology: 时 (shí) 'time'. 差 (chā) 'difference, discrepancy'. Combined: 'time difference'.

examples.chinese: 北京和纽约有十二个小时的时差。
examples.pinyin: Běijīng hé Niǔyuē yǒu shí'èr gè xiǎoshí de shíchā.
examples.english: There is a twelve-hour time difference between Beijing and New York.

examples.chinese: 我刚到，时差还没倒过来。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gāng dào, shíchā hái méi dào guòlái.
examples.english: I just arrived, I haven't gotten over the jet lag yet.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to the time zone difference, and by extension, the physical discomfort (jet lag) caused by it.

vocabulary.mnemonic: TIME (时) doubled for emphasis = all the time.
vocabulary.etymology: Reduplication of 时 (shí) 'time'. Emphasizes continuity or high frequency.

examples.chinese: 我时时想起我们一起旅行的日子。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shíshí xiǎngqǐ wǒmen yīqǐ lǚxíng de rìzi.
examples.english: I often think of the days when we traveled together.

examples.chinese: 开车时要时时注意安全。
examples.pinyin: Kāichē shí yào shíshí zhùyì ānquán.
examples.english: When driving, you must pay attention to safety at all times.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Slightly more formal or literary than 经常, emphasizing constant vigilance or recurring thoughts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A specific TIME (时) SEGMENT/phase (期).
vocabulary.etymology: 时 (shí) 'time'. 期 (qī) 'period, phase'. Combined: 'a period of time'.

examples.chinese: 大学时期是我最快乐的时光。
examples.pinyin: Dàxué shíqī shì wǒ zuì kuàilè de shíguāng.
examples.english: My university period was the happiest time of my life.

examples.chinese: 我们现在处于一个关键的时期。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xiànzài chǔyú yī gè guānjiàn de shíqī.
examples.english: We are now in a critical phase.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to a distinct segment of time, often with defining characteristics (e.g., 战争时期 'war period').

vocabulary.english: now and then; sometimes; from time to time
vocabulary.mnemonic: TIME (时) and then (而)... indicating alternation.
vocabulary.etymology: 时 (shí) 'time'. 而 (ér) a conjunction indicating transition or connection. Combined: 'at times, and then...'.

examples.chinese: 他时而高兴，时而忧郁。
examples.pinyin: Tā shí'ér gāoxìng, shí'ér yōuyù.
examples.english: He is happy now and then, and gloomy at other times.

examples.chinese: 窗外时而传来鸟叫声。
examples.pinyin: Chuāng wài shí'ér chuán lái niǎo jiào shēng.
examples.english: Bird calls come from outside the window from time to time.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in pairs (时而...时而...) to indicate alternating states or intermittent occurrences.

vocabulary.english: season; time; period (often with seasonal/weather connotation)
vocabulary.mnemonic: The TIME (时) for a FESTIVAL/seasonal node (节).
vocabulary.etymology: 时 (shí) 'time'. 节 (jié) originally 'node, joint',引申为 'festival, season'. Combined for a time marked by seasonal characteristics.

examples.chinese: 现在是吃螃蟹的好时节。
examples.pinyin: Xiànzài shì chī pángxiè de hǎo shíjié.
examples.english: Now is the perfect season for eating crabs.

examples.chinese: 清明时节雨纷纷。
examples.pinyin: Qīngmíng shíjié yǔ fēnfēn.
examples.english: During the Qingming season, the rain falls endlessly. (A famous line of poetry)

vocabulary.usage_notes: Has a poetic or traditional flavor, often linked to natural phenomena, agriculture, or festivals. More specific than 时候.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Clothing (装) of the CURRENT TIME (时).
vocabulary.etymology: 时 (shí) 'time, current'. 装 (zhuāng) 'clothing, attire'. Combined: 'clothing of the time'.

examples.chinese: 她很喜欢看时装秀。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn xǐhuan kàn shízhuāng xiù.
examples.english: She really likes watching fashion shows.

examples.chinese: 这家店卖的都是最新款的时装。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn mài de dōu shì zuì xīn kuǎn de shízhuāng.
examples.english: This shop sells all the latest fashion items.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Specifically refers to clothing that is in vogue, as opposed to traditional or uniform clothing.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'orange' fruit and color is CHÉNG, like saying the word 'change' with an orange in your mouth.
vocabulary.etymology: 形声字 (phonetic-semantic). 木 (mù, tree) indicates it's from a plant/tree; 登 (dēng) suggests the pronunciation.

examples.chinese: 我想喝橙汁。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng hē chéngzhī.
examples.english: I want to drink orange juice.

examples.chinese: 这件衣服是橙色的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu shì chéngsè de.
examples.english: This piece of clothing is orange (in color).

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often overlaps with '橘子' (mandarin orange). For color, use '橙色'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: CÌ PǏN = 'Inferior Product'. Think of a product that's 'second' (次) place—not good enough to be first.
vocabulary.etymology: 次 (cì, secondary/inferior) + 品 (pǐn, product/goods). Literally 'inferior goods'.

examples.chinese: 商店在打折卖次品。
examples.pinyin: Shāngdiàn zài dǎzhé mài cìpǐn.
examples.english: The store is selling defective goods at a discount.

examples.chinese: 千万别买，这是次品。
examples.pinyin: Qiānwàn bié mǎi, zhè shì cìpǐn.
examples.english: Definitely don't buy this, it's a defective product.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to goods that don't meet quality standards. Often used in shopping/consumer contexts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: CÌ XÙ is the 'sequence'. 'CÌ' sounds like 'see', XÙ sounds like 'shoe'—see the shoes in the right order.
vocabulary.etymology: 次 (cì, sequence/order) + 序 (xù, order/arrange). A compound word emphasizing ordered arrangement.

examples.chinese: 请按次序排队。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng àn cìxù páiduì.
examples.english: Please line up in order.

examples.chinese: 名单是按姓氏的次序排的。
examples.pinyin: Míngdān shì àn xìngshì de cìxù pái de.
examples.english: The list is arranged in order of last name.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Similar to '顺序', but slightly more formal. Often used for lists, procedures.

vocabulary.mnemonic: CÌ SHÙ = 'time number'. Count (数) how many times (次) something happens.
vocabulary.etymology: 次 (cì, time/occurrence) + 数 (shù, number/count). Literally 'count of occurrences'.

examples.chinese: 我提醒他的次数太多了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ tíxǐng tā de cìshù tài duō le.
examples.english: I've reminded him too many times.

examples.chinese: 你迟到的次数有点儿多。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ chídào de cìshù yǒudiǎn er duō.
examples.english: The number of times you've been late is a bit high.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used to quantify how often an event occurs. Often followed by '多' or '少'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: ŌU ZHŌU. ŌU sounds like 'O' (as in 'Oh, Europe!') and ZHŌU means continent.
vocabulary.etymology: Transliteration. 欧 (Ōu) is a sound-matching character for 'Eu-', and 洲 (zhōu) means continent.

examples.chinese: 他明年想去欧洲旅游。
examples.pinyin: Tā míngnián xiǎng qù Ōuzhōu lǚyóu.
examples.english: He wants to travel to Europe next year.

examples.chinese: 欧洲有很多古老的国家。
examples.pinyin: Ōuzhōu yǒu hěn duō gǔlǎo de guójiā.
examples.english: Europe has many ancient countries.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A proper noun. Refers to the continent of Europe.

vocabulary.mnemonic: QĪ FU sounds like 'chee foo'—imagine a bully taking your 'chee'se and 'foo'd.
vocabulary.etymology: 欺 (qī, to deceive/cheat) + 负 (fù, to bear/be burdened). Original sense 'to take advantage of, oppress'.

examples.chinese: 不要欺负比你小的孩子。
examples.pinyin: Búyào qīfu bǐ nǐ xiǎo de háizi.
examples.english: Don't bully kids younger than you.

examples.chinese: 他上学的时候总被人欺负。
examples.pinyin: Tā shàngxué de shíhou zǒng bèi rén qīfu.
examples.english: He was always picked on when he was in school.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used among kids and in school/peer contexts. Often with passive '被'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: KUǍN DÀI sounds like 'kwan die'—think of being a guest so well treated, you could 'die' happy.
vocabulary.etymology: 款 (kuǎn, sincere/leisure) + 待 (dài, to treat/to receive). Literally 'sincere treatment'.

examples.chinese: 谢谢你们的热情款待！
examples.pinyin: Xièxie nǐmen de rèqíng kuǎndài!
examples.english: Thank you for your warm hospitality!

examples.chinese: 他非常会款待朋友。
examples.pinyin: Tā fēicháng huì kuǎndài péngyou.
examples.english: He is very good at treating friends cordially.

vocabulary.usage_notes: More formal than '招待'. Often used to express gratitude for hospitality.

vocabulary.mnemonic: GĒ CHÀNG = 'song' + 'sing'. It's a verb for singing, often more expressive or formal than just '唱'.
vocabulary.etymology: 歌 (gē, song) + 唱 (chàng, to sing). A compound verb meaning 'to sing a song'.

examples.chinese: 她在舞台上歌唱祖国的美好。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài wǔtái shàng gēchàng zǔguó de měihǎo.
examples.english: She sang of the beauty of her homeland on stage.

examples.chinese: 小鸟在枝头快乐地歌唱。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎoniǎo zài zhītóu kuàilè de gēchàng.
examples.english: The little birds are singing happily on the branches.

vocabulary.usage_notes: More formal, poetic, or descriptive than '唱歌'. Often used for singing in a performance or artistic sense.

vocabulary.mnemonic: GĒ XĪNG = song + star. A star who sings!
vocabulary.etymology: 歌 (gē, song) + 星 (xīng, star). A star associated with singing.

examples.chinese: 她小时候的梦想是当歌星。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎoshíhou de mèngxiǎng shì dāng gēxīng.
examples.english: Her childhood dream was to become a pop star.

examples.chinese: 那位歌星最近发新歌了。
examples.pinyin: Nà wèi gēxīng zuìjìn fā xīn gē le.
examples.english: That singing star recently released a new song.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Specifically refers to famous singers, especially in pop music.

vocabulary.mnemonic: GĒ CÍ = 'song' + 'words'. The words of a song.
vocabulary.etymology: 歌 (gē, song) + 词 (cí, words/lyrics). Literally 'song words'.

examples.chinese: 这首歌的歌词写得真好。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shǒu gē de gēcí xiě de zhēn hǎo.
examples.english: The lyrics to this song are really well written.

examples.chinese: 你能记住所有歌词吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng jìzhù suǒyǒu gēcí ma?
examples.english: Can you remember all the lyrics?

vocabulary.usage_notes: The standard word for song lyrics.

vocabulary.mnemonic: ZHǏ looks like a foot on a line (picture the character: a line with something above it). A foot stopping at a line.
vocabulary.etymology: Pictographic. Originally depicted a foot with a line in front, meaning 'to stop at a boundary'.

examples.chinese: 雨还没止。
examples.pinyin: Yǔ hái méi zhǐ.
examples.english: The rain hasn't stopped yet.

examples.chinese: 到此为止，别再说了。
examples.pinyin: Dào cǐ wéi zhǐ, bié zài shuō le.
examples.english: Let's stop here, don't say any more.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in formal or written contexts, or in set phrases. In spoken language, '停' is more common.

vocabulary.mnemonic: ZHÈNG DĀNG = 'right' + 'should'. It's the proper thing to do, or it's right at the moment something happens.
vocabulary.etymology: 正 (zhèng, correct/right) + 当 (dāng, to be/ought). Literally 'right and proper' or 'right at'.

examples.chinese: 他有正当的理由请假。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu zhèngdàng de lǐyóu qǐngjià.
examples.english: He has a proper reason to ask for leave.

examples.chinese: 我正当要出门，电话响了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhèngdāng yào chūmén, diànhuà xiǎng le.
examples.english: Just as I was about to go out, the phone rang.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As adjective: zhèngdàng (proper). As adverb: zhèngdāng (just when). Tone differs for adjective vs. adverb usage.

vocabulary.mnemonic: ZHĒNG YUÈ = 'upright month'. In ancient China, it was the month the calendar was 'corrected' or set straight.
vocabulary.etymology: 正 (zhēng, here a variant reading meaning 'first/head') + 月 (yuè, month). The first month of the lunar calendar.

examples.chinese: 正月十五是元宵节。
examples.pinyin: Zhēngyuè shíwǔ shì Yuánxiāo Jié.
examples.english: The 15th of the first lunar month is the Lantern Festival.

examples.chinese: 我们正月里要去拜年。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhēngyuè lǐ yào qù bài nián.
examples.english: We go to pay New Year visits during the first lunar month.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers specifically to the first month of the Chinese lunar calendar. Pronounced 'Zhēng yuè'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: ZHÈNG QÌ = 'righteous energy'. Imagine a person glowing with honorable vibes.
vocabulary.etymology: 正 (zhèng, upright/correct) + 气 (qì, energy/spirit). The energy or spirit of being upright.

examples.chinese: 他是一个充满正气的人。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yīgè chōngmǎn zhèngqì de rén.
examples.english: He is a person full of moral integrity.

examples.chinese: 我们要弘扬社会正气。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào hóngyáng shèhuì zhèngqì.
examples.english: We should promote upright social values.

vocabulary.usage_notes: An abstract noun describing moral character or a righteous atmosphere.

vocabulary.mnemonic: ZHÈNG JING = 'right scripture'. Imagine someone acting as properly as if they were following a holy book.
vocabulary.etymology: 正 (zhèng, correct) + 经 (jīng, classic/canon). Originally referred to orthodox Confucian classics, now means proper/serious.

examples.chinese: 说正经的，你到底去不去？
examples.pinyin: Shuō zhèngjīng de, nǐ dàodǐ qù bu qù?
examples.english: Seriously, are you going or not?

examples.chinese: 找份正经工作吧。
examples.pinyin: Zhǎo fèn zhèngjīng gōngzuò ba.
examples.english: Get a decent job.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very common in spoken Chinese to mean 'serious' or 'proper'. '不正经' means 'not serious/flippant'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: ZHÈNG FÙ = 'positive' + 'negative'. Think of math: + and -.
vocabulary.etymology: 正 (zhèng, positive) + 负 (fù, negative). A compound word for the two polarities.

examples.chinese: 电池有正负极。
examples.pinyin: Diànchí yǒu zhèng fù jí.
examples.english: A battery has positive and negative terminals.

examples.chinese: 这件事既有正面影响，也有负面影响。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì jì yǒu zhèngmiàn yǐngxiǎng, yě yǒu fùmiàn yǐngxiǎng.
examples.english: This matter has both positive and negative effects.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used in scientific, mathematical, or evaluative contexts (like pros and cons).

vocabulary.mnemonic: CǏ SHÌ = 'this' + 'matter/affair'. Points specifically to 'this' topic at hand.
vocabulary.etymology: 此 (cǐ, this) + 事 (shì, matter/affair). Literally 'this matter'.

examples.chinese: 此事与我无关。
examples.pinyin: Cǐ shì yǔ wǒ wúguān.
examples.english: This matter has nothing to do with me.

examples.chinese: 此事还需进一步讨论。
examples.pinyin: Cǐ shì hái xū jìn yī bù tǎolùn.
examples.english: This matter requires further discussion.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Slightly formal. In casual speech, people might say '这件事' more often.

vocabulary.mnemonic: CǏ QIÁN = 'this' + 'before'. The time before this point.
vocabulary.etymology: 此 (cǐ, this) + 前 (qián, before). Literally 'before this'.

examples.chinese: 此前我并不知道这件事。
examples.pinyin: Cǐ qián wǒ bìng bù zhīdào zhè jiàn shì.
examples.english: I didn't know about this before.

examples.chinese: 我们此前见过面吗？
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen cǐ qián jiànguò miàn ma?
examples.english: Have we met before (this)?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Formal or written. In casual speech, '以前' or '之前' is more common.

vocabulary.mnemonic: CǏ CHÙ = 'this' + 'place'. The spot right here.
vocabulary.etymology: 此 (cǐ, this) + 处 (chù, place/location). Literally 'this place'.

examples.chinese: 此处禁止停车。
examples.pinyin: Cǐ chù jìnzhǐ tíngchē.
examples.english: No parking here.

examples.chinese: 请在此处签名。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài cǐ chù qiānmíng.
examples.english: Please sign here.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Formal, often used in written instructions, signs, or formal announcements.

vocabulary.mnemonic: CǏ CÌ = 'this' + 'time/occurrence'. This specific instance.
vocabulary.etymology: 此 (cǐ, this) + 次 (cì, time/occurrence). Literally 'this time'.

examples.chinese: 此次活动非常成功。
examples.pinyin: Cǐ cì huódòng fēicháng chénggōng.
examples.english: This event was very successful.

examples.chinese: 感谢您此次的帮忙。
examples.pinyin: Gǎnxiè nín cǐ cì de bāngmáng.
examples.english: Thank you for your help this time.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Formal and often used in reports, speeches, or formal writing. Casual speech uses '这次'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: CǏ ZHÌ = 'this' + 'to send'. Think: 'With this, I send my regards' at the end of a formal letter.
vocabulary.etymology: 此 (cǐ, this) + 致 (zhì, to send/extend). Literally 'with this, I extend (greetings/salutations)'.

examples.chinese: 此致敬礼！
examples.pinyin: Cǐ zhì jìnglǐ!
examples.english: With best regards! (common letter ending)

examples.chinese: 信的最后写着“此致”和“敬礼”。
examples.pinyin: Xìn de zuìhòu xiězhe "cǐ zhì" hé "jìnglǐ".
examples.english: The letter ends with 'With best regards'.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used exclusively in formal letter writing. Always appears before the salutation (e.g., '敬礼').

vocabulary.mnemonic: WǓ XIÁ = 'martial' + 'knight-errant'. Think of Wǔ (武) like Kung Fu, and Xiá (侠) like a heroic knight.
vocabulary.etymology: 武 (wǔ, martial) + 侠 (xiá, chivalrous person). Refers to the genre of chivalrous martial arts fiction.

examples.chinese: 他最喜欢看武侠小说。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuì xǐhuān kàn wǔxiá xiǎoshuō.
examples.english: He loves reading martial arts chivalry novels.

examples.chinese: 这是一部经典的武侠电影。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yī bù jīngdiǎn de wǔxiá diànyǐng.
examples.english: This is a classic martial arts film.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to the entire genre of stories about martial artists and chivalry (e.g., Jin Yong novels).

vocabulary.mnemonic: SǏ WÁNG combines two characters meaning 'die' and 'perish'. Double death for emphasis.
vocabulary.etymology: 死 (sǐ, to die) + 亡 (wáng, to perish/to lose). A compound word for death.

examples.chinese: 这场事故导致了三人死亡。
examples.pinyin: Zhè chǎng shìgù dǎozhìle sān rén sǐwáng.
examples.english: This accident caused three deaths.

examples.chinese: 他死亡的原因还在调查中。
examples.pinyin: Tā sǐwáng de yuányīn hái zài diàochá zhōng.
examples.english: The cause of his death is still under investigation.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Formal term for death. In casual speech, '死' is more common as a verb.

vocabulary.mnemonic: CÁN JÍ = 'incomplete' + 'sickness'. Refers to a condition that impairs function.
vocabulary.etymology: 残 (cán, incomplete/disabled) + 疾 (jí, sickness). Literally 'disabling sickness/injury'.

examples.chinese: 他因车祸留下了终身残疾。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīn chēhuò liú xiàle zhōngshēn cánjí.
examples.english: He was left with a permanent disability from the car accident.

examples.chinese: 社会应该更关心残疾人士。
examples.pinyin: Shèhuì yīnggāi gèng guānxīn cánjí rénshì.
examples.english: Society should care more about people with disabilities.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A formal and respectful term for disability. '残疾人' is the term for a person with a disability.

vocabulary.mnemonic: CÁN JÍ RÉN = 'disability' + 'person'. A person who has a disability.
vocabulary.etymology: 残疾 (cánjí, disability) + 人 (rén, person). Literally 'person with a disability'.

measure_word.example: 一位残疾人 (yī wèi cánjí rén)

examples.chinese: 我们应该帮助残疾人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yīnggāi bāngzhù cánjí rén.
examples.english: We should help people with disabilities.

examples.chinese: 这个设施方便残疾人使用。
examples.pinyin: Zhège shèshī fāngbiàn cánjí rén shǐyòng.
examples.english: This facility is convenient for people with disabilities to use.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Standard, respectful term. More modern/inclusive terms like '残障人士' are also used.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine authorities saying "No SHOu'ing!", as they take something away.
vocabulary.etymology: 沒 (mò): to sink, to submerge, here meaning 'to take away'; 收 (shōu): to collect, to gather.

examples.chinese: 海关没收了他的违禁品。
examples.pinyin: Hǎi guān mò shōu le tā de wéi jìn pǐn.
examples.english: Customs confiscated his contraband.

examples.chinese: 老师没收了学生上课玩的手机。
examples.pinyin: Lǎo shī mò shōu le xué shēng shàng kè wán de shǒu jī.
examples.english: The teacher confiscated the student's phone which he was playing with in class.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in official contexts like law, school, or airport security.

vocabulary.mnemonic: You (油) need paint to bring color (漆) to your room.
vocabulary.etymology: 油 (yóu): oil, paint; 漆 (qī): lacquer, varnish. Originally referred to oil-based paint.

examples.chinese: 这桶油漆的颜色真好看。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tǒng yóu qī de yán sè zhēn hǎo kàn.
examples.english: The color of this paint is really nice.

examples.chinese: 周末我要自己油漆卧室的墙。
examples.pinyin: Zhōu mò wǒ yào zì jǐ yóu qī wò shì de qiáng.
examples.english: I'm going to paint my bedroom wall myself this weekend.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be used as a verb meaning 'to paint' (e.g., 油漆墙壁).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of 'YOU're NIght' out food - it's always greasy!
vocabulary.etymology: 油 (yóu): oil, grease; 膩 (nì): greasy,腻烦 (to be fed up). Describes something oily or a feeling of being overwhelmed by grease.

examples.chinese: 这个菜太油腻了，我吃不下。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè cài tài yóu nì le, wǒ chī bú xià.
examples.english: This dish is too greasy, I can't eat it.

examples.chinese: 他最近脸上很油腻，得好好洗脸。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuì jìn liǎn shàng hěn yóu nì, děi hǎo hǎo xǐ liǎn.
examples.english: His face has been very oily lately, he needs to wash it properly.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can describe food, skin, or figuratively describe overly smooth/flattering speech or behavior (油腻男).

vocabulary.mnemonic: The doctor's aim is to ZHI (治) the BING (病) - to fix the sickness.
vocabulary.etymology: 治 (zhì): to govern, to manage, to treat; 病 (bìng): illness, disease.

examples.chinese: 医生正在给病人治病。
examples.pinyin: Yī shēng zhèng zài gěi bìng rén zhì bìng.
examples.english: The doctor is treating the patient.

examples.chinese: 治病要花不少钱。
examples.pinyin: Zhì bìng yào huā bù shǎo qián.
examples.english: Treating an illness costs a lot of money.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to the act of curing/treating, not just seeing a doctor (看病).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine YAN (沿) river flowing ALONG the valley.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted water flowing along a riverbank. Now means 'to follow a course' or 'edge'.

examples.chinese: 我们沿着这条路一直走就到了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men yán zhe zhè tiáo lù yī zhí zǒu jiù dào le.
examples.english: We just need to keep walking along this road and we'll get there.

examples.chinese: 沿海地区经济比较发达。
examples.pinyin: Yán hǎi dì qū jīng jì bǐ jiào fā dá.
examples.english: Coastal areas are more economically developed.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used as 沿着 (yán zhe) + noun to mean 'along'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It's the area YAN (沿) the HAI (海) - along the sea.
vocabulary.etymology: 沿 (yán): along; 海 (hǎi): sea, ocean.

examples.chinese: 我住在沿海城市，夏天常去海边。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhù zài yán hǎi chéng shì, xià tiān cháng qù hǎi biān.
examples.english: I live in a coastal city and often go to the beach in summer.

examples.chinese: 沿海地区台风比较多。
examples.pinyin: Yán hǎi dì qū tái fēng bǐ jiào duō.
examples.english: Coastal areas have more typhoons.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used to describe regions, cities, or economies near the sea.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It's 沿 with a 着 - makes the action of following along continuous.
vocabulary.etymology: 沿 (yán): along; 着 (zhe): aspect particle indicating continuation.

examples.chinese: 沿着河边散步很舒服。
examples.pinyin: Yán zhe hé biān sàn bù hěn shū fu.
examples.english: It's very comfortable to take a walk along the river.

examples.chinese: 你沿着标记走，别迷路了。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yán zhe biāo jì zǒu, bié mí lù le.
examples.english: Follow the markers, don't get lost.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Must be followed by a noun or noun phrase indicating a path or edge.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The FA (法) law recognizes this REN (人) - but it's a company, not a human.
vocabulary.etymology: 法 (fǎ): law; 人 (rén): person. A 'person' in the eyes of the law, i.e., an organization.

examples.chinese: 我们公司是独立法人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men gōng sī shì dú lì fǎ rén.
examples.english: Our company is an independent legal entity.

examples.chinese: 签合同前要确认对方的法人资格。
examples.pinyin: Qiān hé tong qián yào què rèn duì fāng de fǎ rén zī gé.
examples.english: Confirm the other party's legal status before signing a contract.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Contrast with 自然人 (natural person). Common in business/legal contexts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The FA (法) law holds its meetings in this TING (庭) hall.
vocabulary.etymology: 法 (fǎ): law; 庭 (tíng): courtyard, hall. The hall where law is administered.

examples.chinese: 他明天必须出庭，上法庭。
examples.pinyin: Tā míng tiān bì xū chū tíng, shàng fǎ tíng.
examples.english: He must appear in court tomorrow.

examples.chinese: 法庭上要保持安静。
examples.pinyin: Fǎ tíng shàng yào bǎo chí ān jìng.
examples.english: You must remain quiet in the courtroom.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to the physical courtroom or the institution.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The FA (法) language of France!
vocabulary.etymology: 法 (Fǎ): France, French (abbreviation of 法兰西); 语 (yǔ): language.

examples.chinese: 她的法语说得非常流利。
examples.pinyin: Tā de Fǎ yǔ shuō de fēi cháng liú lì.
examples.english: She speaks French very fluently.

examples.chinese: 我在大学选修了法语课。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài dà xué xuǎn xiū le Fǎ yǔ kè.
examples.english: I took a French course in university.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Capitalized 法 here refers to France. 法国 is the country name.

vocabulary.english: to soak; bubble; to hang out
vocabulary.mnemonic: PAO - sounds like a bubble popping or tea bag soaking.
vocabulary.etymology: Pictograph of water (氵) and a wrapped/bulging form, suggesting bubbles or soaking.

examples.chinese: 泡茶之前最好先洗一下茶叶。
examples.pinyin: Pào chá zhī qián zuì hǎo xiān xǐ yī xià chá yè.
examples.english: It's best to rinse the tea leaves before brewing tea.

examples.chinese: 晚上一起去泡吧吗？
examples.pinyin: Wǎn shàng yī qǐ qù pào bā ma?
examples.english: Want to go hang out at a bar tonight?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Versatile:泡茶 (make tea), 泡妞 (hit on girls, slang), 泡温泉 (soak in hot springs), 气泡 (air bubble).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of BO (波) waves DONG (动) moving up and down - prices do that too.
vocabulary.etymology: 波 (bō): wave; 动 (dòng): to move. Movement like a wave.

examples.chinese: 最近股市波动很大。
examples.pinyin: Zuì jìn gǔ shì bō dòng hěn dà.
examples.english: The stock market has been very volatile recently.

examples.chinese: 他的情绪有点波动，别惹他。
examples.pinyin: Tā de qíng xù yǒu diǎn bō dòng, bié rě tā.
examples.english: His emotions are a bit unstable, don't provoke him.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for prices, emotions, signals, etc., implying irregular changes.

vocabulary.mnemonic: BO (波) LANG (浪) - both mean wave, so it's a wave wave!
vocabulary.etymology: 波 (bō): wave; 浪 (làng): wave. A compound word where both characters mean wave, emphasizing the concept.

examples.chinese: 海上的波浪好大啊！
examples.pinyin: Hǎi shàng de bō làng hǎo dà a!
examples.english: The waves on the sea are so big!

examples.chinese: 她头发的波浪卷很好看。
examples.pinyin: Tā tóu fa de bō làng juǎn hěn hǎo kàn.
examples.english: The waves in her hair look really nice.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Specifically refers to water waves, but can be used for wavy hair (波浪卷).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine BO TAO (波涛) waves being XIONG YONG (汹涌) fiercely powerful and scary.
vocabulary.etymology: 波 (bō): wave; 涛 (tāo): great wave; 汹 (xiōng): surge of water; 涌 (yǒng): to gush. Great waves surging violently.

examples.chinese: 台风来了，海面上波涛汹涌。
examples.pinyin: Tái fēng lái le, hǎi miàn shàng bō tāo xiōng yǒng.
examples.english: The typhoon is here, the sea is rough with turbulent waves.

examples.chinese: 他内心波涛汹涌，但表面很平静。
examples.pinyin: Tā nèi xīn bō tāo xiōng yǒng, dàn biǎo miàn hěn píng jìng.
examples.english: His heart was in turmoil, but he looked calm on the surface.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can describe actual rough seas or metaphorically describe intense emotions or situations.

vocabulary.mnemonic: NI sounds like 'knee' - you get your knees dirty in the mud.
vocabulary.etymology: Pictograph of water (氵) and earth/ground, representing wet soil.

examples.chinese: 下雨后路上全是泥。
examples.pinyin: Xià yǔ hòu lù shàng quán shì ní.
examples.english: The road is full of mud after the rain.

examples.chinese: 小孩喜欢玩泥巴。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo hái xǐ huān wán ní bā.
examples.english: Kids like to play with mud.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used as 泥巴 (ní ba) in casual speech. 水泥 means cement.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It ZHU (注) focuses your attention on the SHI (释) explanation in the margin.
vocabulary.etymology: 注 (zhù): to pour, to concentrate, to annotate; 释 (shì): to explain, to release.

examples.chinese: 这本书的注释写得很详细。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū de zhù shì xiě de hěn xiáng xì.
examples.english: The annotations in this book are very detailed.

examples.chinese: 我在古文旁边加了注释。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài gǔ wén páng biān jiā le zhù shì.
examples.english: I added notes next to the ancient text.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for explanatory notes in books, documents, or code.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It's the big YANG (洋) ocean, and also where foreign (洋) things come from.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally meant 'vast body of water'. Later used for things from 'across the ocean', i.e., foreign.

examples.chinese: 太平洋是世界上最大的洋。
examples.pinyin: Tài píng Yáng shì shì jiè shàng zuì dà de yáng.
examples.english: The Pacific Ocean is the world's largest ocean.

examples.chinese: 她穿得很洋气。
examples.pinyin: Tā chuān de hěn yáng qì.
examples.english: She dresses in a very fashionable/Western style.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As a noun, it's 'ocean'. As an adjective, it often means 'foreign' or 'Western-style' (洋快餐 fast food).

vocabulary.mnemonic: XI (洗) wash YI (衣) clothes FEN (粉) powder.
vocabulary.etymology: 洗 (xǐ): to wash; 衣 (yī): clothes; 粉 (fěn): powder.

examples.chinese: 超市的洗衣粉正在打折。
examples.pinyin: Chāo shì de xǐ yī fěn zhèng zài dǎ zhé.
examples.english: The laundry detergent is on sale at the supermarket.

examples.chinese: 这包洗衣粉能用一个月。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bāo xǐ yī fěn néng yòng yī gè yuè.
examples.english: This bag of laundry detergent can last a month.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The powdered form. 洗衣液 is liquid laundry detergent.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A DONG (洞) hole that's a XUE (穴) dwelling - a cave!
vocabulary.etymology: 洞 (dòng): hole, cave; 穴 (xué): cave, den, hole. Another compound where both parts mean cave.

examples.chinese: 我们在山里发现了一个很深的洞穴。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men zài shān lǐ fā xiàn le yī gè hěn shēn de dòng xué.
examples.english: We found a very deep cave in the mountains.

examples.chinese: 古代人有时住在洞穴里。
examples.pinyin: Gǔ dài rén yǒu shí zhù zài dòng xué lǐ.
examples.english: Ancient people sometimes lived in caves.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A more formal/literary term for cave than 山洞.

vocabulary.mnemonic: HONG (洪) massive water that's everywhere like the color red (also hóng) is alarming!
vocabulary.etymology: 洪 (hóng): vast, flood; 水 (shuǐ): water. Vast, overflowing water.

examples.chinese: 连续暴雨引发了洪水。
examples.pinyin: Lián xù bào yǔ yǐn fā le hóng shuǐ.
examples.english: Continuous heavy rain caused a flood.

examples.chinese: 洪水把村里的路都淹了。
examples.pinyin: Hóng shuǐ bǎ cūn lǐ de lù dōu yān le.
examples.english: The flood submerged all the roads in the village.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to a large-scale, destructive flood event.

vocabulary.mnemonic: HUO (活) alive and YUE (跃) jumping - full of energy!
vocabulary.etymology: 活 (huó): to live, alive; 跃 (yuè): to leap, to jump.

examples.chinese: 他是班里最活跃的学生。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì bān lǐ zuì huó yuè de xué shēng.
examples.english: He is the most active student in the class.

examples.chinese: 主持人努力活跃现场气氛。
examples.pinyin: Zhǔ chí rén nǔ lì huó yuè xiàn chǎng qì fēn.
examples.english: The host worked hard to liven up the atmosphere.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can describe a person, atmosphere, market, etc. As a verb: 活跃气氛 (to liven up the atmosphere).

vocabulary.mnemonic: PAI (派) to assign and CHU (出) to send out.
vocabulary.etymology: 派 (pài): to assign, to send; 出 (chū): to go out.

examples.chinese: 公司派出了最好的团队去谈判。
examples.pinyin: Gōng sī pài chū le zuì hǎo de tuán duì qù tán pàn.
examples.english: The company dispatched its best team to negotiate.

examples.chinese: 医院派出了救护车。
examples.pinyin: Yī yuàn pài chū le jiù hù chē.
examples.english: The hospital sent out an ambulance.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for official dispatch of people (police, reporters, teams) or vehicles.

vocabulary.mnemonic: LIU (流) flowing like a current, GAN (感) feeling sick - the flu spreads quickly.
vocabulary.etymology: 流 (liú): to flow, epidemic; 感 (gǎn): infection, feeling. Short for 流行性感冒 (liú xíng xìng gǎn mào).

examples.chinese: 最近流感很严重，你要小心。
examples.pinyin: Zuì jìn liú gǎn hěn yán zhòng, nǐ yào xiǎo xīn.
examples.english: The flu is really bad lately, be careful.

examples.chinese: 我打了流感疫苗。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ dǎ le liú gǎn yì miáo.
examples.english: I got a flu shot.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The common short term for influenza. More serious than a common cold (感冒).

vocabulary.mnemonic: CE (测) measure and DING (定) fix/confirm a value.
vocabulary.etymology: 测 (cè): to survey, to measure; 定 (dìng): to fix, to decide.

examples.chinese: 科学家测定了这种物质的化学成分。
examples.pinyin: Kē xué jiā cè dìng le zhè zhǒng wù zhì de huà xué chéng fèn.
examples.english: Scientists determined the chemical composition of this substance.

examples.chinese: 我们需要测定水的pH值。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men xū yào cè dìng shuǐ de pH zhí.
examples.english: We need to measure the water's pH level.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used in scientific, technical, or precision contexts to find out a specific value.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A duck FU (浮) on the water, not sinking.
vocabulary.etymology: Pictograph of water (氵) and a component suggesting a child/light object, meaning to float on water.

examples.chinese: 树叶浮在水面上。
examples.pinyin: Shù yè fú zài shuǐ miàn shàng.
examples.english: Leaves are floating on the water's surface.

examples.chinese: 他最近心情有点浮，静不下心学习。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuì jìn xīn qíng yǒu diǎn fú, jìng bú xià xīn xué xí.
examples.english: He's been feeling a bit restless lately and can't concentrate on studying.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Basic verb for 'to float'. Can be metaphorical: 浮夸 (exaggerated), 浮躁 (impetuous). Opposite is 沉 (chén, to sink).

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 军 (army) of the 海 (sea). Just think of warships.
vocabulary.etymology: 海 (sea) + 军 (army). Literally 'sea army'.

examples.chinese: 我哥哥在海军服役。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gēge zài hǎijūn fúyì.
examples.english: My older brother serves in the navy.

examples.chinese: 海军在海上进行演习。
examples.pinyin: Hǎijūn zài hǎishàng jìnxíng yǎnxí.
examples.english: The navy is conducting exercises at sea.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 通常与国家名称搭配，如“中国海军”。

vocabulary.mnemonic: Beyond the 海 (sea) is 外 (outside), so you're overseas.
vocabulary.etymology: 海 (sea) + 外 (outside). Literally 'outside the sea'.

examples.chinese: 他在海外工作了很多年。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài hǎiwài gōngzuòle hěnduō nián.
examples.english: He worked overseas for many years.

examples.chinese: 这个品牌在海外很受欢迎。
examples.pinyin: Zhège pǐnpái zài hǎiwài hěn shòu huānyíng.
examples.english: This brand is very popular abroad.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 常用在“在海外”、“到海外去”、“海外市场”等短语中。

vocabulary.english: sea floor / bottom of the ocean
vocabulary.mnemonic: The 底 (bottom) of the 海 (sea). Where the fish live.
vocabulary.etymology: 海 (sea) + 底 (bottom). Literally 'sea bottom'.

examples.chinese: 海底有很多美丽的珊瑚。
examples.pinyin: Hǎidǐ yǒu hěnduō měilì de shānhú.
examples.english: There are many beautiful corals on the sea floor.

examples.chinese: 他们发现了海底的宝藏。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen fāxiànle hǎidǐ de bǎozàng.
examples.english: They discovered treasure on the ocean floor.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A 报 (report) you stick on the wall (like a sea 海 of information).
vocabulary.etymology: 海 (sea, suggesting vastness/wide coverage) + 报 (report, notice). A notice for wide dissemination.

examples.chinese: 墙上贴着一张新电影的海报。
examples.pinyin: Qiáng shàng tiēzhe yī zhāng xīn diànyǐng de hǎibào.
examples.english: There's a new movie poster stuck on the wall.

examples.chinese: 帮我设计一个活动海报吧。
examples.pinyin: Bāng wǒ shèjì yīgè huódòng hǎibào ba.
examples.english: Help me design an event poster.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It's a 洋 (ocean), which is a really big 海 (sea).
vocabulary.etymology: 海 (sea) + 洋 (ocean). Together they form the general concept of the ocean.

examples.chinese: 海洋占地球表面的大部分。
examples.pinyin: Hǎiyáng zhàn dìqiú biǎomiàn de dà bùfen.
examples.english: The ocean covers most of the Earth's surface.

examples.chinese: 我喜欢听海洋的声音。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan tīng hǎiyáng de shēngyīn.
examples.english: I like listening to the sound of the ocean.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 比“海”更正式、泛指。

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 浪 (waves) in the 海 (sea). Perfect for surfing.
vocabulary.etymology: 海 (sea) + 浪 (wave). Literally 'sea wave'.

examples.chinese: 今天的海浪很大，不适合游泳。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān de hǎilàng hěn dà, bù shìhé yóuyǒng.
examples.english: The waves are big today, not suitable for swimming.

examples.chinese: 听着海浪的声音很容易睡着。
examples.pinyin: Tīngzhe hǎilàng de shēngyīn hěn róngyì shuìzháo.
examples.english: It's easy to fall asleep listening to the sound of the waves.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A 湾 (bend/curve) in the 海 (sea)'s coastline.
vocabulary.etymology: 海 (sea) + 湾 (bay, gulf). Literally 'sea bay'.

examples.chinese: 那个海湾的风景特别美。
examples.pinyin: Nàgè hǎiwān de fēngjǐng tèbié měi.
examples.english: The scenery of that bay is especially beautiful.

examples.chinese: 我们在海湾附近租了个房子。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài hǎiwān fùjìn zūle gè fángzi.
examples.english: We rented a house near the gulf.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 常作地名的一部分，如“东京湾”、“墨西哥湾”。

vocabulary.english: to smear / to daub / to scribble on
vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of a kid 涂 (smearing) and 抹 (wiping) paint everywhere.
vocabulary.etymology: 涂 (to smear, to daub) + 抹 (to wipe, to smear). A compound with overlapping meanings of applying a substance.

examples.chinese: 他在墙上胡乱涂抹。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài qiáng shàng húluàn túmǒ.
examples.english: He scribbled randomly on the wall.

examples.chinese: 记得出门前涂抹防晒霜。
examples.pinyin: Jìde chūmén qián túmǒ fángshài shuāng.
examples.english: Remember to apply sunscreen before going out.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 可以用于具体的涂抹动作（如药膏、油漆），也可比喻胡乱写作或绘画。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 让敌人或问题 消 (disappear) 灭 (extinguish)。
vocabulary.etymology: 消 (to disappear, vanish) + 灭 (to extinguish, die out). To cause to disappear and be extinguished.

examples.chinese: 我们必须消灭这些害虫。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bìxū xiāomiè zhèxiē hàichóng.
examples.english: We must eliminate these pests.

examples.chinese: 这个新药能消灭病毒。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xīn yào néng xiāomiè bìngdú.
examples.english: This new medicine can wipe out the virus.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 语气较强，常用于彻底清除有害或敌对的事物。

vocabulary.mnemonic: Things 消 (vanish) and are 耗 (used up) — that's consumption.
vocabulary.etymology: 消 (to disappear, consume) + 耗 (to consume, waste). Together emphasizing the process of using up.

examples.chinese: 爬山消耗了很多体力。
examples.pinyin: Páshān xiāohàole hěnduō tǐlì.
examples.english: Hiking consumed a lot of energy.

examples.chinese: 要减少水资源的消耗。
examples.pinyin: Yào jiǎnshǎo shuǐ zīyuán de xiāohào.
examples.english: We need to reduce water consumption.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 宾语常是抽象资源，如时间、精力、能量等。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 事情 涉 (wade into) 及 (reach) 到了某个范围。
vocabulary.etymology: 涉 (to wade, involve) + 及 (to reach). To reach into and become involved with.

examples.chinese: 这个问题涉及到很多人。
examples.pinyin: Zhège wèntí shèjí dào hěnduō rén.
examples.english: This issue involves a lot of people.

examples.chinese: 我们谈话涉及了很多方面。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen tánhuà shèjíle hěnduō fāngmiàn.
examples.english: Our conversation touched on many aspects.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 比较正式，口语中常用“关系到”或“跟...有关”。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 味道 淡 (light/bland) 的 水 (water)，不是咸的海水。
vocabulary.etymology: 淡 (bland, light, not salty) + 水 (water). Literally 'bland water'.

examples.chinese: 地球上可用的淡水很少。
examples.pinyin: Dìqiú shàng kěyòng de dànshuǐ hěn shǎo.
examples.english: There is very little usable fresh water on Earth.

examples.chinese: 这个湖是淡水湖。
examples.pinyin: Zhège hú shì dànshuǐ hú.
examples.english: This lake is a freshwater lake.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 与“咸水”或“海水”相对。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 让理解或关系变得更 深 (deep)，进行变 化 (change)。
vocabulary.etymology: 深 (deep) + 化 (-ize, suffix indicating transformation). To make something deep or deeper.

examples.chinese: 我们需要深化教育改革。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xūyào shēnhuà jiàoyù gǎigé.
examples.english: We need to deepen the education reform.

examples.chinese: 这次谈话深化了我们的友谊。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì tánhuà shēnhuàle wǒmen de yǒuyì.
examples.english: This conversation deepened our friendship.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 宾语多为抽象事物，如改革、合作、认识等。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 感情又 深 (deep) 情 (feeling) 又 厚 (thick) 谊 (friendship)。
vocabulary.etymology: 深情 (deep feeling) + 厚谊 (profound friendship). A four-character idiom expressing deep emotional bonds.

examples.chinese: 感谢你对我的深情厚谊。
examples.pinyin: Gǎnxiè nǐ duì wǒ de shēnqíng hòuyì.
examples.english: Thank you for your profound friendship towards me.

examples.chinese: 他们之间有着多年的深情厚谊。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zhī jiān yǒuzhe duōnián de shēnqíng hòuyì.
examples.english: They share many years of deep affection between them.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 书面语，情感色彩非常浓厚。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 又 深 (deep) 又 沉 (heavy/sunken) —— 形容思想或夜色。
vocabulary.etymology: 深 (deep) + 沉 (heavy, deep, sinking). Describing something that is both deep and weighty.

examples.chinese: 他是一个思想深沉的人。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yīgè sīxiǎng shēnchén de rén.
examples.english: He is a deep thinker.

examples.chinese: 夜晚非常深沉安静。
examples.pinyin: Yèwǎn fēicháng shēnchén ānjìng.
examples.english: The night was very deep and quiet.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 多用于形容抽象事物，如思想、感情、夜色、声音等。

vocabulary.mnemonic: “深”字说两遍，强调程度很深。
vocabulary.etymology: 深 (deep) reduplicated for emphasis, forming an adverb.

examples.chinese: 我深深地爱着我的家人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shēnshēn de àizhe wǒ de jiārén.
examples.english: I love my family deeply.

examples.chinese: 他的话让我深深地感动。
examples.pinyin: Tā de huà ràng wǒ shēnshēn de gǎndòng.
examples.english: His words moved me deeply.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 副词，修饰动词，表示程度极高。

vocabulary.english: to mix / to get along / to muddle through
vocabulary.mnemonic: 像水（氵）和太阳（日）混在一起——很随意。
vocabulary.etymology: 从水 (氵)，表示与水有关；昆声。本义为水势盛大，引申为掺杂、杂乱。

examples.chinese: 他把几种饮料混在一起喝。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ jǐ zhǒng yǐnliào hùn zài yīqǐ hē.
examples.english: He mixed several kinds of drinks together and drank them.

examples.chinese: 我刚来这个城市，还没混熟。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gāng lái zhège chéngshì, hái méi hùn shú.
examples.english: I just arrived in this city and haven't gotten familiar with it yet.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 口语常用，意思多样，可指物理混合，也可指社交（混得好）、敷衍度日（混日子）。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 又 混 (mixed up) 又 乱 (disordered)，当然很混乱。
vocabulary.etymology: 混 (to mix, confuse) + 乱 (disorder, chaos). A state of being mixed up and disordered.

examples.chinese: 事故现场一片混乱。
examples.pinyin: Shìgù xiànchǎng yīpiàn hùnluàn.
examples.english: The accident scene was in complete chaos.

examples.chinese: 我的思绪很混乱。
