examples.english: This kind of medicine kills cancer cells.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Strictly a biological term. Also used metaphorically for 'smallest unit' (e.g., 家庭是社会的基本细胞).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Very '细' (tiny) '菌' (fungus/bacteria) you can't see.
vocabulary.etymology: 细 (fine, small) + 菌 (fungus, bacterium).

examples.chinese: 饭前要洗手，不然会有很多细菌。
examples.pinyin: Fàn qián yào xǐ shǒu, bùrán huì yǒu hěnduō xìjūn.
examples.english: You need to wash your hands before eating, otherwise there will be lots of germs.

examples.chinese: 有些细菌对身体是有益的。
examples.pinyin: Yǒu xiē xìjūn duì shēntǐ shì yǒuyì de.
examples.english: Some bacteria are beneficial to the body.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Colloquially, often equated with 'germs'. 病毒 (bìngdú) specifically means 'virus'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Picture threads interlocking to '织' a sweater.
vocabulary.etymology: 纟(silk radical) + 只 (originally a phonetic component). Depicts the action of weaving threads.

examples.chinese: 我妈妈会织毛衣。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ māmā huì zhī máoyī.
examples.english: My mom knows how to knit sweaters.

examples.chinese: 蜘蛛在织网。
examples.pinyin: Zhīzhū zài zhī wǎng.
examples.english: The spider is weaving a web.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for knitting clothes (织毛衣) and weaving fabric or webs.

vocabulary.english: all year round / age at death
vocabulary.mnemonic: The '终' (end) of the '年' (year) -> throughout the whole year. Or the year life ended.
vocabulary.etymology: 终 (end, throughout) + 年 (year).

examples.chinese: 这座雪山终年积雪。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò xuěshān zhōngnián jīxuě.
examples.english: This snow-capped mountain is covered in snow all year round.

examples.chinese: 他终年八十五岁。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhōngnián bāshíwǔ suì.
examples.english: He died at the age of eighty-five.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Has two distinct meanings: 1) throughout the year; 2) (formal/elegiac) age at which someone passed away.

vocabulary.english: longitude and latitude / warp and weft
vocabulary.mnemonic: '经' (longitude lines) and '纬' (latitude lines) crisscross the globe.
vocabulary.etymology: 经 (warp, longitude) + 纬 (weft, latitude). Originally from weaving terms applied to geography.

examples.chinese: 在地图上可以根据经纬度确定位置。
examples.pinyin: Zài dìtú shàng kěyǐ gēnjù jīngwěidù quèdìng wèizhì.
examples.english: On a map, you can determine a location based on longitude and latitude.

examples.chinese: 这件事经纬万端，很复杂。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì jīngwěi wànduān, hěn fùzá.
examples.english: This matter is as complex as warp and weft; it's very complicated.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Mostly used in the compound 经纬度 (jīngwěidù) for coordinates. Can be used metaphorically for complex interrelations.

vocabulary.mnemonic: To '结' (conclude/finish) the '算' (calculation/bill).
vocabulary.etymology: 结 (to settle, to conclude) + 算 (to calculate, to reckon).

examples.chinese: 我们吃完饭用手机结算吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen chī wán fàn yòng shǒujī jiésuàn ba.
examples.english: Let's use our phones to settle the bill after dinner.

examples.chinese: 每月五号是工资结算日。
examples.pinyin: Měi yuè wǔ hào shì gōngzī jiésuàn rì.
examples.english: The 5th of every month is payday (salary settlement day).

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common in financial, commercial, and daily payment contexts (like settling a restaurant bill).

vocabulary.mnemonic: To '绘' (depict) a '画' (picture).
vocabulary.etymology: 绘 (to draw, to paint) + 画 (picture, to draw).

examples.chinese: 他从小就对绘画特别感兴趣。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù duì huìhuà tèbié gǎn xìngqù.
examples.english: He has been very interested in painting since he was a child.

examples.chinese: 这幅绘画作品价值连城。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fú huìhuà zuòpǐn jiàzhí liánchéng.
examples.english: This painting is priceless.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The general, formal term for the art of painting/drawing. Colloquially, 画画儿 (huà huàr) is more common for the activity.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think '给' (give) + '予' (also means 'to give') – giving doubled!
vocabulary.etymology: 给 (to give) + 予 (to give). A compound of two synonymous characters.

examples.chinese: 公司给予优秀员工丰厚的奖励。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī jǐyǔ yōuxiù yuángōng fēnghòu de jiǎnglì.
examples.english: The company gives outstanding employees generous rewards.

examples.chinese: 感谢你给予我的信任。
examples.pinyin: Gǎnxiè nǐ jǐyǔ wǒ de xìnrèn.
examples.english: Thank you for the trust you have placed in me.

vocabulary.usage_notes: More formal and written than '给'. The pronunciation 'jǐ yǔ' is standard, though 'gěi yǔ' is sometimes heard colloquially.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Something so good or bad it's '绝' (cut off) from the ordinary.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted cutting silk threads (纟) with a knife (刀 variant). Means to sever,引申为 unique or extreme.

examples.chinese: 这家的火锅味道绝了！
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā de huǒguō wèidào jué le!
examples.english: The hotpot at this place is absolutely incredible!

examples.chinese: 他做事太绝，不留后路。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuò shì tài jué, bù liú hòulù.
examples.english: He does things too ruthlessly, leaving no way out.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As an adjective/adverb, it's a strong colloquial intensifier meaning 'awesome', 'terrible', or 'absolute'.

vocabulary.english: the vast majority / the overwhelming majority
vocabulary.mnemonic: '绝' (absolute) '大' (big) '多' (many) '数' (number) -> an absolutely huge number of people.
vocabulary.etymology: 绝 (absolute) + 大 (big) + 多 (many) + 数 (number).

examples.chinese: 绝大多数同学都同意这个方案。
examples.pinyin: Jué dà duōshù tóngxué dōu tóngyì zhège fāng'àn.
examples.english: The vast majority of classmates agree with this plan.

examples.chinese: 这件事得到了绝大多数人的支持。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì dédào le jué dà duōshù rén de zhīchí.
examples.english: This matter has gained the support of the overwhelming majority of people.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Stronger than just '大多数'. Used for statistics and emphasizing near-unanimity.

vocabulary.english: to make overall plans and take all factors into account
vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of a chef '统筹' (planning the whole meal) while '兼顾' (keeping an eye on all pots).
vocabulary.etymology: 统筹 (to plan as a whole) + 兼顾 (to give consideration to multiple aspects).

examples.chinese: 做项目经理要懂得统筹兼顾。
examples.pinyin: Zuò xiàngmù jīnglǐ yào dǒng dé tǒngchóu jiāngù.
examples.english: A project manager needs to know how to plan comprehensively and balance all factors.

examples.chinese: 制定政策必须统筹兼顾各方面的利益。
examples.pinyin: Zhìdìng zhèngcè bìxū tǒngchóu jiāngù gè fāngmiàn de lìyì.
examples.english: When formulating policies, we must make overall plans and consider the interests of all parties.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A formal, managerial term used in work, government, or complex planning contexts.

vocabulary.english: to carry on the past and open up the future
vocabulary.mnemonic: '继往' (succeed the past) and '开来' (open up the future) – bridging history and tomorrow.
vocabulary.etymology: 继往 (to continue the past legacy) + 开来 (to open up the future).

examples.chinese: 我们这一代人肩负着继往开来的重任。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhè yīdài rén jiānfù zhe jìwǎngkāilái de zhòngrèn.
examples.english: Our generation shoulders the heavy responsibility of carrying forward the past and ushering in the future.

examples.chinese: 这次大会是一次继往开来的大会。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì dàhuì shì yī cì jìwǎngkāilái de dàhuì.
examples.english: This congress is one that builds on past achievements and forges ahead into the future.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A formal, aspirational idiom, often used in speeches, writing, and historical commentary.

vocabulary.mnemonic: '维' (maintain) '生' (life) '素' (element) — the element that maintains life.
vocabulary.etymology: A phonetic and semantic translation: 维 (to maintain) + 生 (life) + 素 (element). Coined from the Japanese 'bitamin'.

examples.chinese: 多吃水果可以补充维生素C。
examples.pinyin: Duō chī shuǐguǒ kěyǐ bǔchōng wéishēngsù C.
examples.english: Eating more fruit can supplement your Vitamin C.

examples.chinese: 你缺乏维生素，需要多吃点蔬菜。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ quēfá wéishēngsù, xūyào duō chī diǎn shūcài.
examples.english: You're lacking vitamins; you need to eat more vegetables.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often shortened to 维他命 (wéitāmìng), especially in older contexts or influenced by Cantonese.

vocabulary.english: to plant trees / to green / greening
vocabulary.mnemonic: To make an area '绿' (green) by '化' (-ize/transform) it.
vocabulary.etymology: 绿 (green) + 化 (suffix meaning 'to make into', '-ize').

examples.chinese: 我们小区这几年绿化做得很好。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xiǎoqū zhè jǐ nián lǜhuà zuò dé hěn hǎo.
examples.english: The greening in our residential area has been done very well these past few years.

examples.chinese: 政府计划绿化这片荒地。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ jìhuà lǜhuà zhè piàn huāngdì.
examples.english: The government plans to plant trees on this wasteland.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A common term in urban planning and environmental protection.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of '父' as Dad and '女' as daughter — a family unit.
vocabulary.etymology: '父' is a pictograph of a hand holding a tool, representing a father or elder. '女' is a pictograph of a kneeling woman.

examples.chinese: 那对父女长得真像。
examples.pinyin: Nà duì fù nǚ zhǎng de zhēn xiàng.
examples.english: That father and daughter look so alike.

examples.chinese: 他们父女关系特别好。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen fù nǚ guānxì tèbié hǎo.
examples.english: Their father-daughter relationship is especially good.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers specifically to the relationship pair, not to one individual.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Like '父女', but with '子' (son) completing the picture.
vocabulary.etymology: '父' (father). '子' is a pictograph of a swaddled infant, later meaning child or son.

examples.chinese: 这家店是父子俩经营的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn shì fù zǐ liǎ jīngyíng de.
examples.english: This shop is run by the father and son pair.

examples.chinese: 他们父子都是足球迷。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen fù zǐ dōu shì zúqiú mí.
examples.english: Both the father and son are football fans.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers specifically to the relationship pair.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine a cool breeze on a hot day — that refreshing '爽' feeling!
vocabulary.etymology: The character originally depicted a person with light radiating from both sides, implying brightness and clarity.

examples.chinese: 喝一口冰水真爽！
examples.pinyin: Hē yī kǒu bīng shuǐ zhēn shuǎng!
examples.english: Drinking a sip of ice water is so refreshing!

examples.chinese: 他这人说话很爽快。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhè rén shuōhuà hěn shuǎngkuai.
examples.english: He's a very straightforward talker.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very common in spoken Chinese to express feeling good, satisfied, or straightforward.

vocabulary.mnemonic: '片' (slice) + '刻' (carve/moment) = a slice of time.
vocabulary.etymology: '片' means a thin slice or fragment. '刻' originally meant to carve, and by extension a unit of time (a quarter of an hour).

examples.chinese: 请等我片刻。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng děng wǒ piànkè.
examples.english: Please wait a moment for me.

examples.chinese: 他片刻都不想离开手机。
examples.pinyin: Tā piànkè dōu bù xiǎng líkāi shǒujī.
examples.english: He doesn't want to be away from his phone for even a moment.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Slightly more formal/literary than '一会儿', but still common.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Like a broken piece ('断') of a larger picture or story ('片').
vocabulary.etymology: '片' (slice/fragment). '断' (to break/to sever). Combined, it means a broken-off fragment.

examples.chinese: 我只记得一些零碎的片断。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhǐ jìde yīxiē língsuì de piànduàn.
examples.english: I only remember some scattered fragments.

examples.chinese: 这部电影有几个精彩的片断。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng yǒu jǐ gè jīngcǎi de piànduàn.
examples.english: This movie has several brilliant episodes.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for memories, stories, or videos. Can be interchangeable with '片段'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of different 'editions' of a book or app — '版' (printing block) + '本' (book).
vocabulary.etymology: '版' refers to a printing block. '本' means root or book. Together it means a printed edition of a book, now extended to versions of anything.

examples.chinese: 你手机系统是什么版本？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ shǒujī xìtǒng shì shénme bǎnběn?
examples.english: What version is your phone's operating system?

examples.chinese: 这个故事有好多不同版本。
examples.pinyin: Zhège gùshi yǒu hǎo duō bùtóng bǎnběn.
examples.english: There are many different versions of this story.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Extremely common for software, games, books, and news stories.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A '牢' is a secure enclosure — think '牢固' (firm) or '牢房' (jail cell).
vocabulary.etymology: The character depicts an ox ('牛') under a roof, originally meaning a pen for sacrificial animals, implying confinement and solidity.

examples.chinese: 这个结打得很牢。
examples.pinyin: Zhège jié dǎ de hěn láo.
examples.english: This knot is tied very firmly.

examples.chinese: 他被关进了牢里。
examples.pinyin: Tā bèi guān jìnle láo lǐ.
examples.english: He was locked up in prison.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As a single character, it's often used for 'prison' or in the adjective '牢固'. More common in compounds.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine someone '牢' (trapped) with negative feelings, '骚' (disturbed) enough to complain.
vocabulary.etymology: '牢' here may imply being bound/fixated. '骚' means disturbance or unrest.

examples.chinese: 他整天对工作发牢骚。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhěng tiān duì gōngzuò fā láosāo.
examples.english: He complains about work all day.

examples.chinese: 别听他的牢骚，他就是心情不好。
examples.pinyin: Bié tīng tā de láosāo, tā jiùshì xīnqíng bù hǎo.
examples.english: Don't listen to his grumbling, he's just in a bad mood.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used with the verb '发' (to vent). Slightly negative connotation of petty complaining.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A formal word for 'things' — '物' (thing) + '品' (article/grade).
vocabulary.etymology: '物' is a pictograph of an ox, representing things/animals. '品' depicts three mouths, representing many or grade/class.

examples.chinese: 请保管好您的个人物品。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎoguǎn hǎo nín de gèrén wùpǐn.
examples.english: Please take good care of your personal belongings.

examples.chinese: 超市里有各种各样的物品。
examples.pinyin: Chāoshì lǐ yǒu gèzhǒng gèyàng de wùpǐn.
examples.english: There are all kinds of items in the supermarket.

vocabulary.usage_notes: More formal than '东西', common in announcements, signs, and official contexts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Things ('物') are beautiful ('美') and price ('价') is cheap ('廉') — the perfect deal!
vocabulary.etymology: A four-character idiom built logically: '物' (thing), '美' (beautiful/good), '价' (price), '廉' (cheap/inexpensive).

examples.chinese: 这家小店的东西物美价廉。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā xiǎo diàn de dōngxi wù měi jià lián.
examples.english: The stuff in this small shop is good and cheap.

examples.chinese: 我们都喜欢物美价廉的产品。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen dōu xǐhuan wù měi jià lián de chǎnpǐn.
examples.english: We all like products that are high-quality and low-priced.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very common and positive phrase used in advertising and everyday praise.

vocabulary.english: to pull; to lead along; to involve
vocabulary.mnemonic: Picture leading an ox ('牛') with a rope — that's '牵'. Also used for emotional '牵'挂.
vocabulary.etymology: Depicts an ox ('牛') being led by a rope. The top part represents the rope or halter.

examples.chinese: 妈妈牵着孩子的手过马路。
examples.pinyin: Māma qiānzhe háizi de shǒu guò mǎlù.
examples.english: The mother held the child's hand to cross the street.

examples.chinese: 这件事牵涉到很多人。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì qiānshè dào hěn duō rén.
examples.english: This matter involves a lot of people.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often implies a gentle pull or a connection. Common in compounds like '牵手' (hold hands) and '牵挂' (worry about).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Something '特'别 stands out from the herd (the character contains '牛' - ox).
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted a special type of sacrificial ox ('牛'). Evolved to mean 'special' or 'unique'.

examples.chinese: 今天是个特好的日子。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān shì gè tè hǎo de rìzi.
examples.english: Today is an especially good day.

examples.chinese: 他有特长。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu tècháng.
examples.english: He has a special skill.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Extremely versatile. As an adverb ('特好'), it's very colloquial in Northern Chinese. Also a common prefix meaning 'special-'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: You go out of your way ('特') to a place ('地') to do something — that's doing it '特地'.
vocabulary.etymology: '特' (special) + '地' (a modal particle/adverbial suffix).

examples.chinese: 我特地去车站接你。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ tèdì qù chēzhàn jiē nǐ.
examples.english: I came to pick you up at the station specially.

examples.chinese: 这是他特地为你做的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì tā tèdì wèi nǐ zuò de.
examples.english: This is what he made specially for you.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Emphasizes the deliberate effort made. Very common in spoken Chinese.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Something '特' (extra) '大' (big) is huge!
vocabulary.etymology: Literal combination: '特' (special/extra) + '大' (big).

examples.chinese: 昨天下了场特大的雨。
examples.pinyin: Zuótiān xiàle chǎng tè dà de yǔ.
examples.english: There was an exceptionally heavy rain yesterday.

examples.chinese: 我需要一个特大号的T恤。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xūyào yī gè tè dà hào de T xù.
examples.english: I need an extra large T-shirt.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for weather, sizes, news events ('特大新闻'), etc.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A '特' (special) '快' (fast) train or service.
vocabulary.etymology: Literal combination: '特' (special) + '快' (fast).

examples.chinese: 我坐特快列车去北京。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuò tèkuài lièchē qù Běijīng.
examples.english: I'm taking the express train to Beijing.

examples.chinese: 这是特快专递。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì tèkuài zhuāndì.
examples.english: This is express mail.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly refers to a class of Chinese trains (T-trains) or express mail services.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Very similar to '特地', focusing on special '意' (intention).
vocabulary.etymology: '特' (special) + '意' (intention).

examples.chinese: 这是我特意给你留的蛋糕。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ tèyì gěi nǐ liú de dàngāo.
examples.english: This is the cake I specially saved for you.

examples.chinese: 他不是特意迟到的。
examples.pinyin: Tā bùshì tèyì chídào de.
examples.english: He wasn't deliberately late.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Almost interchangeable with '特地'. '特意' might emphasize the thought/intention slightly more.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Originally meant sacrificing an animal (犠) for a ceremony (牲). Now means personal sacrifice.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally complex characters: '犠' refers to a sacrificial ox, '牲' refers to a sacrificial animal. Combined, it meant ritual animal sacrifice.

examples.chinese: 他牺牲了休息时间来完成工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā xīshēngle xiūxí shíjiān lái wánchéng gōngzuò.
examples.english: He sacrificed his rest time to finish the work.

examples.chinese: 为了和平，他们做出了巨大的牺牲。
examples.pinyin: Wèile hépíng, tāmen zuò chūle jùdà de xīshēng.
examples.english: For peace, they made a tremendous sacrifice.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A strong word, used for serious, often commendable sacrifices (time, life, interests).

vocabulary.mnemonic: The pictograph looks like a running dog. It's the formal/radical for 'dog' (like in '狗').
vocabulary.etymology: A pictograph of a dog. It is the semantic component in many characters related to animals (e.g., 狗, 狼, 猛).

examples.chinese: 那是一只训练有素的警犬。
examples.pinyin: Nà shì yī zhī xùnliàn yǒusù de jǐngquǎn.
examples.english: That is a well-trained police dog.

examples.chinese: 他家养了一只小犬。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiā yǎngle yī zhī xiǎo quǎn.
examples.english: His family keeps a small dog.

vocabulary.usage_notes: More formal or used in specific terms like '警犬' (police dog). '狗' is the everyday word.

vocabulary.english: to violate; to commit (crime); to offend
vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of a '犭' (dog/beast) going too far — it '犯'法 (breaks the law).
vocabulary.etymology: Composed of the 'dog/beast' radical (犭) and '㔾' which may represent something bent or transgressing.

examples.chinese: 他又犯老毛病了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòu fàn lǎo máobìng le.
examples.english: He's making his old mistake again.

examples.chinese: 你这样做会犯法的。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhèyàng zuò huì fànfǎ de.
examples.english: Doing this will break the law.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very common verb for making mistakes, breaking rules/laws, or recurring (bad habits).

vocabulary.mnemonic: '犯' (violate) the '罪' (guilt/sin) — that's committing a crime.
vocabulary.etymology: '犯' (to violate) + '罪' (crime/sin).

examples.chinese: 他因为犯罪被抓了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi fànzuì bèi zhuā le.
examples.english: He was arrested for committing a crime.

examples.chinese: 暴力犯罪是很可怕的。
examples.pinyin: Bàolì fànzuì shì hěn kěpà de.
examples.english: Violent crime is terrifying.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The standard term for 'to commit a crime' or 'crime' as an abstract concept.

vocabulary.english: to foul; to break the rules; foul
vocabulary.mnemonic: In sports, you '犯' (violate) the '规' (rules) and get a yellow card.
vocabulary.etymology: '犯' (to violate) + '规' (rules/regulations).

examples.chinese: 那个球员又犯规了。
examples.pinyin: Nà gè qiúyuán yòu fànguī le.
examples.english: That player fouled again.

examples.chinese: 这是技术犯规。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì jìshù fànguī.
examples.english: This is a technical foul.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Primarily used in sports and games. Can be used metaphorically.

vocabulary.english: ruthless; fierce; to a severe degree
vocabulary.mnemonic: A wild animal ('犭') being '狠' — think of a vicious wolf.
vocabulary.etymology: Composed of the 'dog/beast' radical (犭) and '艮' which may imply stubbornness or limit, giving a sense of ferocity.

examples.chinese: 他对敌人特别狠。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì dírén tèbié hěn.
examples.english: He is especially ruthless towards his enemies.

examples.chinese: 我昨天狠睡了一觉。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān hěn shuìle yī jiào.
examples.english: I slept really heavily yesterday.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can describe a person's character (ruthless) or, colloquially, emphasize the degree of an action ('狠睡' = sleep deeply).

vocabulary.mnemonic: A '狠' (ruthless) '心' (heart). Having the heart to do something harsh.
vocabulary.etymology: '狠' (ruthless) + '心' (heart/mind).

examples.chinese: 他狠心拒绝了她的请求。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěnxīn jùjuéle tā de qǐngqiú.
examples.english: He cruelly rejected her request. / He hardened his heart and rejected her request.

examples.chinese: 别这么狠心嘛！
examples.pinyin: Bié zhème hěnxīn ma!
examples.english: Don't be so heartless!

vocabulary.usage_notes: Describes a person or an action that shows a lack of mercy. Can be a verb phrase '狠下心来'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: One person '独' (alone) makes the '裁' (decisions/judgments) — that's a dictatorship.
vocabulary.etymology: '独' (alone/single) + '裁' (to cut/to judge/to decide). Implies single-person rule.

examples.chinese: 那个国家过去是军事独裁。
examples.pinyin: Nàge guójiā guòqù shì jūnshì dú cái.
examples.english: That country used to be a military dictatorship.

examples.chinese: 他有一个独裁的性格。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu yī gè dú cái de xìnggé.
examples.english: He has an autocratic personality.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A political term with a strong negative connotation.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of a '犭' (beast) like a tiger being '猛' — fierce and sudden!
vocabulary.etymology: Composed of the 'dog/beast' radical (犭) and '孟' (which may imply eldest/vigorous), giving a sense of fierceness.

examples.chinese: 风刮得很猛。
examples.pinyin: Fēng guā de hěn měng.
examples.english: The wind is blowing fiercely.

examples.chinese: 他猛地站了起来。
examples.pinyin: Tā měng de zhànle qǐlái.
examples.english: He stood up suddenly/vigorously.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can describe force (wind, attack), animals, or sudden actions ('猛地').

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of compiling staff 'ranks' (制) with pen and paper (编).
vocabulary.etymology: 编 (biān, 'to weave, compile') + 制 (zhì, 'system, control'). Originally referred to weaving bamboo strips into a 'system', now extended to organizing personnel or plans.

examples.chinese: 我们部门正在编制明年的预算。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bùmén zhèngzài biānzhì míngnián de yùsuàn.
examples.english: Our department is compiling next year's budget.

examples.chinese: 这个岗位已经超编制了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè gǎngwèi yǐjīng chāo biānzhì le.
examples.english: This position is already over the authorized staffing limit.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As a verb, often used for plans, reports, budgets. As a noun, often refers to the official quota of personnel.

vocabulary.mnemonic: You 'weave' (织) something with your fingers (扌 in 编).
vocabulary.etymology: 编 (biān, 'to plait, arrange') + 织 (zhī, 'to weave'). Both characters relate to intertwining threads.

examples.chinese: 我奶奶会编织漂亮的毛衣。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ nǎinai huì biānzhī piàoliang de máoyī.
examples.english: My grandma can knit beautiful sweaters.

examples.chinese: 别听他瞎说，他就是在编织谎言。
examples.pinyin: Bié tīng tā xiāshuō, tā jiùshì zài biānzhī huǎngyán.
examples.english: Don't listen to his nonsense, he's just weaving lies.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for both literal knitting/crocheting and figurative 'weaving' (e.g., stories, dreams).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of 'the original (缘) story (故)' behind something.
vocabulary.etymology: 缘 (yuán, 'cause, edge') + 故 (gù, 'reason, old'). Together meaning 'the originating reason'.

examples.chinese: 不知道什么缘故，他突然生气了。
examples.pinyin: Bù zhīdào shénme yuángù, tā túrán shēngqì le.
examples.english: For some reason, he suddenly got angry.

examples.chinese: 他今天没来，可能是生病的缘故。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīntiān méi lái, kěnéng shì shēngbìng de yuángù.
examples.english: He didn't come today, probably because he's sick.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in patterns '...的缘故' or '不知什么缘故'. Slightly more formal than 原因 in daily speech.

vocabulary.english: to twine; to entangle; to bother
vocabulary.mnemonic: Picture vines 'winding' (缠) around something and 'wrapping' (绕) it up.
vocabulary.etymology: 缠 (chán, 'to wind around, pester') + 绕 (rào, 'to wind, coil'). Both characters have the 'silk' radical (纟), indicating thread-like action.

examples.chinese: 藤蔓缠绕着那棵老树。
examples.pinyin: Téngmàn chánrào zhe nà kē lǎo shù.
examples.english: Vines are twining around that old tree.

examples.chinese: 这个问题一直缠绕在我心里。
examples.pinyin: Zhège wèntí yīzhí chánrào zài wǒ xīnlǐ.
examples.english: This problem has been bothering me constantly.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be used for physical tangling or metaphorical worries 'entangling' the mind.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Something is 'lacking' (缺) and has a visible 'flaw' (陷 like a pitfall).
vocabulary.etymology: 缺 (quē, 'lack, be short of') + 陷 (xiàn, 'pitfall, defect'). A 'lack' that is a 'pitfall'.

examples.chinese: 这款手机的设计有个小缺陷。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuǎn shǒujī de shèjì yǒu gè xiǎo quēxiàn.
examples.english: There's a minor flaw in this phone's design.

examples.chinese: 每个人都有自己的缺陷，这很正常。
examples.pinyin: Měi gè rén dōu yǒu zìjǐ de quēxiàn, zhè hěn zhèngcháng.
examples.english: Everyone has their own shortcomings, that's normal.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for products, systems, or character flaws. More formal than 毛病.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A 'net' (网) 'bar' (吧) where you drink internet instead of coffee.
vocabulary.etymology: 网 (wǎng, 'net, internet') + 吧 (bā, transliteration of 'bar'). A hybrid Chinese-English word.

examples.chinese: 大学旁边总有好几家网吧。
examples.pinyin: Dàxué pángbiān zǒng yǒu hǎo jǐ jiā wǎngbā.
examples.english: There are always several internet cafes near the university.

examples.chinese: 我们以前常去网吧打游戏。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yǐqián cháng qù wǎngbā dǎ yóuxì.
examples.english: We used to often go to internet cafes to play games.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A 'net' (网) 'page' (页).
vocabulary.etymology: 网 (wǎng, 'net, internet') + 页 (yè, 'page, leaf'). A direct calque.

examples.chinese: 这个网页加载得太慢了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège wǎngyè jiāzǎi de tài màn le.
examples.english: This web page loads too slowly.

examples.chinese: 你把那个网页的链接发给我吧。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bǎ nàge wǎngyè de liànjiē fā gěi wǒ ba.
examples.english: Send me the link to that web page.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of waving a hand and saying 'Bà le' - 'Ah, forget it, let it go.'
vocabulary.etymology: 罢 (bà, 'stop, cease') + 了 (le, modal particle). Literally 'let it stop'.

examples.chinese: 我不过是开个玩笑罢了，别当真。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ búguò shì kāi gè wánxiào bàle, bié dàngzhēn.
examples.english: I was merely joking, don't take it seriously.

examples.chinese: 他不去也罢，我们自己去吧。
examples.pinyin: Tā bú qù yě bà, wǒmen zìjǐ qù ba.
examples.english: If he's not going, so be it, let's go ourselves.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used at the end of a sentence to downplay importance, similar to '...而已'. Often in patterns '不过是...罢了' or '...也罢'.

vocabulary.english: to go on strike; a strike
vocabulary.mnemonic: Workers 'stop' (罢) 'working' (工).
vocabulary.etymology: 罢 (bà, 'stop, cease') + 工 (gōng, 'work, labor'). To cease work.

examples.chinese: 工人们为了涨工资开始罢工了。
examples.pinyin: Gōngrénmen wèile zhǎng gōngzī kāishǐ bàgōng le.
examples.english: The workers have gone on strike for a raise.

examples.chinese: 这次罢工持续了整整一周。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì bàgōng chíxù le zhěngzhěng yī zhōu.
examples.english: This strike lasted a whole week.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used as a verb-noun: 举行罢工 (hold a strike), 开始罢工 (start a strike).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Picture a 'net' (罒) over 'non' (非), capturing wrongdoing.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted a net (罒) capturing a 'non-conforming' (非) person, i.e., a criminal. The modern form is a simplification.

examples.chinese: 他犯了什么罪？
examples.pinyin: Tā fàn le shénme zuì?
examples.english: What crime did he commit?

examples.chinese: 我心里一点罪过感都没有。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xīnlǐ yīdiǎn zuìguò gǎn dōu méiyǒu.
examples.english: I don't feel any guilt at all.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A core character forming many related words (e.g., 犯罪, 罪犯, 罪恶). Can refer to legal crimes or moral sins.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The combination of 'crime/sin' (罪) and 'evil' (恶).
vocabulary.etymology: 罪 (zuì, 'crime, sin') + 恶 (è, 'evil, bad'). The essence of serious wrongdoing.

examples.chinese: 这部电影揭露了战争的罪恶。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng jiēlù le zhànzhēng de zuì'è.
examples.english: This movie exposes the evils of war.

examples.chinese: 他最终为自己犯下的罪恶付出了代价。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuìzhōng wèi zìjǐ fàn xià de zuì'è fùchū le dàijià.
examples.english: He finally paid the price for the sins he committed.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Stronger and more abstract than 罪 alone, referring to the nature of evil or grave sinfulness.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 'Beautifying' (美) your 'appearance' (容).
vocabulary.etymology: 美 (měi, 'beautiful') + 容 (róng, 'appearance, face'). To make the appearance beautiful.

examples.chinese: 她每周都去做美容。
examples.pinyin: Tā měi zhōu dōu qù zuò měiróng.
examples.english: She goes for beauty treatments every week.

examples.chinese: 这家美容院的口碑很好。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā měiróngyuàn de kǒubēi hěn hǎo.
examples.english: This beauty salon has a very good reputation.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in compounds: 美容院 (beauty salon), 做美容 (get a beauty treatment).

vocabulary.mnemonic: A sheep (羊) is 'ashamed' (羞) and 'stops' (止) in its tracks.
vocabulary.etymology: 羞 (xiū, 'shy, ashamed', originally depicted offering a sheep) + 耻 (chǐ, 'disgrace, shame', combines 'ear' 耳 and 'heart' 心, implying something that makes ears hot and heart uneasy).

examples.chinese: 他作弊被抓住，感到非常羞耻。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuòbì bèi zhuāzhù, gǎndào fēicháng xiūchǐ.
examples.english: He was caught cheating and felt deeply ashamed.

examples.chinese: 这没什么好羞耻的，大胆说出来。
examples.pinyin: Zhè méi shénme hǎo xiūchǐ de, dàdǎn shuō chūlái.
examples.english: There's nothing to be ashamed of, say it boldly.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A strong word for deep shame. 感到羞耻 (feel ashamed), 不知羞耻 (shameless).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Looks like a person (羽) standing on a field (田) with wings spread.
vocabulary.etymology: Pictograph of a bird's wings. The modern character combines 羽 (yǔ, 'feather') with other elements indicating sound/symbolism.

examples.chinese: 小鸟受伤了，一只翼不能动。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo niǎo shòushāng le, yī zhī yì bù néng dòng.
examples.english: The little bird is injured, one wing can't move.

examples.chinese: 这家公司是集团的重要左翼。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī shì jítuán de zhòngyào zuǒyì.
examples.english: This company is an important left wing of the conglomerate.

vocabulary.usage_notes: More formal/literary than 翅膀. Also used in political (左翼/右翼) and geometric terms (机翼 - airplane wing).

vocabulary.english: fellow townsman; someone from the same hometown
vocabulary.mnemonic: An 'old' (老) acquaintance from your 'hometown' (乡).
vocabulary.etymology: 老 (lǎo, 'old') + 乡 (xiāng, 'hometown, countryside'). An 'old hometown' person.

examples.chinese: 在外地遇到一个老乡，感觉特别亲切。
examples.pinyin: Zài wàidì yù dào yī gè lǎoxiāng, gǎnjué tèbié qīnqiè.
examples.english: Meeting someone from my hometown while away feels especially warm.

examples.chinese: 嘿，老乡，你也是山东来的？
examples.pinyin: Hēi, lǎoxiāng, nǐ yě shì Shāndōng lái de?
examples.english: Hey, fellow townsman, are you also from Shandong?

vocabulary.usage_notes: A friendly, colloquial term. Can be used as a direct form of address.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 'Examining' (考) 'ancient' (古) things.
vocabulary.etymology: 考 (kǎo, 'to examine, test') + 古 (gǔ, 'ancient'). To examine ancient things.

examples.chinese: 他大学学的是考古专业。
examples.pinyin: Tā dàxué xué de shì kǎogǔ zhuānyè.
examples.english: He majored in archaeology in university.

examples.chinese: 最近在河边发现了一处重要的考古遗址。
examples.pinyin: Zuìjìn zài hébiān fāxiàn le yī chù zhòngyào de kǎogǔ yízhǐ.
examples.english: An important archaeological site was recently discovered by the river.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'field' (场) where you take an 'exam' (考).
vocabulary.etymology: 考 (kǎo, 'exam, test') + 场 (chǎng, 'field, ground, venue'). The venue for exams.

examples.chinese: 请提前15分钟进入考场。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng tíqián 15 fēnzhōng jìnrù kǎochǎng.
examples.english: Please enter the examination hall 15 minutes early.

examples.chinese: 考场上安静得能听见针掉在地上的声音。
examples.pinyin: Kǎochǎng shàng ānjìng de néng tīng jiàn zhēn diào zài dìshang de shēngyīn.
examples.english: It was so quiet in the exam room you could hear a pin drop.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'topic' (题) of an 'exam' (考).
vocabulary.etymology: 考 (kǎo, 'exam, test') + 题 (tí, 'topic, question'). Exam topic/question.

examples.chinese: 最后一道考题太难了，我没答出来。
examples.pinyin: Zuìhòu yī dào kǎotí tài nán le, wǒ méi dá chūlái.
examples.english: The last exam question was too hard, I couldn't answer it.

examples.chinese: 这次的考题出得很灵活。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì de kǎotí chū de hěn línghuó.
examples.english: This time's exam questions were set very flexibly.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can refer to a single question or the whole set of questions.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It can 'withstand' (耐) 'use' (用) for a long time.
vocabulary.etymology: 耐 (nài, 'to endure, withstand') + 用 (yòng, 'to use'). Able to endure use.

examples.chinese: 这个牌子的手机特别耐用。
examples.pinyin: Zhège páizi de shǒujī tèbié nàiyòng.
examples.english: Phones of this brand are especially durable.

examples.chinese: 买家具要选耐用一点的。
examples.pinyin: Mǎi jiājù yào xuǎn nàiyòng yīdiǎn de.
examples.english: When buying furniture, choose something more durable.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used to describe appliances, furniture, clothing, etc. 很耐用 (very durable).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 'Ear' (耳) 'ring' (环).
vocabulary.etymology: 耳 (ěr, 'ear') + 环 (huán, 'ring, hoop'). A ring for the ear.

examples.chinese: 她戴了一对很闪的耳环。
examples.pinyin: Tā dài le yī duì hěn shǎn de ěrhuán.
examples.english: She is wearing a pair of very shiny earrings.

examples.chinese: 我好像丢了一只耳环。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hǎoxiàng diū le yī zhī ěrhuán.
examples.english: I think I've lost one earring.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Pair is 一对耳环, single one is 一只耳环.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A person (从) with two raised 'ears' (耳) shrugging.
vocabulary.etymology: From 聳 (sǒng). Combines elements suggesting 'ears' and 'standing tall'. The simplified form 耸 is phonetic (从 cóng) with meaning components.

examples.chinese: 他耸了耸肩，表示不知道。
examples.pinyin: Tā sǒng le sǒng jiān, biǎoshì bù zhīdào.
examples.english: He shrugged his shoulders to indicate he didn't know.

examples.chinese: 远处耸立着几座高山。
examples.pinyin: Yuǎnchù sǒnglì zhe jǐ zuò gāo shān.
examples.english: Several tall mountains tower in the distance.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common in 耸耸肩 (shrug one's shoulders) and 耸立 (to tower aloft).

vocabulary.english: to chat; merely (in 无聊, etc.)
vocabulary.mnemonic: Friends chat using their 'ears' (耳).
vocabulary.etymology: Originally related to the ear (耳). The modern meaning 'chat' may derive from the idea of listening and talking.

examples.chinese: 周末我们一起吃饭聊聊吧。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen yīqǐ chīfàn liáo liáo ba.
examples.english: Let's get together for a meal and chat this weekend.

examples.chinese: 这本书无聊透了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū wúliáo tòu le.
examples.english: This book is utterly boring.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Core verb for informal chatting. Also appears in 无聊 (boring), 聊天 (to chat).

vocabulary.english: to chat; to have a chat
vocabulary.mnemonic: 'Chat' (聊) about 'heaven' (天) and earth - just talk casually.
vocabulary.etymology: 聊 (liáo, 'chat') + 天 (tiān, 'sky, day') + 儿 (ér, retroflex suffix). Literally 'chatting about the skies', i.e., casual talk.

examples.chinese: 我们经常在微信上聊天儿。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen jīngcháng zài Wēixìn shàng liáotiānr.
examples.english: We often chat on WeChat.

examples.chinese: 过来坐坐，聊聊天儿。
examples.pinyin: Guòlái zuò zuò, liáo liáo tiānr.
examples.english: Come over, sit down, and have a chat.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The quintessential word for casual, informal chatting. The 儿化音 (érhuàyīn) is common in Northern Mandarin.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'dragon' (龙 in 聋) has no ears, the 'dumb' (亚 in 哑) has no voice.
vocabulary.etymology: 聋 (lóng, 'deaf', combines 'dragon' 龙 for sound and 'ear' 耳 for meaning) + 哑 (yǎ, 'mute', combines 'mouth' 口 and something that restricts).

examples.chinese: 这所学校是为聋哑儿童开设的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè suǒ xuéxiào shì wèi lóngyǎ értóng kāishè de.
examples.english: This school is set up for deaf and mute children.

examples.chinese: 他通过学习手语来帮助聋哑人。
examples.pinyin: Tā tōngguò xuéxí shǒuyǔ lái bāngzhù lóngyǎ rén.
examples.english: He helps deaf-mute people by learning sign language.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be used as an adjective (聋哑儿童) or noun (聋哑人). Modern, respectful terms are 听障 (hearing impaired) and 语障 (speech impaired).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Your 'post/role' (职) and the 'responsibility' (责) that comes with it.
vocabulary.etymology: 职 (zhí, 'duty, post') + 责 (zé, 'responsibility, blame'). The responsibilities of one's post.

examples.chinese: 保护客户的安全是我们的职责。
examples.pinyin: Bǎohù kèhù de ānquán shì wǒmen de zhízé.
examples.english: Protecting our clients' safety is our duty.

examples.chinese: 他非常清楚自己的职责是什么。
examples.pinyin: Tā fēicháng qīngchǔ zìjǐ de zhízé shì shénme.
examples.english: He is very clear about what his responsibilities are.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Formal, often used in professional or official contexts. 履行职责 (fulfill one's duties).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine someone STIR-FRYING (炒) a story in a PAN to make it BIGGER and HOTTER – that's 'hype'!
vocabulary.etymology: 炒 (chǎo) 'to stir-fry', here meaning to process something intensely for effect; 作 (zuò) 'to make, to do'. Combined, it means to deliberately 'cook up' attention.

examples.chinese: 这个新闻完全是为了吸引眼球的炒作。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge xīnwén wánquán shì wèile xīyǐn yǎnqiú de chǎozuò.
examples.english: This news story is completely a hype to attract attention.

examples.chinese: 别信，那只是明星的炒作手段。
examples.pinyin: Bié xìn, nà zhǐshì míngxīng de chǎozuò shǒuduàn.
examples.english: Don't believe it, that's just a celebrity's hype tactic.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often has a slightly negative connotation, implying the hype is artificial or excessive.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Picture yourself in a hot kitchen STIR-FRYING (炒) SHARES (股) in a wok, trying to make them sizzle with profit.
vocabulary.etymology: 炒 (chǎo) 'to stir-fry', used metaphorically for rapid trading; 股 (gǔ) 'share, stock'. Refers to the active, speculative buying and selling of stocks.

examples.chinese: 他最近辞职在家专职炒股。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuìjìn cízhí zài jiā zhuānzhí chǎogǔ.
examples.english: He recently quit his job to trade stocks full-time at home.

examples.chinese: 炒股有风险，入市需谨慎。
examples.pinyin: Chǎogǔ yǒu fēngxiǎn, rùshì xū jǐnshèn.
examples.english: Stock trading has risks; enter the market with caution.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Colloquial verb-object phrase. Can be separated, e.g., '炒了几只股' (traded a few stocks).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of 'BAO' as a quick BURST of boiling water to blanch something.
vocabulary.etymology: This reading (bāo) is specific to cooking. The character 炮 (火 'fire' + 包 'to wrap') originally meant 'to roast meat wrapped in mud'. The cooking method evolved to mean quick boiling.

examples.chinese: 把菠菜放水里炮一下再凉拌。
examples.pinyin: Bǎ bōcài fàng shuǐ lǐ bāo yíxià zài liángbàn.
examples.english: Quick-boil the spinach in water before making the cold salad.

examples.chinese: 做这道菜要先炮肉片。
examples.pinyin: Zuò zhè dào cài yào xiān bāo ròupiàn.
examples.english: To make this dish, you need to parboil the meat slices first.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A specific cooking term (read as bāo), different from the more common pào (cannon).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Read it as 'ZHÁ' and think of the SIZZLING sound (zhá zhá zhá) in a wok full of hot oil.
vocabulary.etymology: 炸 (火 'fire' + 乍 'suddenly'). The reading zhá is specifically for the cooking method of deep-frying, where food is suddenly immersed in hot oil.

examples.chinese: 我妈炸的春卷特别好吃。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ mā zhá de chūnjuǎn tèbié hǎochī.
examples.english: The spring rolls my mom deep-fries are especially delicious.

examples.chinese: 晚上我们炸点儿鸡翅吃吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǎnshang wǒmen zhá diǎnr jīchì chī ba.
examples.english: Let's deep-fry some chicken wings for dinner.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The cooking verb is pronounced zhá. It's different from zhà (to explode).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 炸 (explode) + 弹 (projectile) = A projectile that EXPLODES.
vocabulary.etymology: 炸 (zhà) 'to explode'; 弹 (dàn) 'bullet, projectile'. Literally, an 'exploding projectile'.

examples.chinese: 电影里主角拆除了炸弹。
examples.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ zhǔjué chāichú le zhàdàn.
examples.english: In the movie, the protagonist defused the bomb.

examples.chinese: 那个消息像个重磅炸弹。
examples.pinyin: Nà ge xiāoxi xiàng ge zhòngbàng zhàdàn.
examples.english: That news was like a bombshell.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Also used metaphorically for shocking news ('news bomb').

vocabulary.mnemonic: The MEDICINE/AGENT (药) that makes things EXPLODE (炸).
vocabulary.etymology: 炸 (zhà) 'to explode'; 药 (yào) 'medicine, chemical agent'. The 'chemical agent for exploding'.

examples.chinese: 工人们在矿山使用炸药。
examples.pinyin: Gōngrén men zài kuàngshān shǐyòng zhàyào.
examples.english: The workers use explosives at the mine.

examples.chinese: 运输炸药需要特殊许可。
examples.pinyin: Yùnshū zhàyào xūyào tèshū xǔkě.
examples.english: Transporting explosives requires a special permit.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to the explosive material itself, not the assembled device (which is 炸弹).

vocabulary.english: to bake; to dry by heat
vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine a FIRE (火) providing warmth ALL AROUND (共) to bake bread.
vocabulary.etymology: 烘 (火 'fire' + 共 'together, all around'). Depicts heat being applied evenly from all sides.

examples.chinese: 用烤箱烘饼干要二十分钟。
examples.pinyin: Yòng kǎoxiāng hōng bǐnggān yào èrshí fēnzhōng.
examples.english: It takes twenty minutes to bake cookies in the oven.

examples.chinese: 下雨了，我把湿衣服烘一下。
examples.pinyin: Xià yǔ le, wǒ bǎ shī yīfu hōng yíxià.
examples.english: It's raining, I'll dry the wet clothes with some heat.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for baking food or drying clothes/appliances (e.g., 烘干机 dryer).

vocabulary.mnemonic: It's like SMOKE (烟) made of FLOWERS (花) in the sky.
vocabulary.etymology: 烟 (yān) 'smoke, mist'; 花 (huā) 'flower'. The 'smoke flowers' that bloom in the night sky.

examples.chinese: 除夕夜我们一家人去看烟花。
examples.pinyin: Chúxī yè wǒmen yì jiā rén qù kàn yānhuā.
examples.english: On New Year's Eve, our whole family goes to watch the fireworks.

examples.chinese: 禁止在市区内燃放烟花。
examples.pinyin: Jìnzhǐ zài shìqū nèi ránfàng yānhuā.
examples.english: Setting off fireworks is prohibited within the city limits.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can also refer to 'prostitute' in classical/literary context, but the primary modern meaning is fireworks.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Exactly what it says: 热 (hot) + 水 (water).
vocabulary.etymology: 热 (rè) 'hot'; 水 (shuǐ) 'water'. A straightforward compound.

examples.chinese: 感冒了要多喝热水。
examples.pinyin: Gǎnmào le yào duō hē rèshuǐ.
examples.english: You should drink more hot water when you have a cold.

examples.chinese: 小心，这壶热水很烫！
examples.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn, zhè hú rèshuǐ hěn tàng!
examples.english: Be careful, this pot of hot water is very scalding!

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very common daily term. 开水 means 'boiled water' (safe to drink), while 热水 can be any hot water.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The DEVICE (器) that makes HOT WATER (热水).
vocabulary.etymology: 热水 (rèshuǐ) 'hot water' + 器 (qì) 'device, appliance'.

examples.chinese: 我家新装了燃气热水器。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā xīn zhuāng le ránqì rèshuǐqì.
examples.english: We just had a gas water heater installed at home.

examples.chinese: 热水器坏了，洗不了澡。
examples.pinyin: Rèshuǐqì huài le, xǐ bù liǎo zǎo.
examples.english: The water heater is broken, I can't take a shower.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common types: 电热水器 (electric), 燃气热水器 (gas), 太阳能热水器 (solar).

vocabulary.mnemonic: HOT TEARS (热泪) FILLING (盈) the EYE SOCKETS (眶) to the brim.
vocabulary.etymology: 热泪 (rè lèi) 'hot tears'; 盈 (yíng) 'to be full of'; 眶 (kuàng) 'eye socket'. Describes being deeply moved.

examples.chinese: 听到那个故事，我感动得热泪盈眶。
examples.pinyin: Tīng dào nà ge gùshi, wǒ gǎndòng de rè lèi yíng kuàng.
examples.english: Hearing that story moved me to the point of tears welling up in my eyes.

examples.chinese: 他领奖时热泪盈眶，说不出话。
examples.pinyin: Tā lǐng jiǎng shí rè lèi yíng kuàng, shuō bù chū huà.
examples.english: When he received the award, his eyes filled with tears and he couldn't speak.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used to describe being overwhelmingly touched, happy, or sad. A very vivid emotional expression.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A hot (热) point (点) of attention, like a trending topic on social media.
vocabulary.etymology: 热 (rè) 'hot'; 点 (diǎn) 'point, spot'. A point of concentrated activity or attention.

examples.chinese: 这条微博成了今天的网络热点。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo wēibó chéng le jīntiān de wǎngluò rèdiǎn.
examples.english: This Weibo post became today's online hot topic.

examples.chinese: 那个咖啡馆是年轻人的社交热点。
examples.pinyin: Nà ge kāfēiguǎn shì niánqīng rén de shèjiāo rèdiǎn.
examples.english: That cafe is a hot social spot for young people.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can refer to physical places (tourist hot spot) or abstract topics (news hot spot).

vocabulary.mnemonic: A 'hot' (热) telephone LINE (线) for urgent or direct communication.
vocabulary.etymology: 热 (rè) 'hot'; 线 (xiàn) 'line, wire'.

examples.chinese: 消费者投诉请拨打12315热线。
examples.pinyin: Xiāofèizhě tóusù qǐng bōdǎ yāo èr sān yāo wǔ rèxiàn.
examples.english: For consumer complaints, please call the 12315 hotline.

examples.chinese: 两国领导人之间设有热线。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng guó lǐngdǎo rén zhī jiān shè yǒu rèxiàn.
examples.english: There is a hotline between the leaders of the two countries.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used for customer service, emergency, or direct communication lines.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 亨 (enjoy) + 饪 (food preparation) = The art of preparing food to be ENJOYED.
vocabulary.etymology: 烹 (pēng) originally meant 'to boil meat'; 饪 (rèn) 'to cook food until done'. Combined, it means the art of cooking.

examples.chinese: 我对烹饪很感兴趣，经常看美食节目。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ duì pēngrèn hěn gǎn xìngqù, jīngcháng kàn měishí jiémù.
examples.english: I'm very interested in cooking and often watch food shows.

examples.chinese: 他报名参加了烹饪课程。
examples.pinyin: Tā bàomíng cānjiā le pēngrèn kèchéng.
examples.english: He signed up for a cooking class.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Slightly more formal than 做饭. Can be used as a noun ('Chinese cuisine' 中国烹饪) or verb.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The BURNING (焦) POINT (点) where all attention or light converges.
vocabulary.etymology: 焦 (jiāo) 'burnt, scorched', related to intense heat or concentration; 点 (diǎn) 'point'. A point of concentrated energy or attention.

examples.chinese: 这次会议的焦点是环境保护。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì huìyì de jiāodiǎn shì huánjìng bǎohù.
examples.english: The focus of this meeting is environmental protection.

examples.chinese: 她一下子成了全场关注的焦点。
examples.pinyin: Tā yíxiàzi chéng le quán chǎng guānzhù de jiāodiǎn.
examples.english: She instantly became the focus of attention for the entire room.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used in both literal (physics, photography) and figurative (attention, discussion) contexts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: SHINE (照) upon someone and RESPOND (应) to their needs – to look after them.
vocabulary.etymology: 照 (zhào) 'to shine on, to illuminate'; 应 (yìng) 'to respond, to correspond'. To 'shine upon and respond to', i.e., to take care of or coordinate.

examples.chinese: 我出差时，麻烦你照应一下我家的猫。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ chūchāi shí, máfan nǐ zhàoyìng yíxià wǒ jiā de māo.
examples.english: Could you please look after my cat while I'm on a business trip?

examples.chinese: 文章的开头和结尾要互相照应。
examples.pinyin: Wénzhāng de kāitóu hé jiéwěi yào hùxiāng zhàoyìng.
examples.english: The beginning and end of an article should coordinate with each other.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often pronounced as 'zhào yìng'. It means 'to take care of' someone or 'to coordinate/eho' in writing.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Following the SAME PATTERN (样) you USED TO (照).
vocabulary.etymology: 照 (zhào) 'according to, in accordance with'; 样 (yàng) 'manner, pattern'. 'According to the same pattern'.

examples.chinese: 虽然下雨了，我们照样去公园。
examples.pinyin: Suīrán xià yǔ le, wǒmen zhàoyàng qù gōngyuán.
examples.english: Even though it's raining, we're going to the park all the same.

examples.chinese: 别管他，你照样做你的工作。
examples.pinyin: Bié guǎn tā, nǐ zhàoyàng zuò nǐ de gōngzuò.
examples.english: Don't mind him, just do your work as usual.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used to indicate that something continues or happens despite changed circumstances.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The sun SHINES (照) BRIGHTLY (耀), lighting up everything.
vocabulary.etymology: 照 (zhào) 'to shine on'; 耀 (yào) 'to shine brightly, to dazzle'. Emphasizes bright, radiant shining.

examples.chinese: 温暖的阳光照耀着大地。
examples.pinyin: Wēnnuǎn de yángguāng zhàoyào zhe dàdì.
examples.english: The warm sunshine shines upon the earth.

examples.chinese: 他的笑容像阳光一样照耀着我。
examples.pinyin: Tā de xiàoróng xiàng yángguāng yíyàng zhàoyào zhe wǒ.
examples.english: His smile shines upon me like sunshine.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in a poetic or descriptive context for light sources (sun, moon, lights) or metaphorically for positive influence.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Picture a CHEF (者) by the FIRE (灬火) boiling something in a pot.
vocabulary.etymology: 煮 (者 'person/this' + 灬火 'fire'). The modern form suggests 'this' (method) with 'fire' – to cook with fire, typically involving liquid.

examples.chinese: 我煮了点儿粥当早餐。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhǔ le diǎnr zhōu dàng zǎocān.
examples.english: I boiled some congee for breakfast.

examples.chinese: 水开了，可以煮饺子了。
examples.pinyin: Shuǐ kāi le, kěyǐ zhǔ jiǎozi le.
examples.english: The water is boiling, we can cook the dumplings now.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The most common verb for boiling food in water (noodles, eggs, soup).

vocabulary.mnemonic: The breath (息) makes the fire (灭) go OUT.
vocabulary.etymology: 熄 (xī) 'to extinguish'; 灭 (miè) 'to die out, to destroy'. A synonym compound meaning to put out a fire/light.

examples.chinese: 出门前记得把蜡烛熄灭。
examples.pinyin: Chūmén qián jìde bǎ làzhú xīmiè.
examples.english: Remember to blow out the candles before going out.

examples.chinese: 篝火慢慢熄灭了。
examples.pinyin: Gōuhuǒ mànmàn xīmiè le.
examples.english: The bonfire slowly went out.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be transitive (to extinguish sth) or intransitive (for a fire/light to go out by itself).

vocabulary.mnemonic: You need a HAND (尉) holding a hot object over CLOTH (巾) to iron it.
vocabulary.etymology: The character 熨 combines 尉 (an old official, implying pressure) and 火 (fire) in its seal form, representing the use of heat and pressure. The modern form 熨 (yù) is specific to ironing.

examples.chinese: 我明天要穿这件衬衫，得先熨一下。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ míngtiān yào chuān zhè jiàn chènshān, děi xiān yù yíxià.
examples.english: I want to wear this shirt tomorrow, I need to iron it first.

examples.chinese: 你会熨裤子吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ huì yù kùzi ma?
examples.english: Can you iron pants?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Read as 'yù'. Often used with 熨斗 (yùndǒu, iron).

vocabulary.mnemonic: A VIOLENT (暴) FIRE (火) bursting out.
vocabulary.etymology: 爆 (火 'fire' + 暴 'violent, sudden'). Depicts a sudden, violent explosion or bursting of fire.

examples.chinese: 小心，那个气球要爆了！
examples.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn, nà ge qìqiú yào bào le!
examples.english: Be careful, that balloon is about to burst!

examples.chinese: 这条新闻在网上爆了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo xīnwén zài wǎngshàng bào le.
examples.english: This news story blew up online.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very versatile. Can mean literal explosion (爆胎 flat tire) or figurative popularity/sudden occurrence (火爆 popular, 爆料 to spill the beans).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Something EXPLODES (爆) and SENDS OUT (发), like a volcano.
vocabulary.etymology: 爆 (bào) 'to explode'; 发 (fā) 'to send out, to issue'. To erupt and send energy/force/matter outward.

examples.chinese: 两国之间爆发了战争。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng guó zhī jiān bàofā le zhànzhēng.
examples.english: War broke out between the two countries.

examples.chinese: 他突然爆发出一阵大笑。
examples.pinyin: Tā tūrán bàofā chū yí zhèn dàxiào.
examples.english: He suddenly burst out laughing.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for sudden, often large-scale events: wars, epidemics, volcanic eruptions, emotions, etc.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 爆 (explode) + 炸 (explode) – a double explosion!
vocabulary.etymology: 爆 (bào) 'to explode violently'; 炸 (zhà) 'to explode'. A synonym compound emphasizing a powerful explosion.

examples.chinese: 远处传来一声巨大的爆炸声。
examples.pinyin: Yuǎnchù chuánlái yì shēng jùdà de bàozhà shēng.
examples.english: A huge explosion sound came from the distance.

examples.chinese: 煤气泄漏可能会导致爆炸。
examples.pinyin: Méiqì xièlòu kěnéng huì dǎozhì bàozhà.
examples.english: A gas leak could cause an explosion.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The standard term for a violent, destructive explosion. Can be a verb or noun.

vocabulary.mnemonic: LOVE (爱) and place them on your HEAD (戴) – to hold in high esteem.
vocabulary.etymology: 爱 (ài) 'to love'; 戴 (dài) 'to wear (on the head), to support'. The image is of loving someone enough to lift them up and place them on your head, i.e., to revere.

examples.chinese: 这位老校长深受学生们的爱戴。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi lǎo xiàozhǎng shēn shòu xuésheng men de àidài.
examples.english: This old principal is deeply loved and respected by the students.

examples.chinese: 人民爱戴他们的领袖。
examples.pinyin: Rénmín àidài tāmen de lǐngxiù.
examples.english: The people love and respect their leader.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for respect towards esteemed figures like leaders, teachers, elders. Not used for romantic love or between peers.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of a '监' (supervisor) watching over the '督' (governance). Like a boss keeping an eye on things.
vocabulary.etymology: 监 (jiān) originally depicted someone looking into a water basin to see their reflection, meaning 'to oversee'. 督 (dū) combines '目' (eye) with '叔' (phonetic), meaning 'to supervise'.

examples.chinese: 老师要监督学生完成作业。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī yào jiāndū xuéshēng wánchéng zuòyè.
examples.english: The teacher needs to supervise the students completing their homework.

examples.chinese: 这个项目由他负责监督。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiàngmù yóu tā fùzé jiāndū.
examples.english: He is responsible for supervising this project.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be used as both a verb (监督工作) and a noun (接受监督).

vocabulary.mnemonic: You '盖' (cover) the paper with your '章' (seal/stamp). The final step to make it official.
vocabulary.etymology: 盖 (gài) means 'to cover' or 'lid'. 章 (zhāng) means 'seal' or 'stamp', derived from the idea of a patterned, official mark.

examples.chinese: 合同需要双方盖章才能生效。
examples.pinyin: Hétong xūyào shuāngfāng gàizhāng cáinéng shēngxiào.
examples.english: The contract needs to be stamped by both parties to take effect.

examples.chinese: 我去找经理盖个章。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ qù zhǎo jīnglǐ gài gè zhāng.
examples.english: I'm going to find the manager to get a stamp.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very common bureaucratic action. Often used in the pattern '盖个章'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Someone '盗' (steals) the original '版' (edition/copy). Like a pirate flag on a fake DVD.
vocabulary.etymology: 盗 (dào) means 'to steal' or 'robber'. 版 (bǎn) means 'edition', 'printing block', or 'version'.

examples.chinese: 这是盗版电影，画质很差。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì dàobǎn diànyǐng, huàzhì hěn chà.
examples.english: This is a pirated movie, the video quality is terrible.

examples.chinese: 买盗版软件可能会有病毒。
examples.pinyin: Mǎi dàobǎn ruǎnjiàn kěnéng huì yǒu bìngdú.
examples.english: Buying pirated software might give you a virus.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used for software, movies, books, and games. As an adjective: 盗版软件 (pirated software).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine a hawk '盘' (coiling) and '旋' (spinning) in the sky before it dives.
vocabulary.etymology: 盘 (pán) means 'tray', 'coil', or 'to curl'. 旋 (xuán) means 'to revolve', 'circle', or 'return'.

examples.chinese: 一只老鹰在天空中盘旋。
examples.pinyin: Yì zhī lǎoyīng zài tiānkōng zhōng pánxuán.
examples.english: An eagle is circling in the sky.

examples.chinese: 这个问题一直在我脑子里盘旋。
examples.pinyin: Zhège wèntí yìzhí zài wǒ nǎozi lǐ pánxuán.
examples.english: This problem has been circling in my mind.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used literally for things circling (birds, planes) and metaphorically for thoughts lingering.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A place that's '盛' (flourishing) in its '产' (production). Picture a basket overflowing with local fruit.
vocabulary.etymology: 盛 (shèng) means 'flourishing', 'abundant', or 'vigorous'. 产 (chǎn) means 'to produce' or 'give birth to'.

examples.chinese: 这个地区盛产茶叶。
examples.pinyin: Zhège dìqū shèngchǎn cháyè.
examples.english: This region abounds in tea production.

examples.chinese: 我的家乡盛产海鲜。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de jiāxiāng shèngchǎn hǎixiān.
examples.english: My hometown is rich in seafood.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Almost always used to describe regions or places and what they produce in large quantities.

vocabulary.mnemonic: An '盛' (overflowing) amount of '情' (feeling/warmth) from a host.
vocabulary.etymology: 盛 (shèng) means 'flourishing' or 'abundant'. 情 (qíng) means 'feeling', 'emotion', or 'sentiment'.

examples.chinese: 感谢你的盛情款待！
examples.pinyin: Gǎnxiè nǐ de shèngqíng kuǎndài!
examples.english: Thank you for your great hospitality!

examples.chinese: 他盛情邀请我去他家做客。
examples.pinyin: Tā shèngqíng yāoqǐng wǒ qù tā jiā zuòkè.
examples.english: He warmly invited me to be a guest at his home.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A formal and positive word, often used in phrases like '盛情难却' (hard to refuse such warm hospitality).

vocabulary.mnemonic: A trend that's '盛' (booming) and '行' (walking/going) everywhere. It's on fire!
vocabulary.etymology: 盛 (shèng) means 'flourishing' or 'vigorous'. 行 (xíng) means 'to walk', 'to go', or 'to be current'.

examples.chinese: 现在短视频非常盛行。
examples.pinyin: Xiànzài duǎn shìpín fēicháng shèngxíng.
examples.english: Short videos are very much in vogue now.

examples.chinese: 这种穿搭风格前几年很盛行。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng chuāndā fēnggé qián jǐ nián hěn shèngxíng.
examples.english: This fashion style was very popular a few years ago.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Describes trends, fashions, customs, or ideas that are widespread during a period.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A '人' (person) whose eyes are '盲' (blind).
vocabulary.etymology: 盲 (máng) combines '目' (eye) and '亡' (deceased/lost), indicating 'loss of sight'. 人 (rén) means 'person'.

examples.chinese: 这位盲人的听力特别敏锐。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi mángrén de tīnglì tèbié mǐnruì.
examples.english: This blind person's hearing is particularly sharp.

examples.chinese: 公共设施应该考虑盲人的需求。
examples.pinyin: Gōnggòng shèshī yīnggāi kǎolǜ mángrén de xūqiú.
examples.english: Public facilities should consider the needs of blind people.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The standard, respectful term. Avoid using '瞎子' which is impolite.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It '直' (straight) up '升' (rises/lifts) into the air. A flying '机' (machine).
vocabulary.etymology: 直 (zhí) means 'straight' or 'vertical'. 升 (shēng) means 'to rise' or 'ascend'. 机 (jī) means 'machine'.

examples.chinese: 救援队派来了直升机。
examples.pinyin: Jiùyuán duì pài lái le zhíshēngjī.
examples.english: The rescue team dispatched a helicopter.

examples.chinese: 我还没坐过直升机呢。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hái méi zuò guo zhíshēngjī ne.
examples.english: I haven't ridden in a helicopter yet.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The common word for helicopter. Sometimes shortened to '直升機' or just '直升' in casual speech.

vocabulary.mnemonic: You '盼' (hope) while '望' (gazing) into the distance, waiting for something good.
vocabulary.etymology: 盼 (pàn) combines '目' (eye) and '分' (to divide), implying 'eyes looking intently'. 望 (wàng) depicts a person standing on earth looking at the moon, meaning 'to gaze into the distance' or 'hope'.

examples.chinese: 我盼望暑假快点到来。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ pànwàng shǔjià kuài diǎn dàolái.
examples.english: I'm looking forward to summer vacation arriving soon.

examples.chinese: 父母盼望孩子健康成长。
examples.pinyin: Fùmǔ pànwàng háizi jiànkāng chéngzhǎng.
examples.english: Parents yearn for their children to grow up healthy.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Expresses a deep, earnest hope or longing, stronger than just '希望'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The '省' (province)'s main '会' (meeting/gathering) place. The big city where the province's government is.
vocabulary.etymology: 省 (shěng) means 'province'. 会 (huì) means 'gathering', 'meeting', or 'association'.

examples.chinese: 南京是江苏省的省会。
examples.pinyin: Nánjīng shì Jiāngsū Shěng de shěnghuì.
examples.english: Nanjing is the capital of Jiangsu Province.

examples.chinese: 我们开车去省会办事。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen kāi chē qù shěnghuì bànshì.
examples.english: We're driving to the provincial capital to take care of some business.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers specifically to the capital city of a Chinese province (e.g., 广州是广东的省会).

vocabulary.mnemonic: You want to '省' (save) some '钱' (money). Putting coins into a piggy bank.
vocabulary.etymology: 省 (shěng) here means 'to save' or 'economize'. 钱 (qián) means 'money'.

examples.chinese: 自己做饭比点外卖省钱。
examples.pinyin: Zìjǐ zuòfàn bǐ diǎn wàimài shěngqián.
examples.english: Cooking for yourself saves money compared to ordering delivery.

examples.chinese: 这个月得省点儿钱了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège yuè děi shěng diǎnr qián le.
examples.english: I need to save a bit of money this month.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very common verb-object phrase. Can be separated: 省不了多少钱 (can't save much money).

vocabulary.mnemonic: You '看' (look) at something and '作' (make/treat) it as something else.
vocabulary.etymology: 看 (kàn) means 'to look at' or 'see'. 作 (zuò) means 'to make', 'regard as', or 'take for'.

examples.chinese: 我一直把他看作最好的朋友。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yìzhí bǎ tā kànzuò zuì hǎo de péngyou.
examples.english: I have always regarded him as my best friend.

examples.chinese: 别把客气看作虚伪。
examples.pinyin: Bié bǎ kèqi kànzuò xūwěi.
examples.english: Don't mistake politeness for hypocrisy.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in the structure '把 A 看作 B' (regard A as B). Formal synonym for '当成'.

vocabulary.english: be optimistic about; think highly of
vocabulary.mnemonic: You '看' (look) at something and think it's '好' (good). Giving a thumbs-up to its future.
vocabulary.etymology: 看 (kàn) means 'to look at' or 'view'. 好 (hǎo) means 'good'.

examples.chinese: 大家都很看好这支球队。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu hěn kānhǎo zhè zhī qiúduì.
examples.english: Everyone is very optimistic about this team.

examples.chinese: 专家看好明年的经济形势。
examples.pinyin: Zhuānjiā kānhǎo míngnián de jīngjì xíngshì.
examples.english: Experts are optimistic about next year's economic situation.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Specifically used for expressing positive expectations about someone's future or something's prospects.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The result of '看' (looking) is '得见' (able to be seen). The opposite of invisible.
vocabulary.etymology: 看 (kàn) means 'to look'. 得 (de) is a potential complement marker. 见 (jiàn) means 'to see'.

examples.chinese: 从我家窗户看得见那座山。
examples.pinyin: Cóng wǒ jiā chuānghu kàndéjiàn nà zuò shān.
examples.english: You can see that mountain from my window.

examples.chinese: 他的进步大家都看得见。
examples.pinyin: Tā de jìnbù dàjiā dōu kàndéjiàn.
examples.english: Everyone can see his progress.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A potential complement structure (V+得+见). Its negative form is '看不见' (cannot see).

vocabulary.mnemonic: When you '看' (look) at someone and feel they are '得起' (worthy enough to be lifted up). Giving them respect.
vocabulary.etymology: 看 (kàn) means 'to look at' or 'view'. 得 (de) is a potential complement marker. 起 (qǐ) means 'to rise' or 'raise up'.

examples.chinese: 老板很看得起他，把重要项目交给他。
examples.pinyin: Lǎobǎn hěn kàndeqǐ tā, bǎ zhòngyào xiàngmù jiāo gěi tā.
examples.english: The boss thinks highly of him and gave him the important project.

examples.chinese: 谢谢你这么看得起我。
examples.pinyin: Xièxie nǐ zhème kàndeqǐ wǒ.
examples.english: Thank you for having such a high opinion of me.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A colloquial phrase about social esteem. The opposite is '看不起' (look down on).

vocabulary.mnemonic: You '看' (watch) and '管' (manage/control) something. Like a security guard on duty.
vocabulary.etymology: 看 (kàn) means 'to look after' or 'watch'. 管 (guǎn) means 'to manage', 'control', or 'be in charge of'.

examples.chinese: 请帮我看管一下行李。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ kānguǎn yíxià xíngli.
examples.english: Please help me look after the luggage for a moment.

examples.chinese: 这个仓库需要专人看管。
examples.pinyin: Zhège cāngkù xūyào zhuān rén kānguǎn.
examples.english: This warehouse needs a dedicated person to guard it.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Implies a temporary or specific duty of watching over things, children, or premises to keep them safe.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The '目' (eye) radical gives it away. The action your eye does in a split second.
vocabulary.etymology: Contains '目' (mù, eye) as the semantic component. The character depicts the quick action of the eyelid.

examples.chinese: 她对我眨了一下眼睛。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì wǒ zhǎ le yíxià yǎnjīng.
examples.english: She blinked/winked at me.

examples.chinese: 别一直眨眼，是不是进东西了？
examples.pinyin: Bié yìzhí zhǎ yǎn, shì bù shì jìn dōngxi le?
examples.english: Stop blinking constantly, did something get in your eye?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Almost always used with '眼睛' (eye) as the object: '眨眼'. Can imply a wink if done intentionally.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Your '目' (eye) is being affected by '米' (rice) – imagine squinting at tiny grains of rice.
vocabulary.etymology: Contains '目' (mù, eye) as the semantic component. 米 (mǐ, rice) likely serves as a phonetic component.

examples.chinese: 阳光太强了，我只能眯着眼睛看。
examples.pinyin: Yángguāng tài qiáng le, wǒ zhǐ néng mī zhe yǎnjīng kàn.
examples.english: The sunlight is too strong, I can only look while squinting.

examples.chinese: 他眯起眼睛，露出神秘的笑容。
examples.pinyin: Tā mī qǐ yǎnjīng, lòuchū shénmì de xiàoróng.
examples.english: He narrowed his eyes and revealed a mysterious smile.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Describes the action of partially closing one's eyes, often due to bright light, smile, or to see more clearly.

vocabulary.english: soon; be about to; watch helplessly
vocabulary.mnemonic: With your own '眼' (eyes) you '看' (see) something about to happen, often something you can't stop.
vocabulary.etymology: 眼 (yǎn) means 'eye'. 看 (kàn) means 'to look' or 'see'.

examples.chinese: 眼看就要下雨了，我们快回家吧。
examples.pinyin: Yǎnkàn jiù yào xià yǔ le, wǒmen kuài huí jiā ba.
examples.english: It's about to rain soon, let's go home quickly.

examples.chinese: 我眼看着他摔倒，却来不及帮忙。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǎnkàn zhe tā shuāidǎo, què láibují bāngmáng.
examples.english: I watched helplessly as he fell, but couldn't help in time.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As an adverb: '眼看就要...' (something is about to happen). As a verb: '眼看着...' (to watch something happen helplessly).

vocabulary.mnemonic: His name is '知' (known) by the many '口' (mouths) that speak it. A star.
vocabulary.etymology: 知 (zhī) means 'to know'. 名 (míng) means 'name' or 'fame'.

examples.chinese: 他是一位知名的作家。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yí wèi zhīmíng de zuòjiā.
examples.english: He is a well-known writer.

examples.chinese: 这家餐厅在当地很知名。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng zài dāngdì hěn zhīmíng.
examples.english: This restaurant is very well-known locally.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used as an attributive adjective before nouns: 知名人士 (well-known personage), 知名品牌 (well-known brand).

vocabulary.mnemonic: If you '知足' (know what's enough), you will '常乐' (often be happy). The secret to a smile.
vocabulary.etymology: 知 (zhī) 'to know'. 足 (zú) 'enough'. 常 (cháng) 'often'. 乐 (lè) 'happy'. Literally 'Knowing contentment brings constant joy.'

examples.chinese: 老人总是说，知足常乐。
examples.pinyin: Lǎorén zǒng shì shuō, zhīzúchánglè.
examples.english: The old man always says, contentment brings happiness.

examples.chinese: 生活简单一点，知足常乐嘛。
examples.pinyin: Shēnghuó jiǎndān yìdiǎn, zhīzúchánglè ma.
examples.english: Live a simpler life, contentment brings happiness, you know.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A common proverb expressing a traditional philosophy of life. Used as a complete saying or advice.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Time that is '短' (short) and feels '促' (hurried/pressed). Like a quick breath.
vocabulary.etymology: 短 (duǎn) means 'short'. 促 (cù) means 'hurried', 'urgent', or 'to press'.

examples.chinese: 他的发言非常短促。
examples.pinyin: Tā de fāyán fēicháng duǎncù.
examples.english: His speech was very brief.

examples.chinese: 我听见一声短促的尖叫。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ tīngjiàn yì shēng duǎncù de jiānjiào.
examples.english: I heard a short, sharp scream.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Emphasizes not just short duration, but also a sense of abruptness or being cut short.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A '片' (film) that is '短' (short). Like those videos on your phone.
vocabulary.etymology: 短 (duǎn) means 'short'. 片 (piàn) means 'a slice', 'film', or 'video'.

examples.chinese: 他拍了一个三分钟的创意短片。
examples.pinyin: Tā pāi le yí gè sān fēnzhōng de chuàngyì duǎnpiàn.
examples.english: He made a three-minute creative short film.

examples.chinese: 我喜欢在网上看搞笑短片。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan zài wǎngshàng kàn gǎoxiào duǎnpiàn.
examples.english: I like watching funny short videos online.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The common term for any short video or film, from artistic films to social media clips.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The '石' (stone/rock) that is '广' (vast/extensive) underground. Where miners work.
vocabulary.etymology: Simplified form of 礦 (kuàng). Contains '石' (shí, stone) as the semantic component. The original traditional character 礦 also contains '石'.

examples.chinese: 这个小镇以前有一座大煤矿。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiǎo zhèn yǐqián yǒu yí zuò dà méikuàng.
examples.english: This small town used to have a big coal mine.

examples.chinese: 这种矿石很有价值。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng kuàngshí hěn yǒu jiàzhí.
examples.english: This kind of ore is very valuable.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in compound words: 煤矿 (coal mine), 金矿 (gold mine), 矿泉水 (mineral water). Can refer to the mine itself or the ore.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine someone's good name being '败' (defeated) and '坏' (broken).
vocabulary.etymology: 败 - originally 'to destroy', 坏 - originally 'earthen wall collapse'

examples.chinese: 他这么做是在败坏公司的名誉。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhème zuò shì zài bài huài gōngsī de míngyù.
examples.english: What he's doing is ruining the company's reputation.

examples.chinese: 他简直道德败坏。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiǎnzhí dàodé bài huài.
examples.english: He has utterly corrupt morals.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for abstract concepts like reputation, morale, morals, or customs.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 贝 (shell/money) radical on the side of 长 (long) reminds you of a long bill.
vocabulary.etymology: From 貝 (shell currency) + 長 (originally tally stick for recording debts).

examples.chinese: 服务员，买单！把账算一下。
examples.pinyin: Fúwùyuán, mǎi dān! Bǎ zhàng suàn yīxià.
examples.english: Waiter, the bill! Please settle the account.

examples.chinese: 我们俩的账以后再算。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen liǎ de zhàng yǐhòu zài suàn.
examples.english: We'll settle our score later.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often interchangeable with 帐, but 账 is preferred for financial matters. It's the basis for many finance-related compounds.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Your money 账 is in a household/place 户.
vocabulary.etymology: 账 (account) + 户 (door/household; here meaning an entry or entity).

examples.chinese: 你绑定的是哪个银行账户？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bǎngdìng de shì nǎge yínháng zhànghù?
examples.english: Which bank account did you link?

examples.chinese: 我的社交媒体账户被黑了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shèjiào méitǐ zhànghù bèi hēi le.
examples.english: My social media account was hacked.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A general term for any kind of account, financial or online.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'famine' 乏 (lack) within 'poverty' 贫.
vocabulary.etymology: 贫 (poor) + 乏 (to lack). Literally 'poor and lacking'.

examples.chinese: 这篇文章的内容太贫乏了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè piān wénzhāng de nèiróng tài pínfá le.
examples.english: The content of this article is too impoverished.

examples.chinese: 他觉得自己的词汇很贫乏。
examples.pinyin: Tā juéde zìjǐ de cíhuì hěn pínfá.
examples.english: He feels his vocabulary is very lacking.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for abstract things like content, experience, or imagination, not just material poverty.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Stuck in 'poverty' 贫 and 'difficulty' 困.
vocabulary.etymology: 贫 (poor) + 困 (to be stranded/in difficulty). Literally 'poor and trapped'.

examples.chinese: 他小时候家里很贫困。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎoshíhou jiā li hěn pínkùn.
examples.english: His family was very poor when he was a child.

examples.chinese: 政府正在努力消除贫困。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ zhèngzài nǔlì xiāochú pínkùn.
examples.english: The government is working hard to eliminate poverty.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Describes a serious state of material deprivation.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The meaning 义 that is '贬' (lowered/demeaned).
vocabulary.etymology: 贬 (to demote, belittle) + 义 (meaning). Literally 'demeaning meaning'.

examples.chinese: “狡猾”这个词带有贬义。
examples.pinyin: "Jiǎohuá" zhège cí dài yǒu biǎnyì.
examples.english: The word 'cunning' has a derogatory meaning.

examples.chinese: 别用有贬义的词来形容他。
examples.pinyin: Bié yòng yǒu biǎnyì de cí lái xíngróng tā.
examples.english: Don't use derogatory words to describe him.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Always used with 带, 有, 是, etc. to describe a word's connotation.

vocabulary.mnemonic: To '贬' (demean) and make someone/something '低' (low).
vocabulary.etymology: 贬 (to demote, belittle) + 低 (low). Literally 'to belittle and lower'.

examples.chinese: 他总是贬低别人的成就。
examples.pinyin: Tā zǒng shì biǎndī biérén de chéngjiù.
examples.english: He always belittles other people's achievements.

examples.chinese: 别为了抬高自己而贬低朋友。
examples.pinyin: Bié wèile táigāo zìjǐ ér biǎndī péngyou.
examples.english: Don't put down your friends to make yourself look better.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Takes a direct object (the person or thing being disparaged). It's a conscious, often verbal action.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A person 者 risking their money 贝 on a bet.
vocabulary.etymology: From 貝 (shell/money) + 者 (person). Original meaning related to gambling or competing for money.

examples.chinese: 我赌十块钱他今天会迟到。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ dǔ shí kuài qián tā jīntiān huì chídào.
examples.english: I bet ten bucks he'll be late today.

examples.chinese: 他因为赌钱输了很多。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi dǔ qián shūle hěnduō.
examples.english: He lost a lot because he gambled.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be used literally (gambling) or figuratively (betting on an outcome).

vocabulary.mnemonic: The act of 赌 (betting) combined with the broad concept of 博 (games/vast).
vocabulary.etymology: 赌 (to gamble) + 博 (extensive, to gamble). A double emphasis on the act of gambling.

examples.chinese: 在中国，赌博是违法的。
examples.pinyin: Zài Zhōngguó, dǔbó shì wéifǎ de.
examples.english: In China, gambling is illegal.

examples.chinese: 他因为赌博家破人亡。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi dǔbó jiā pò rén wáng.
examples.english: He lost his family and life because of gambling.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Has a stronger, more formal, and negative connotation than just 赌.

vocabulary.english: to rely on; to blame; to be shameless
vocabulary.mnemonic: A 'lazy' person leaning on a bundle 束.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted a person (貝/束) being lazy or leaning on something. Evolved to meanings of reliance and bad behavior.

examples.chinese: 这孩子就赖着妈妈不走。
examples.pinyin: Zhè háizi jiù lài zhe māmā bù zǒu.
examples.english: This kid is clinging to his mom and won't leave.

examples.chinese: 自己做错事，别赖别人。
examples.pinyin: Zìjǐ zuò cuò shì, bié lài biérén.
examples.english: You made the mistake yourself, don't blame others.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very versatile and colloquial word. Can be negative (shameless, blame) or neutral (rely on).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Your wealth 贝 is 'turned' or 'transformed' 兼 (兼 historically had meanings related to change).
vocabulary.etymology: From 貝 (shell/money) + 兼 (to unite; historical phonetic component). Literally related to the acquisition of money.

examples.chinese: 你一个月能赚多少钱？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yí gè yuè néng zhuàn duōshǎo qián?
examples.english: How much money can you earn a month?

examples.chinese: 他做这个生意赚了一大笔。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuò zhège shēngyì zhuànle yí dà bǐ.
examples.english: He made a huge profit from this business.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Implies earning or profiting, not just getting paid (发工资). Opposite is 赔 or 亏.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It's simply the act of '赚' (earning/profiting) + '钱' (money).
vocabulary.etymology: 赚 (to earn/profit) + 钱 (money). A verb-object compound.

examples.chinese: 现在做什么工作最赚钱？
examples.pinyin: Xiànzài zuò shénme gōngzuò zuì zhuàn qián?
examples.english: What kind of job makes the most money now?

examples.chinese: 他开网店赚了不少钱。
examples.pinyin: Tā kāi wǎngdiàn zhuàn le bù shǎo qián.
examples.english: He made a lot of money running an online shop.

vocabulary.usage_notes: An extremely common and practical phrase. The object is already included, so you don't say '赚钱钱'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: They put out their 'treasures' 贝 under a 'roof' 宀 to compete.
vocabulary.etymology: From ancient rituals involving offerings. Evolved to mean 'to compare' or 'compete'.

examples.chinese: 下午我们赛一场乒乓球吧。
examples.pinyin: Xiàwǔ wǒmen sài yì chǎng pīngpāng qiú ba.
examples.english: Let's have a table tennis match this afternoon.

examples.chinese: 看谁跑得快，敢不敢跟我赛一下？
examples.pinyin: Kàn shuí pǎo de kuài, gǎn bù gǎn gēn wǒ sài yíxià?
examples.english: See who runs faster, dare to race me?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in compounds or casually for 'to have a match/contest'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The place/field 场 for the competition 赛.
vocabulary.etymology: 赛 (competition) + 场 (field, venue).

examples.chinese: 赛场上的气氛非常热烈。
examples.pinyin: Sàichǎng shàng de qìfēn fēicháng rèliè.
examples.english: The atmosphere in the stadium is very intense.

examples.chinese: 他一走进赛场就紧张。
