examples.english: That cargo spaceship successfully docked with the International Space Station.

vocabulary.usage_notes: In modern context, almost exclusively means 'spaceship'. For old-fashioned 'airship', context is needed.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 飞行 (to fly) + 员 (person) = the person who flies.
vocabulary.etymology: 飞行 (to fly, flight) + 员 (member, person). A modern compound for a flight crew member.

examples.chinese: 我哥哥的梦想是当一名飞行员。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gēge de mèngxiǎng shì dāng yī míng fēixíngyuán.
examples.english: My older brother's dream is to become a pilot.

examples.chinese: 这位飞行员有二十年的飞行经验。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi fēixíngyuán yǒu èrshí nián de fēixíng jīngyàn.
examples.english: This pilot has twenty years of flying experience.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The standard term for both civilian and military pilots.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 食 (food) + 欲 (desire) = desire for food.
vocabulary.etymology: 食 (to eat, food) + 欲 (desire, wish).

examples.chinese: 我感冒了，一点食欲都没有。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gǎnmào le, yīdiǎn shíyù dōu méiyǒu.
examples.english: I have a cold and have no appetite at all.

examples.chinese: 运动完以后，我的食欲特别好。
examples.pinyin: Yùndòng wán yǐhòu, wǒ de shíyù tèbié hǎo.
examples.english: After exercising, my appetite is especially good.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used in phrases like '食欲不振' (loss of appetite), '增进食欲' (to stimulate appetite).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of 'can' (as in 'can of food') but it's a full meal. Also found in 餐厅 (restaurant).
vocabulary.etymology: Originally meant 'to eat'. The character is complex, but the simplified form 餐 retains the 食 (food) radical at the bottom.

examples.chinese: 我们一天吃三餐：早餐、午餐和晚餐。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yī tiān chī sān cān: zǎocān, wǔcān hé wǎncān.
examples.english: We eat three meals a day: breakfast, lunch, and dinner.

examples.chinese: 这餐饭你花了多少钱？
examples.pinyin: Zhè cān fàn nǐ huā le duōshǎo qián?
examples.english: How much did you spend on this meal?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in compound words (早餐, 午餐, 晚餐, 餐厅). In casual speech, 饭 is more common for 'meal'.

vocabulary.english: to have experienced the vicissitudes of life
vocabulary.mnemonic: 饱 (full of) + 经 (to experience) + 沧桑 (blue sea changed to mulberry fields) = 'full of' having seen seas turn to fields = lived through many changes.
vocabulary.etymology: 饱 (full) + 经 (to pass through) + 沧桑 (short for 沧海桑田, 'the blue sea turns into mulberry fields', i.e., great worldly changes).

examples.chinese: 爷爷的脸上刻着皱纹，一看就是饱经沧桑的人。
examples.pinyin: Yéye de liǎn shàng kèzhe zhòuwén, yī kàn jiù shì bǎojīngcāngsāng de rén.
examples.english: Grandpa's face is etched with wrinkles; you can tell he's a man who has been through a lot in life.

examples.chinese: 这座饱经沧桑的古桥，见证了数百年的历史。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò bǎojīngcāngsāng de gǔ qiáo, jiànzhèngle shù bǎi nián de lìshǐ.
examples.english: This ancient bridge, having witnessed countless changes, has stood witness to hundreds of years of history.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A literary idiom used to describe someone or something that has endured many hardships and changes over a long time.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Sounds like 'man tou' – a man's (蛮) head? It's a round, steamed head of dough!
vocabulary.etymology: The character 馒 is specific to this food. 头 (head) might refer to its round shape. One folk etymology links it to 蛮头 (barbarian head), but this is uncertain.

examples.chinese: 北方人早上爱吃馒头就咸菜。
examples.pinyin: Běifāng rén zǎoshang ài chī mántou jiù xiáncài.
examples.english: Northerners like to eat steamed buns with pickles for breakfast.

examples.chinese: 给我两个馒头，再打一份菜。
examples.pinyin: Gěi wǒ liǎng gè mántou, zài dǎ yī fèn cài.
examples.english: Give me two steamed buns and a serving of vegetables.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A staple Northern Chinese food. Often plain, unlike 包子 (baozi) which has filling.

vocabulary.english: chief, head, principal (e.g., CEO, first chair)
vocabulary.mnemonic: 首 (first, head) + 席 (seat) = the seat of the head, the top seat.
vocabulary.etymology: 首 (head, first) + 席 (mat, seat). Refers to the seat of honor or the highest position.

examples.chinese: 他刚被任命为公司的首席技术官。
examples.pinyin: Tā gāng bèi rènmìng wéi gōngsī de shǒuxí jìshù guān.
examples.english: He was just appointed as the company's Chief Technology Officer.

examples.chinese: 她在乐团里担任首席小提琴手。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yuètuán lǐ dānrèn shǒuxí xiǎotíqín shǒu.
examples.english: She is the concertmaster (first violin) in the orchestra.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used as a title prefix (首席XX官) or to denote the top position in a group (e.g., 首席代表).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 首 (first) + 次 (time) = the first time.
vocabulary.etymology: 首 (first) + 次 (time, occasion).

examples.chinese: 这是我首次来中国，感觉很兴奋。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ shǒucì lái Zhōngguó, gǎnjué hěn xīngfèn.
examples.english: This is my first time coming to China; I feel very excited.

examples.chinese: 电影的首次公演取得了巨大成功。
examples.pinyin: Diànyǐng de shǒucì gōngyǎn qǔdéle jùdà chénggōng.
examples.english: The movie's premiere was a huge success.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Slightly more formal than 第一次, often used in news or reports.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 首 (head) + 相 (minister) = the head minister.
vocabulary.etymology: 首 (head, chief) + 相 (minister, chancellor). Historically used in some Asian countries, now a common translation for 'Prime Minister'.

examples.chinese: 英国首相发表了关于经济的演讲。
examples.pinyin: Yīngguó shǒuxiàng fābiǎole guānyú jīngjì de yǎnjiǎng.
examples.english: The British Prime Minister gave a speech on the economy.

examples.chinese: 新首相明天将正式上任。
examples.pinyin: Xīn shǒuxiàng míngtiān jiāng zhèngshì shàngrèn.
examples.english: The new Prime Minister will officially take office tomorrow.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Specifically refers to the head of government in parliamentary systems (e.g., UK, Japan). 总理 is used for China, Germany, etc.

vocabulary.english: head, leader (of an organization or country)
vocabulary.mnemonic: 首 (head) + 脑 (brain) = the head and brain, the leader.
vocabulary.etymology: 首 (head) + 脑 (brain). Emphasizes the 'thinking/commanding' part of the head.

examples.chinese: 各国首脑将在下个月举行峰会。
examples.pinyin: Gè guó shǒunǎo jiāng zài xià gè yuè jǔxíng fēnghuì.
examples.english: The heads of state will hold a summit next month.

examples.chinese: 他是这个犯罪集团的首脑人物。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì zhège fànzuì jítuán de shǒunǎo rénwù.
examples.english: He is the leader of this criminal organization.

vocabulary.usage_notes: More formal and often used for political or organizational leaders in official contexts. Can have a slightly negative connotation in some contexts (e.g., 犯罪首脑).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 马 (horse) + 车 (vehicle) = a horse vehicle.
vocabulary.etymology: 马 (horse) + 车 (cart, vehicle). A straightforward compound.

examples.chinese: 公园里提供马车游览服务。
examples.pinyin: Gōngyuán lǐ tígōng mǎchē yóulǎn fúwù.
examples.english: The park offers carriage tour services.

examples.chinese: 在汽车发明以前，马车是重要的交通工具。
examples.pinyin: Zài qìchē fāmíng yǐqián, mǎchē shì zhòngyào de jiāotōng gōngjù.
examples.english: Before the invention of the car, carriages were an important means of transportation.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Now mainly seen in tourist spots or historical contexts.

vocabulary.english: to be stationed, to be located (for troops, diplomats, offices)
vocabulary.mnemonic: 马 (horse) + 主 (master) – a master with horses is 'stationed' somewhere (like an army).
vocabulary.etymology: From 馬 (horse) and 主 (master). Originally meant a halt for horses, later extended to mean to station troops.

examples.chinese: 美国驻华大使馆在北京。
examples.pinyin: Měiguó zhù Huá dàshǐ guǎn zài Běijīng.
examples.english: The U.S. Embassy in China is in Beijing.

examples.chinese: 我们公司在这里驻了一个办事处。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen gōngsī zài zhèlǐ zhùle yī gè bànshì chù.
examples.english: Our company has set up a representative office here.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for organizations or personnel stationed in a place, often officially (embassies, troops, offices).

vocabulary.english: (of troops) to be stationed, to be quartered
vocabulary.mnemonic: 驻 (be stationed) + 扎 (to pitch, pierce) = to pitch a camp and be stationed there.
vocabulary.etymology: 驻 (to halt, station) + 扎 (to prick, pitch a tent). Emphasizes the action of setting up camp.

examples.chinese: 军队在城外驻扎了下来。
examples.pinyin: Jūnduì zài chéng wài zhùzhāle xiàlái.
examples.english: The troops were stationed outside the city.

examples.chinese: 救援队已经驻扎在灾区了。
examples.pinyin: Jiùyuán duì yǐjīng zhùzhā zài zāiqū le.
examples.english: The rescue team has already set up camp in the disaster area.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Almost exclusively used for military or organized groups setting up a temporary base. More specific than 驻.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 高 (high) + 层 (layer, floor) = high layers/floors.
vocabulary.etymology: 高 (high) + 层 (layer, storey).

examples.chinese: 我住在那个高层公寓的二十楼。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhù zài nàgè gāocéng gōngyù de èrshí lóu.
examples.english: I live on the 20th floor of that high-rise apartment.

examples.chinese: 公司高层明天要开一个紧急会议。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī gāocéng míngtiān yào kāi yī gè jǐnjí huìyì.
examples.english: The company's senior management will have an emergency meeting tomorrow.

vocabulary.usage_notes: When referring to people (高层), it's a collective noun meaning 'top management/leadership'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 高 (high) + 峰 (mountain peak) = a high peak.
vocabulary.etymology: 高 (high) + 峰 (mountain peak).

examples.chinese: 我们终于爬上了这座山的最高峰。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōngyú pá shàngle zhè zuò shān de zuì gāo fēng.
examples.english: We finally climbed to the highest peak of this mountain.

examples.chinese: 早上七点到九点是地铁的高峰期。
examples.pinyin: Zǎoshang qī diǎn dào jiǔ diǎn shì dìtiě de gāofēngqī.
examples.english: 7 to 9 AM is the subway's rush hour.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used both literally (mountain peak) and figuratively (peak period, peak performance).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 高 (high) + 手 (hand) = someone with high hand-skills, a master.
vocabulary.etymology: 高 (high) + 手 (hand, person skilled in an art).

examples.chinese: 他玩游戏是个高手，没人能赢他。
examples.pinyin: Tā wán yóuxì shì gè gāoshǒu, méi rén néng yíng tā.
examples.english: He's a master at playing games; nobody can beat him.

examples.chinese: 我想找个电脑高手帮我修一下电脑。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng zhǎo gè diànnǎo gāoshǒu bāng wǒ xiū yīxià diànnǎo.
examples.english: I want to find a computer expert to help me fix my computer.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very common and casual term for someone highly skilled in any field (sports, games, tech, etc.).
